body: A ski can only deliver what the boot gives it. Boots are roughly 80 percent of the equipment problem: one that lets the heel lift or the foot slide sideways cannot produce edge angle, however well the skier moves. Buy boots first, and buy from a fitter who will pull the liner out.

Shell fit is measured with the liner removed. Put the bare foot in the empty shell, slide the toes forward until they touch the front, and measure the gap behind the heel. One finger, roughly 10-20 mm (0.4-0.8 in), is a performance fit. Two fingers, about 25 mm (1 in), means the shell is a full size too big.

Put the liner back, drive the heel rearward, and buckle. The heel must stay down when you rise onto your toes; more than a few millimetres of lift means a shell too roomy through the instep, and buckle tension will not fix it.
A correct shell feels tight in the shop and loosens as the liner packs out over 5-10 days. A boot comfortable on the first try-on is the one you regret at st-06.
hard_rules: Never buy a boot without a liner-out shell check. A boot sold on comfort alone is sold a size too big.
Measure both feet. They are rarely the same length or width.
sections.heading: Boots are 80 percent of the equipment problem

tables.caption: Shell-fit gap, liner removed, toes touching the front of the shell.
rows: st-10 and beyond, high tolerance for pressure
First season, st-01 to st-05 only

adaptation_notes.note: Mass loads a boot the way speed does. Take the next flex step up rather than the next size, and expect a stock liner to pack out faster.
Where ankle dorsiflexion is reduced, a softer flex plus a fitted footbed skis better than a shell the ankle cannot move inside.

body: Flex numbers are not standardized between brands. A 100 from one maker can feel stiffer than a 110 from another, and the same model in a shorter shell flexes differently again. Treat it as a ranking within one brand, flex the boot in the shop, and remember that cold snow stiffens it.

Choose flex from body mass, terrain and stage, not from ambition. A boot too stiff to bend at all locks the ankle, drives the hips back, and manufactures the fore/aft problems that st-06 and st-10 spend their time undoing. A boot too soft collapses at the ankle and gives no edge at speed.

Last width across the forefoot matters more than length: roughly 95-97 mm narrow, 98-100 mm medium, 101-104 mm wide in a size 26.5. Volume - instep height and cuff circumference - decides whether the boot closes at all. A wide forefoot in a narrow last can be punched out; a low-volume foot swimming in a big shell cannot.
sections.heading: Flex, last width and volume

tables.caption: Indicative adult flex ranges. Brand-relative only; junior boots use a separate 30-70 scale.

body: Stock footbeds are flat foam packing material. A supportive trim-to-fit or custom footbed stops the arch collapsing, which stops the knee rolling inward, which stops the ski flattening under load. It is the cheapest change with a visible effect on edge grip.

An A-frame - knees closer together than the feet, inside ski over-edged - that survives cueing and drills across several days is an alignment problem, not a technique problem. Cuff alignment, the adjustable rivet on most boots, matches the cuff angle to the lower leg. Canting, planing the boot sole or shimming the binding, changes where the ski sits under the knee.

Order matters: footbed, then cuff alignment, then canting - and canting only once the skier can hold a clean sideslip on both edges (st-04). Canting a developing stance bakes a temporary fault into the hardware.
hard_rules: Canting is a fitter's job with the skier on a measuring stand. Do not shim a binding at home.
sections.heading: Footbeds, cuff alignment and canting

adaptation_notes.note: Add 3-5 cm over the table and favour a stiffer ski. A ski bent past its designed camber washes out at the tail regardless of technique.
Re-measure every season. A ski at chin height in December is often shoulder height by the next winter.

body: Length comes from height and mass together. Chin-to-nose is a starting point for a first pair, not a rule for life. From st-06 onward, add length for mass, speed and soft snow; subtract it for short-radius work and bumps. Two skiers of equal height 25 kg (55 lb) apart do not belong on the same ski.

Waist width decides what the ski is for. A narrow waist comes to edge quickly and holds on hard snow; a wide waist floats and damps but is slow edge-to-edge and unpleasant on ice. Sidecut radius sets the turn the ski wants: a 13 m ski turns whether you ask or not, a 20 m ski has to be asked.
One ski cannot be optimal everywhere. Buy for the snow you ski most weekends rather than the trip you take once a year, and demo before committing.
sections.heading: Skis: length, width and radius

tables.caption: Starting points for ski selection, length measured against standing height.

body: Release values, still spoken of as DIN, are calculated from mass, height, boot sole length, age and skier type, then set and function-tested on a calibrated jig by a technician. Do not set them yourself, and do not raise them after a pre-release: a pre-release is usually a worn boot sole, ice under the toe piece, or a value that was wrong to begin with.

Have the values checked and the binding function-tested at the start of every season, after any hard impact, after a change of boot, and after any change of more than about 5 kg (11 lb) in body mass. Growing juniors get a recheck every season regardless.

Boot sole standards are not interchangeable. ISO 5355 alpine, GripWalk and ISO 9523 touring soles differ in geometry, height and rubber, and a binding must be certified for the sole it holds. A mismatch can prevent release altogether or cause release at random. The marking is on the boot heel; the compatibility list is on the binding.
hard_rules: Never ski a boot and binding whose sole standards do not match.
Never adjust a release value yourself, and never let a shop skip the function test.
Brakes or leashes on both skis, every day - point 5 of the Code, see mod-safety.
sections.heading: Bindings, release values and sole standards

tables.caption: Boot sole standards and the bindings that accept them.
rows: Alpine bindings; adjustable bindings set to alpine

adaptation_notes.note: Fit the helmet to this head, this season. A size up, padded out, leaves the shell free to rotate on impact.

body: A helmet must carry ASTM F2040 or EN 1077 certification. Fit test: with the straps undone it should not shift when you shake your head, and the goggle should meet the brow with no gap of forehead showing. Replace it after any impact it absorbed, even with no visible damage, and otherwise on the maker's schedule, typically 3-5 years.

Goggles are matched to light by lens VLT - the percentage of visible light the lens transmits. A storm lens is blinding in spring sun and a sun lens is useless in cloud. Carry two lenses, or one all-round 20-40 percent tint. Flat light wants rose, amber or high-contrast yellow, which lifts terrain definition rather than brightness.

Poles are sized by inverting one: grip the shaft below the basket, stand the grip on the floor, and the forearm should be horizontal, elbow near 90 degrees. In boots that measures about 5 cm shorter than in shoes. Poles become useful at st-07.

Layers: a wicking base, an insulating mid, a windproof and waterproof shell - and one thin sock per foot. Never two, and never a thick sock in a shell-fitted boot. Two socks slide against each other, eat the volume the foot needs, and make feet colder.
hard_rules: A bike or skate helmet is not a ski helmet - uncertified for this impact profile and for cold.
Never ski a helmet of unknown history. One absorbed impact you did not see makes it decorative.
sections.heading: Helmet, goggles, poles and layers

adaptation_notes.note: Rent rather than buy at this size. Feet change faster than a season, and this band needs correct fit more than ownership.
Rent the package for two or three days, then buy boots. Skiing teaches you more than a shop conversation.

body: Buy boots first, rent skis. Boots are personal and fit-critical; skis are interchangeable, and a demo fleet lets you test length and width first. Buy boots past roughly 6-8 days a season; buy skis once you are past st-06 and know what terrain you actually ski.

Tuning: the recreational carving spec is 0.5-1 degree of base bevel and 1-2 degrees of side bevel, with tip and tail detuned by a few passes of a gummi stone so the ski enters and leaves a turn without hooking. 2-3 degrees of side bevel is a race setting - it grips hard and punishes every late edge change. Wax every 4-6 days.

Kids' gear: an oversized boot makes skiing physically impossible, not merely harder. A child cannot flex a shell they do not fill, cannot feel the ski, and stands back and wedges defensively. That reads as a technique problem and is not one. Fit for this season, even if it means renting every year.

Fleet junior skis are frequently blunt and unwaxed - a season of rock has rounded the edges. A child who cannot hold an edge on a green run is often on skis that cannot hold one. Run a thumb along the edge underfoot at pickup and ask for a sharpen.
checklist: Shell check done with the liner out, one finger behind the heel.
Release values set and function-tested by a technician this season.
Boot sole standard matches the binding's certification marking.
Helmet certified, undamaged, no gap at the goggle brow.
Edges sharp underfoot, tip and tail detuned, bases waxed.
One thin sock per foot, plus a spare dry pair.
hard_rules: Never buy a child a boot one or two sizes large to last two seasons. It removes their ability to ski, not just their comfort.
sections.heading: Rent or buy, tuning, and kids' gear

body: 雪板能交付的，不会超过雪靴传给它的。装备上的麻烦大约八成在雪靴：一双让后跟能抬、前脚掌能侧向滑动的靴子，无论动作多干净，都做不出刃角。先买靴，而且要找愿意把内胆抽出来量壳的靴技师。
壳测要在取出内胆的空壳上做。光脚放进空壳，脚趾向前顶到壳前端，量后跟与壳之间的间隙。一根手指、大约 10-20 mm (0.4-0.8 in)，是性能配；两根手指、约 25 mm (1 in)，说明这只壳整整大了一号。
把内胆装回去，后跟向后顶实，再扣扣。提起脚尖站立时后跟必须留在原位；抬起超过几毫米，说明壳在足背一带太空，扣得再紧也补不回来。
合适的壳在店里试穿时是紧的，滑 5-10 天内胆压实后才会松开。第一次试穿就舒服的靴子，正是你到 st-06 时会后悔的那双。
hard_rules: 没有做过取出内胆的壳测，就不要买靴。凭试穿舒适卖出去的靴子，都大了一号。
两只脚都要量。长度和宽度极少一样。
sections.heading: 装备问题的八成出在雪靴

tables.caption: 壳测间隙：取出内胆，脚趾顶住壳前端时的读数。
rows: st-10 以后，且对压迫感耐受度高
st-06 往上的多数滑雪者
仅限第一个雪季，st-01 到 st-05
没有人适合——换小一号壳

adaptation_notes.note: 体重对靴子的加载方式和速度一样。要往上加一档硬度，而不是往上加一码；同时要预期原厂内胆压实得更快。
踝关节背屈幅度受限时，软一档的硬度加一副定制足弓垫，滑起来好过一只踝关节在里面动不了的壳。

body: 硬度数值在品牌之间不统一。一家的 100 可能比另一家的 110 还硬，同一型号换成短一号的壳，弯曲手感又不一样。把它当成同品牌内部的排序，在店里亲手压一压，并且记住低温会让靴子变硬。
按体重、地形和阶段选硬度，不要按志向选。压根压不动的靴子会锁死踝关节、把髋推到后面去，制造出 st-06 与 st-10 要花大量时间去拆的前后平衡问题。太软的靴子则在踝部塌掉，速度一上来就没有刃。
前脚掌处的鞋楦宽度比长度更要紧：以 26.5 码为例，约 95-97 mm 属窄楦，98-100 mm 中楦，101-104 mm 宽楦。容积——足背高度与上筒周长——决定这双靴子扣不扣得上。宽前掌配窄楦可以做扩壳；低容积的脚在大壳里晃荡，无解。
sections.heading: 硬度、鞋楦宽度与容积

tables.caption: 成人硬度参考区间。仅在品牌内部可比；青少年靴另用 30-70 的标尺。

body: 原厂鞋垫就是一层平的泡棉填充物。一副有支撑的热塑修剪垫或定制足弓垫能拦住足弓塌陷，足弓不塌膝就不往内倒，膝不内倒板就不会在受力时被压平。这是花钱最少、对刃的咬合看得见效果的一项改动。
A 形腿——双膝比双脚更靠近、内板刃立过头——如果连着几天给口令、做练习都改不掉，那是对线问题，不是技术问题。上筒对线（多数靴子上那颗可调铆钉）把上筒角度对到小腿上；楔片调整（打磨靴底或在固定器下加垫片）改变雪板在膝下的位置。
顺序很重要：先足弓垫，再上筒对线，最后才是楔片——而楔片只在滑雪者两侧刃都能稳住干净侧滑之后（st-04）才做。给还在变化的站姿上楔片，等于把一个临时的毛病烧进硬件里。
hard_rules: 楔片是靴技师的活，要让滑雪者站在测量台上做。不要在家里给固定器垫垫片。
sections.heading: 足弓垫、上筒对线与楔片

adaptation_notes.note: 在表上再加 3-5 cm，并偏向硬一点的板。被压过设计反弓的板，板尾一定会甩出去，跟技术无关。
每个雪季重新量一次。十二月还在下巴高度的板，第二个冬天往往已经到肩膀了。

body: 板长要由身高和体重一起决定。下巴到鼻尖只是第一副板的起点，不是一辈子的规矩。从 st-06 起，为体重、速度和松软雪加长，为小回转和雪包减短。身高相同但体重差 25 kg (55 lb) 的两个人，不该站在同一支板上。
腰宽决定这支板是干什么的。窄腰立刃快、硬雪上咬得住；宽腰有浮力、更稳，但换刃慢，在冰面上很难受。侧切半径决定板自己想走的弯：13 m 的板你不叫它也转，20 m 的板你必须叫它。
一支板不可能处处最优。按你多数周末实际滑的雪来买，而不是按一年去一次的那趟行程来买，下单前先试板。
sections.heading: 雪板：长度、腰宽与半径

tables.caption: 选板起点，板长以站立身高为基准。

body: 脱离值（口语里仍叫 DIN）由体重、身高、靴底长度、年龄和滑行类型算出，再由技师在校准过的测试台上设定并做功能测试。不要自己设，也不要在一次误脱离之后把值调高：误脱离通常是靴底磨损、前趾片下结冰，或者本来就设错了。
每个雪季开始时、任何一次重摔之后、换靴之后、体重变化超过约 5 kg (11 lb) 之后，都要重新核对脱离值并做功能测试。正在长个儿的青少年不论有没有变化，每季都要复检。
靴底标准之间不能互换。ISO 5355 高山底、GripWalk 与 ISO 9523 登山底在几何形状、高度和胶料上都不同，固定器必须对它所夹持的靴底取得认证。配错可能导致完全不脱离，也可能导致随机脱离。标记印在靴子后跟上，兼容清单印在固定器上。
hard_rules: 绝不要用靴底标准与固定器不匹配的组合上雪。
绝不要自己调脱离值，也绝不允许雪具店跳过功能测试。
每一天、每一支板都要有刹车片或防跑绳——守则第 5 条，见 mod-safety。
sections.heading: 固定器、脱离值与靴底标准

tables.caption: 靴底标准与可接受它们的固定器。
rows: 高山固定器；调到高山模式的可调固定器
仅限 GripWalk 认证或 MultiNorm 固定器
仅限登山或 MultiNorm 认证固定器

adaptation_notes.note: 按这个头、这个雪季来配盔。大一号再用垫片塞满，等于让壳在撞击时可以自己转。

body: 头盔必须带 ASTM F2040 或 EN 1077 认证。合头测试：不扣带子摇头，头盔不该移动；雪镜上缘要贴住眉骨，中间不露出一条额头。任何一次吸收过冲击之后就换掉，哪怕看不出损伤；否则按厂家年限更换，通常 3-5 年。
雪镜靠镜片 VLT——可见光透过率——来匹配光线。暴风雪镜片在春天的太阳下会晃得看不见，晴天镜片在阴云里等于没有。带两片镜片，或者用一片 20-40% 的全能色。平光天要玫瑰、琥珀或高对比黄，它们提的是地形层次，不是亮度。
雪杖用倒握法量：手握在杖篮上方的杖身，把握把立在地上，前臂应呈水平，肘部接近 90 度。穿雪靴时量出来大约比穿鞋时短 5 cm。雪杖到 st-07 才真正开始有用。
穿衣：一层排汗内层、一层保暖中层、一层防风防水外壳——每只脚一只薄袜。不要两只，合脚壳测的靴子里更不要穿厚袜。两只袜子会互相打滑、吃掉脚需要的容积，还让脚更冷。
hard_rules: 自行车盔和轮滑盔不是滑雪盔——它们没有针对这种冲击形式和低温取得认证。
绝不要戴来历不明的头盔。一次你没看见的冲击，就让它只剩装饰作用。
sections.heading: 头盔、雪镜、雪杖与穿衣

tables.caption: 镜片 VLT 与光线的对应。
rows: 强日照、春季玉米雪、冰川

adaptation_notes.note: 这个尺码阶段租不买。脚变化的速度快过一个雪季，而这个年龄段比谁都更需要正确的适配，而不是所有权。
先整套租两三天，再去买靴。雪上教会你的，比在店里聊一小时多。

body: 先买靴，板先租。靴子是私人物品、对适配极端敏感；板是可替换的，试板队还能让你先试出长度和腰宽。一季滑到大约 6-8 天以上就该买靴；过了 st-06、知道自己实际滑什么地形之后再买板。
打磨：大众刻滑的规格是底刃角 0.5-1 度、侧刃角 1-2 度，板头板尾用磨石走几下做钝刃处理，让板进弯出弯都不挂刃。侧刃角 2-3 度是竞技设定——抓地极强，也会惩罚每一次晚了的换刃。每滑 4-6 天打一次蜡。
孩子的装备：过大的靴子不是让滑雪变难，是让滑雪在物理上不成立。孩子撑不满的壳压不动，感觉不到板，只能后座、用防御性的犁式站着。这看起来像技术问题，其实不是。按当季的脚配，哪怕意味着每年都租。
租赁队里的青少年板经常是钝的、没蜡的——一季的石头已经把刃磨圆了。一个在绿道上立不住刃的孩子，往往是踩着一支立不住刃的板。取板时用拇指沿脚下那段刃摸一遍，然后要求开刃。
checklist: 壳测已在取出内胆的情况下做过，后跟留一根手指。
脱离值本季已由技师设定并做过功能测试。
靴底标准与固定器上的认证标记一致。
头盔有认证、无损伤，雪镜上缘不露额头。
脚下那段刃锋利，板头板尾做过钝刃处理，底面打过蜡。
每只脚一只薄袜，另备一双干袜。
hard_rules: 绝不要给孩子买大一码或两码、想撑两个雪季的靴子。那拿掉的是他滑雪的能力，不只是舒适。
sections.heading: 租还是买、打磨，以及孩子的装备

body: The snow types are defined in the shared reference vocabulary; this module is about what each one asks of you and when to expect it. The habit worth building is naming the surface out loud at the top of the run. A skier who has named the condition has already chosen a turn size, an edge angle and a speed.

Two groupings do most of the work. Firm surfaces (sn-corduroy, sn-hardpack, sn-boilerplate) reward progressive early edging and punish anything abrupt. Soft and variable surfaces (sn-powder-light, sn-crud, sn-slush-deep) reward a two-footed platform, absorption and patience, and punish the aggressive outside-ski-only stance that firm snow rewards.

The two hardest common conditions, sn-crust-breakable and sn-spring-refreeze, are hard for the same reason: support is intermittent, so no single tactic survives two consecutive turns. Recognising them from the chairlift is more valuable than any technique for skiing them, and the table below is meant to be read before the first lift rather than mid-run.
sections.heading: Reading the surface

tables.caption: Condition, tactics and difficulty (1 easiest, 5 hardest), matching the snow ids in the reference vocabulary
rows: Early progressive edging; honest feedback from your own tracks. The learning surface.
Nothing special: grippy and forgiving. The default assumption for drills.
Sharp edges, edge engaged above the fall line, no abrupt movements.
Lower edge angle and better balance; ski the edges of the run. Test, do not learn.
Enough speed to plane, an even two-footed platform, rounder and more patient turns.
More speed, wider ski, and less edge than instinct asks for; it grabs the tips.
Two-footed platform, absorb with the legs, quiet torso. The least-practised common condition.
Both feet as one platform, slow round turns, and a willingness to go elsewhere.
Predictable once identified; aspect and hour tell you exactly where it is.
Expect resistance to change without warning; stay centred and shorten the turn.
A narrow window of excellent skiing; follow the sun from east aspects to west.
Grabby and tiring, and a caught tip is a real injury. Stop earlier than you want to.
Wait for the sun. Not difficult so much as not worth skiing.

body: Aspect and time of day are the single most useful planning tool in skiing, and they cost nothing but attention. The sun moves predictably and the snow responds predictably. Knowing where the sun has been for the last three hours tells you more about how a run will ski than its trail rating does.

In the northern hemisphere, east faces catch the first sun and soften first, which makes them the spring morning choice and the refrozen afternoon trap. North faces hold cold winter snow longest and are where powder survives for days after a storm. West and south faces soften late, go to slush, and refreeze hardest overnight.

Southern hemisphere skiers swap north and south; the logic is identical. The practical habit is to follow the sun around the mountain instead of skiing a fixed circuit, and to accept that the same run is genuinely two different sports at nine in the morning and one in the afternoon.
sections.heading: Aspect and time of day

adaptation_notes.note: Timing substitutes for force. Choosing the softened hour and the quieter aspect makes terrain skiable that the same skier could not ski at nine in the morning, and it lowers fall consequence at the same time.
Plan the day around temperature rather than vertical: the cold hours are the wrong hours regardless of the snow, and a cold child stops learning before they stop complaining.

body: A ski day has a usable shape. Corduroy owns the first hour or two and is the honest surface for edging work and track inspection. Hardpack steeps are a mid-morning job, once traffic has taken the glaze off but before the surface turns to piles. Put the technical work of the day inside that window deliberately.

Bumps belong to the afternoon, once sun has softened the faces (st-13). Frozen bumps on a cold morning teach nothing and hurt people, because absorption is impossible in a hard trough. Softness is the biggest single variable in mogul skiing, which makes the choice of hour a larger lever than any drill.

Spring is the narrowest window of all. Corn arrives when the overnight freeze has released the top few centimetres and is gone within two or three hours as the snow saturates. Start high on east aspects and move west through the morning. Arriving an hour early is worse than arriving an hour late.
checklist: Overnight low and current temperature: did it freeze, and has it released yet?
New snow depth and wind direction over the last 24 hours
Which aspects have had sun, and for how long
One primary objective plus one easier fallback, chosen before the first lift
A named turn-around time for spring skiing, before the snow saturates
Lens or goggle choice matched to the forecast light, with a spare carried
sections.heading: How a day unfolds

body: A storm does not open the mountain all at once. Patrol works from low consequence upward, so groomers open first, then in-bounds ungroomed terrain, then the steeper avalanche-controlled zones, sometimes a full day later. The best in-bounds snow is frequently available on the second morning rather than during the storm itself.

Wind is the variable most often underestimated. It strips snow from windward slopes and loads it onto lee slopes and behind ridges, gullies and terrain breaks, producing sn-wind-slab. In bounds that is a technique problem: resistance changes abruptly, sometimes turn to turn. Out of bounds it is an avalanche problem and outside this curriculum entirely.

After a storm, expect the surviving snow at the edges of runs, in trees where wind cannot reach it (st-15), and on north aspects. Expect it to be tracked into sn-crud by mid-morning on a weekend - a condition worth practising deliberately rather than mourning, since it is what off-piste terrain looks like most of the time.
sections.heading: Storm cycles and wind

body: Flat light removes the shadows that tell you where the surface is. Rolls, troughs and edges disappear, and skiers respond by leaning back and slowing down, which makes them less stable rather than more. The response has an optical half and a tactical half, and the tactical half matters more.

Lens choice is expressed as visible light transmission. Bright sun wants roughly 5-20 percent; broken cloud 20-40 percent; overcast and falling snow 40-70 percent; dusk and dense fog above 70 percent. Rose, amber and yellow tints raise contrast in flat light. Carry a second lens or a second goggle rather than squinting through the wrong one all day.

Tactically, ski where there is something to see. Stay near a treeline, a trail edge, a lift line or a marker line, because a vertical reference restores the horizon the light has taken away. Shorten the turns, keep the stance centred, and follow another skier at a safe distance to read the terrain a second early.
sections.heading: Flat light and visibility

body: Cold changes equipment before it changes snow. Boot plastic stiffens noticeably below about -10 C (14 F), so a boot that flexes well at freezing point may barely flex on a January morning - a real and frequently misdiagnosed reason a skier feels stuck in the back seat. Store boots warm and expect the first runs to feel different.

Wax hardness follows snow temperature: harder for cold snow, softer for warm. That is a glide question on flats and cat tracks rather than a technique question. Edge grip is also a temperature story, since the same run holds an edge at -8 C (18 F) and lets go near freezing, when a film of free water forms at the surface.

Some conditions test skill instead of building it. Breakable crust, spring refreeze and boilerplate punish every error and reward almost nothing, and the learning rate in them is close to zero. They are worth one or two runs a season as an audit of what actually holds up, and no more than that.

So the right response to a bad surface is a different run or a different hour, not more determination. Choosing the surface is a tactical skill in its own right, and it is a large part of what separates skiers who keep improving for thirty years from skiers who plateau and blame the conditions.
hard_rules: Do not ski spring refreeze before it softens. Wait for the sun or ski somewhere else.
sections.heading: Temperature, equipment, and the conditions that only test

body: 雪质的定义放在共用参考词表里；本模块讲的是每一种雪质向你要求什么、以及什么时候会遇到它。值得养成的习惯是在雪道顶上把雪面的名字说出来。一个说得出雪况名字的人，其实已经顺手选好了弯的大小、刃角和速度。
两个大类承担了大部分工作。硬雪面（压雪纹 sn-corduroy、硬雪 sn-hardpack、冰面 sn-boilerplate）奖励渐进的早立刃，惩罚一切突然的动作。软而多变的雪面（轻粉雪 sn-powder-light、乱雪 sn-crud、深烂雪 sn-slush-deep）奖励双脚一个平台、吸收和耐心，惩罚硬雪上那种只压外板的进攻性站姿。
两种最难的常见雪况——易碎壳雪 sn-crust-breakable 和春季再冻雪 sn-spring-refreeze——难在同一个理由上：支撑是断续的，所以没有哪一种战术能连续撑过两个弯。在缆车上就把它们认出来，比任何滑它们的技术都更值钱；下面这张表是给上第一趟缆车之前看的，不是滑到一半再想的。
sections.heading: 读雪面

tables.caption: 雪况、战术与难度（1 最易，5 最难），与参考词表中的 sn-* 一一对应
rows: 渐进的早立刃；能从自己的雪痕里得到诚实反馈。学习用的雪面。
没什么特别的：抓得住、宽容。本课程练习默认的就是它。
刃要锋利，刃在落线以上就立好，任何突然的动作都不行。
降低刃角、把平衡做好；走雪道两侧。用来检验，不要用来学。
速度够才浮得起来，双脚要一个均匀的平台，弯更圆、更有耐心。
速度更快、板更宽、刃比直觉要求的更少；它会抓板头。
双脚一个平台，用腿吸收，躯干安静。最常见却最少练的雪况。
两脚当成一个平台，慢而圆的弯，以及换个地方滑的觉悟。
认出来之后很好预测；坡向和钟点就能准确告诉你它在哪里。
预期阻力会毫无预告地变化；保持中立站姿并把弯做小。
一个很窄的时间窗里非常好滑；跟着太阳从东坡走到西坡。
抓板、耗体力，板头一被抓住就是真实的受伤风险。比你想收工的时间更早收工。
等太阳。它不算难，只是不值得滑。

body: 坡向和时间是滑雪里最有用的单一规划工具，成本只是留意而已。太阳的移动是可预测的，雪的反应也是可预测的。知道过去三小时太阳照在哪里，对一条雪道会怎么滑的判断价值，高于它的难度标记。
在北半球，东坡最先吃到太阳、最先变软，所以它是春季上午的首选，也是下午的再冻陷阱。北坡把冬天的冷雪保住最久，暴风雪之后粉雪能在那里活好几天。西坡和南坡变软最晚，接着化成烂雪，夜里也冻得最硬。
南半球把南北互换，逻辑完全一样。落到实践上的习惯是：跟着太阳绕山走，而不是走一条固定的环线；并且接受同一条雪道在上午九点和下午一点确实是两个不同的项目。
sections.heading: 坡向与时间

adaptation_notes.note: 时机可以替代力量。选对变软的钟点和人少的坡向，能让同一个人滑得动早上九点滑不动的地形，同时还降低了摔倒的后果。
按温度而不是按落差安排一天：不管雪好不好，冷的那几个钟点就是错的钟点，而冷起来的孩子会先停止学习，然后才开始抱怨。

body: 一个滑雪日有可用的形状。头一到两小时属于压雪纹，它是做立刃练习和查看自己雪痕最诚实的雪面。硬雪陡坡是上午中段的活儿：等人流把那层釉面刮掉，但要赶在雪面被推成一堆一堆之前。有意识地把当天的技术工作放进这个窗口里。
雪包属于下午，等太阳把包面晒软之后（st-13）。冷的早上滑冻硬雪包既教不了东西又伤人，因为在硬槽里根本没法吸收。软硬是雪包滑行里最大的单一变量，这让选钟点成为比任何练习都更大的杠杆。
春天的窗口最窄。玉米雪在夜冻把表面几厘米松开时出现，随着雪含水饱和，两三小时内就消失。从高处的东坡开始，一个上午里逐渐往西移。早到一小时比晚到一小时更糟。
checklist: 夜间最低温与当前温度：夜里冻了吗？现在松开了吗？
过去 24 小时的新雪厚度与风向
哪些坡向已经吃到太阳，晒了多久
上第一趟缆车之前定好一个主要目标，加一个更简单的备选
春季滑雪定一个明确的收工时刻，在雪含水饱和之前
镜片或雪镜按预报的光线条件选，并且随身带一副备用
sections.heading: 一天是怎么展开的

body: 一场暴风雪不会一次就把整座山打开。巡逻队从后果最小的地方往上做，所以压雪道先开，然后是场内非压雪地形，再然后是更陡的雪崩控制区，有时要晚整整一天。场内最好的雪，往往出现在第二天上午，而不是暴风雪当时。
风是最常被低估的变量。它把雪从迎风坡剥走，堆积到背风坡以及山脊、沟槽和地形断层的后方，形成风板雪 sn-wind-slab。在场内这是技术问题：阻力会突然改变，有时一个弯换一个样。出了场界它就是雪崩问题，完全不在本课程范围内。
暴风雪之后，活下来的雪要到雪道边缘、风进不去的树林里（st-15）和北坡去找。也要预期它在周末上午过半时就被滑成乱雪 sn-crud——这是一种值得专门去练、而不是拿来惋惜的雪况，因为野雪地形大多数时候就长这样。
sections.heading: 暴风雪周期与风

body: 平光把告诉你雪面在哪里的那些阴影拿走了。起伏、凹槽和落差消失，滑雪者的反应是后坐加减速，而这让人更不稳，不是更稳。应对分成光学的一半和战术的一半，战术那半更重要。
镜片选择用可见光透过率来表达。大晴天大约要 5-20%；多云间晴 20-40%；阴天和降雪 40-70%；黄昏和浓雾在 70% 以上。玫红、琥珀和黄色镜片能在平光下提高对比。带第二片镜片或第二副雪镜，而不是戴着错的那副眯一整天。
战术上，去有东西可看的地方滑。贴着林线、雪道边缘、缆车线或标杆线走，因为一条竖直的参照物能把光线拿走的那条地平线还给你。把弯做小，站姿保持中立，跟在另一位滑雪者后面保持安全距离，好提前一秒读到地形。
sections.heading: 平光与能见度

body: 低温改变装备，早于它改变雪。靴壳塑料在大约 -10 C（14 F）以下明显变硬，所以一双在零度附近弯得挺顺的靴子，在一月的早上可能几乎压不动——这是滑雪者觉得自己被卡在后座上的真实原因，而且经常被误诊。把靴子放在暖处存放，并预期前几趟的感觉不一样。
蜡的硬度跟着雪温走：冷雪用硬蜡，暖雪用软蜡。这在平缓段和猫道上是滑行速度的问题，不是技术问题。刃的抓地也是温度的故事：同一条雪道在 -8 C（18 F）能咬住刃，接近零度时就松开了，因为表面形成了一层自由水膜。
有些雪况只检验能力，不生长能力。易碎壳雪、春季再冻雪和冰面惩罚每一个错误，几乎不奖励任何东西，在其中的学习速率接近零。它们一个雪季值得滑一两趟，作为对「哪些东西真的立得住」的一次审计，仅此而已。
所以对糟糕雪面的正确回应是换一条雪道或换一个钟点，不是加大决心。挑雪面本身就是一项独立的战术能力，也是那些能连续进步三十年的人与那些停在原地、把责任推给雪况的人之间，很大一部分的差别所在。
hard_rules: 春季再冻雪变软之前不要滑。等太阳，或者换个地方滑。
sections.heading: 气温、装备，以及那些只能用来检验的雪况

body: Every rating is set by the resort that owns the run, relative to the rest of that resort's terrain. There is no cross-resort standard, no gradient threshold, and no external audit. A grade describes one mountain's own range, published partly for safety and partly for marketing.

Hence the one rule here: on an unfamiliar mountain, drop one grade for your first run. It costs a single descent and calibrates everything after it. Do the same on the first run of a trip and after any layoff.
The tr-* ids in reference.json carry the gradient bands and regional equivalents; read those, not the colour on the sign. A European red is typically steeper than a North American blue.
hard_rules: Drop one grade for the first run on any unfamiliar mountain. It matters more for experts, whose error is larger and faster.
sections.heading: Rating systems, and why a rating is not a measurement

tables.caption: How the regional systems behave, and the trap in each
rows: Green circle, blue square, black diamond, double black
Graded within the resort by patrol and marketing. A small hill's black is often a large resort's blue.
Double black means consequence — exposure, narrow entrances, mandatory lines — not only pitch.
Green and blue gentler than the North American names suggest; red carries most intermediate terrain; black is a very wide band.
Read red as tr-blue at best, a hard red as tr-black-groomed.
Green, red, black, gradient often posted at the top
Signage quotes a percentage or degree gradient, more useful than any colour.
The figure is the steepest point, not the average.
Imported North American or Japanese colours, sometimes both
Small vertical compresses the mountain into few grades; a black may be short, groomed and 22 degrees.
Read pitch, length and run-out, not the grade.

body: Terrain is a prerequisite, not a preference. The wrong ground stalls a skier doing everything else right, and the commonest venue problem is not a mountain that is too hard but one that lacks the single thing the current tier needs.

Read the table as a shopping list and check the map against it before booking. Vertical matters as much as grade: tier 2 needs runs of 300 vertical metres (1,000 ft) or more, because rhythm cannot be built in eight-turn fragments.
Where the terrain is missing, change the venue rather than the standard. Skiing the wrong ground harder is how a stage gets claimed without being passed.
sections.heading: What terrain each tier actually requires

tables.caption: Terrain required by tier, and what quietly kills progress in each
rows: tr-flat, tr-carpet, tr-green: shallow pitch, flat run-out, wide enough to traverse
Narrow cat tracks. Too flat to turn, too narrow to traverse, and they reward the defensive stance this tier exists to prevent.
tr-blue-easy and tr-blue: wide groomers long enough for 25-30 turns, plus a rolling pitch change
Only crowded mid-day blues. Traffic forces reactive skiing and fragments the run, so no rhythm survives.
tr-black-groomed for edge work, soft tr-bumps-blue for absorption, firm morning snow
Only frozen bumps. Absorption cannot be learned on a surface that punishes every error.
tr-ungroomed and tr-glades, plus snow that changes: crud, crust, corn, wind-affected
A resort that grooms everything, so the tier's conditions never appear.

adaptation_notes.note: A fenced children's area with its own conveyor, out of adult traffic, matters more than the mountain attached to it.
A learning area crossed by fast traffic turns an ordinary fear response into a lost day.

body: A steep or crowded beginner area is the most common reason a first day fails, and it is visible before anybody clicks in. Walk over and look before booking the lesson or the rental.

What you want: a pitch of roughly 3-8 degrees, a flat run-out that stops a skier who does nothing at all, conveyor or rope access rather than a chairlift, width to traverse, and separation from traffic descending from above.

What disqualifies an area: a slope running out into a lift queue, a flat that must be poled across, faster skiers crossing the teaching ground, or a first lift that is a chair. A resort with a poor learning area and a good mountain is a bad choice for a first day and a fine one for a fifth.
checklist: Stand at the top: can you see a flat run-out with nothing in it?
Where does through-traffic from above cross? If it crosses the teaching slope, choose elsewhere.
Is the access a conveyor or rope tow rather than a chairlift?
How many people are on it at 10 a.m., not at opening?
sections.heading: Learning-area quality, which decides the first day

body: A short repeatable pitch is genuinely good for drill work. Sixty laps of a 150-metre (500 ft) slope in an evening delivers more edge releases than a day at a large resort, and the conditions do not move underneath you. Practice wants repeatability more than scenery.
What a short pitch cannot teach is a full run's rhythm — the 25-30 turns without stopping that tier 2 is built on — nor fatigue management, nor snow that changes down the hill.

Use both deliberately: local frequency to change a pattern, destination trips to make it survive. The common mistake runs the other way, treating one week a year at a big mountain as the whole programme.
sections.heading: Indoor slopes, dry slopes, small hills and big resorts

tables.caption: Venue types: what each can and cannot teach
rows: Indoor snow hall, 100-200 m (330-660 ft), uniform pitch
Everything to st-05, and drill work at any stage. Conditions never vary, so a change in the skiing is a change in the skier.
Rhythm over a full run, pitch changes, snow variation, tier-3 and tier-4 content.
Wedge, edging and turn shape; cheap off-season volume.
Sliding and grip, which differ enough to need re-learning on snow. Falls hurt more, which suppresses commitment.
Small local hill, 100-250 m (330-820 ft) vertical
Tier 1 and most tier-2 drill work. Frequency beats grandeur for grooving a movement.
Sustained rhythm, long-run fatigue, the varied snow of tier 4.
Every tier, plus the variety and vertical tiers 3 and 4 need.
Nothing in principle, but one week changes less than ten evenings on a repeatable pitch.

body: A trail map is a marketing document that happens to contain topography. It compresses pitch, exaggerates width, and omits the two things that matter most: where a run actually ends, and what happens if you cannot ski it.

Read it for four things: where the run finishes and which lift that is; whether there is an exit partway down; whether the run-out is flat, a cat track, or a traverse above something; and where the run narrows. A run with no exit and no visible end is a commitment, whatever its colour.

Contour lines are usually absent, so use proxies: closely drawn switchbacks mean a traverse or cat track; a run drawn shorter than its neighbours off the same lift is steeper; a run ending at a different lift means a long flat exit.
checklist: Where does this run end, and which lift or road is there?
Is there an exit partway down, and at what point?
Is the run-out flat, a cat track, or a traverse above something?
Where is the narrowest point, and does it merge with another run?
sections.heading: Reading a trail map

adaptation_notes.note: Fearlessness makes judgement the limiter, not skill. Agree terrain and a regroup point from the map before loading.
Fall avoidance makes venue and timing a technique decision: uncrowded runs, early corduroy, an exit on every line.

body: Look at a run three times: from the lift that passes over it, from the top at the entrance, and from the first few turns taken near the edge, where sideslipping out is still available.

The lift gives the only honest view of pitch and of the whole shape at once — where the bumps are, where the ice is, where people are stopping, whether the fall line runs into a merge. Ride it once to look, and choose the line then.

From the top, look for the run-out and the exit. If you cannot see where the run goes, you are looking at a rollover, and the pitch beyond it is unknown. That is information: sideslip in from the edge until it is visible, or ski something else.
Time of day and traffic move the assessment as much as pitch does. The crowded version of any run is a grade harder than the empty one.
hard_rules: No visible run-out means unknown pitch and unknown consequence. Sideslip in from the edge until you can see it, or ski something else.
On an unfamiliar mountain, do not commit to terrain you have not seen from below or from the lift.
sections.heading: Assessing a run before committing to it

body: 每一个难度标记都由拥有这条道的雪场自己定，而且相对于该雪场其余地形来定。没有跨雪场的统一标准，没有坡度门槛，也没有外部审核。一个等级描述的是这座山自己的难度跨度，一半为了安全，一半为了宣传。
所以这里只有一条规则：到陌生的山，第一趟降一档。代价只有一趟，换来之后所有判断的校准。行程的第一趟和任何一段停滑之后，同样办理。
reference.json 里的 tr-* 带着坡度区间和各地区对应关系；看那个，不要看标牌上的颜色。欧洲的红道通常比北美的蓝道更陡。
hard_rules: 到任何陌生的山，第一趟降一档。这条对高手更要紧，因为他们的误差更大、也来得更快。
sections.heading: 分级体系，以及为什么分级不是测量值

tables.caption: 各地区体系的实际行为，以及各自的坑
rows: 绿圆圈、蓝方块、黑菱形、双黑菱形
由巡逻队和市场部在本雪场内部定级。小雪场的黑道往往等于大雪场的蓝道。
双黑指的是后果——暴露感、窄入口、必须走的唯一线路——不只是坡度。
绿道和蓝道比北美同名等级更缓；红道装着大部分中级地形；黑道是非常宽的一档。
把红道当 tr-blue 来读已经算乐观，硬红道要按 tr-black-groomed 处理。
绿道、红道、黑道，坡顶常直接标坡度
标识上写百分比或角度，比任何颜色都有用。
那个数字是最陡处，不是平均值。
沿用北美或日本的颜色，有时两套并用
落差小，把整座山压缩进很少的等级里；一条黑道可能又短又压过雪、只有 22 度。
看坡度、长度和出口，不要看等级。

body: 地形是前提条件，不是偏好。地不对，别的都做对的人照样卡住；最常见的场地问题不是山太难，而是这座山缺了当前层级唯一需要的那样东西。
把这张表当采购清单，订行程之前先拿雪道图对一遍。落差和等级一样要紧：第二层级需要 300 米（1,000 ft）以上落差的雪道，因为节奏没法在「8 个弯一段」里建起来。
地形缺了，就换场地，不要改标准。在错的地上更用力地滑，正是一个级别被宣称却没被通过的方式。
sections.heading: 每个层级真正需要什么地形

tables.caption: 各层级所需地形，以及各层级里悄悄杀死进步的东西
rows: tr-flat、tr-carpet、tr-green：坡度浅、出口平坦、宽到能横切
窄猫道。平到转不起来、窄到没法横切，奖励的正是这一层级要防住的防御性站姿。
tr-blue-easy 和 tr-blue：宽压雪道，长到能连续 25-30 个弯，再加一处坡度变化
只有中午人挤的蓝道。人流逼出被动反应式滑行，把一趟切碎，节奏一点也留不下来。
练刃用 tr-black-groomed，练吸收用软的 tr-bumps-blue，加上早上的硬雪
只有冻硬雪包。在惩罚每个错误的雪面上，吸收学不会。
tr-ungroomed 和 tr-glades，加上会变的雪：乱雪、壳雪、玉米雪、风吹雪
一座什么都压雪的雪场，这一层级需要的雪况根本不会出现。

adaptation_notes.note: 一块围起来、有自己魔毯、隔开成人人流的儿童区，比它挂在哪座山上更重要。
被快速人流横穿的教学区，会把一次普通的恐惧反应变成整天报废。

body: 一块偏陡或人挤的初学区是第一天失败最常见的原因，而这件事在踏板之前就看得出来。走过去看一眼，再决定订课或租具。
你要的是：大约 3-8 度的坡度、一片什么都不做也能把人停住的平坦出口、魔毯或牵引绳而不是吊椅、够横切的宽度，以及与上方下来的人流隔开。
让一块教学区不合格的条件：坡底直接汇入缆车排队区、必须靠撑杖走过去的平段、更快的滑雪者横穿教学场地，或者第一条上山设施就是吊椅。教学区差而山不错的雪场，第一天是坏选择，第五天是好选择。
checklist: 站在坡顶：能看到一片什么都没有的平坦出口吗？
上方过路的人流从哪里穿过？穿过教学坡就换地方。
上山设施是魔毯或牵引绳，而不是吊椅吗？
上午 10 点这块地上有多少人？看这个点，不是看刚开门。
sections.heading: 教学区质量，它决定了第一天

body: 一段短而可重复的坡，对练习来说确实好用。一个晚上在 150 米（500 ft）的坡上刷 60 趟，交付的解刃次数多于在大雪场滑一天，而且雪况不会在脚下变来变去。练习要的是可重复，不是风景。
短坡教不了一整趟的节奏——第二层级立身之本的那连续 25-30 个弯——也教不了体力分配，也没有沿坡而下不断变化的雪。
两样都有意识地用：靠本地的高频率改掉一个动作模式，靠目的地行程让这个改变站得住。常见错误方向正好相反：把一年一周的大山之行当成全部训练计划。
sections.heading: 室内雪场、旱雪场、小雪场与大雪场

tables.caption: 场地类型：各自能教什么、教不了什么
rows: st-05 以前的一切，以及任何级别的练习。雪况从不变化，所以滑行变了就是人变了。
一整趟的节奏、坡度变化、雪质变化，以及第三、第四层级的内容。
犁式、立刃和弯形；便宜的夏季训练量。
滑行感与抓地，两者差别大到上雪后要重新学。摔了更疼，会压抑投入程度。
第一层级和第二层级大部分练习。要把一个动作刻进身体，频率胜过气派。
持续的节奏、长距离的疲劳，以及第四层级那种多变的雪。
所有层级，加上第三、第四层级需要的多样性和落差。
原理上没有教不了的，但一周带来的改变少于在可重复的坡上练十个晚上。

body: 雪道图是一份恰好含地形信息的宣传材料。它压缩坡度、夸大宽度，漏掉最要紧的两件事：这条道到底在哪里结束，以及滑不下来会怎么办。
读它就读四件事：这条道在哪里结束、那里是哪条缆车；中途有没有撤出口；出口是平段、猫道，还是横切在某个东西上方；以及它在哪里变窄。一条没有撤出口又看不到尽头的道，无论标什么颜色，都是不可撤回的投入。
等高线通常没有，所以用替代线索：折返画得密表示有横切道或猫道；同一条缆车下画得比邻道短的道更陡；结束在另一条缆车的道意味着很长的平坦出口。
checklist: 这条道在哪里结束，那里是哪条缆车或哪条路？
中途有撤出口吗？在什么位置？
出口是平段、猫道，还是横切在某个东西上方？
最窄的地方在哪里，会不会与另一条道汇合？
sections.heading: 读雪道图

adaptation_notes.note: 不怕摔让判断力成为限制因素，不是技术。上缆车之前先对着雪道图约定好地形和一个集合点。
以不摔为前提，场地和时机就成了技术决策：人少的雪道、清早的压雪纹，每条线路都留一个撤出口。

body: 一条道要看三次：从它上方的缆车上看、从坡顶入口看，以及贴着边缘滑最初几个弯时看——那时还有侧滑撤出的余地。
缆车提供唯一诚实的视角：坡度，以及整条道的形状一次看全——雪包、冰、人停在哪里，落线会不会撞进汇合口。先坐一趟专门去看，线路那时就选好。
从坡顶看，要找出口和撤出点。看不到这条道往哪里去，你看的就是一个凸起翻越点，翻过去的坡度未知。这本身就是信息：从边缘侧滑进去直到看清，或者去滑别的。
时间和人流对评估的影响和坡度一样大。任何一条道人挤的版本都比空的版本难一档。
hard_rules: 看不见出口，就意味着坡度未知、后果未知。从边缘侧滑进去直到看清，或者去滑别的。
在陌生的山上，绝不踏进没有从下方或从缆车上看过的地形。
sections.heading: 踏进一条雪道之前怎么评估它

glossary.definition: Creating edge angle by bending at hip, knee and ankle while keeping the upper body comparatively upright.
Tipping the whole body toward the inside of the turn. Necessary at speed, insufficient on its own.
Inclination without angulation — the fault version of leaning in, which loads the inside ski and loses grip.
The moment both skis move from their old edges to their new ones. Simultaneous edge change is the defining feature of parallel skiing.
Pushing one ski out to an angle to start a turn or create a platform. Legitimate in tier 1, a fault from st-06 onward.
Tips together, tails apart. The first speed-control and turning tool.
A turn started in a wedge whose skis are matched to parallel in the second half.
Bringing the inside ski parallel to the outside ski during the turn.
The low-pressure moment between two arcs, where both skis pass through flat.
The steepest, most direct line down the slope at a given point.
The geometry of the arc. A round C-shape controls speed; a Z-shape brakes.
How tight the arc is. Short, medium and long radius are choices, not consequences.
Balance along the length of the ski, forward versus back.
Body mass over the middle of the feet, with light even shin contact on the boot tongues.
The ski on the outside of the arc — the downhill ski, and the one that should carry most of the load.
The ski on the inside of the arc. Engaged and parallel, but light.
The outside edge of a foot. Tipping the new inside foot onto it is what starts a modern turn.
The inside edge of a foot — the gripping edge of the outside ski in a turn.
How load is split between the two skis, commonly expressed as a ratio such as 80/20.
The upper body facing a different direction from the legs and skis.
Actively facing the outside of the turn, so the legs can rotate under a stable torso.
Lateral movement that keeps the body's mass over the outside ski at high edge angle.
A turn in which the skis track along their edges without sliding sideways; the tail follows the tip.
A turn in which the ski travels partly across its own length. A tool, not only a fault.
Drill: pure tipping with no steering, leaving two thin parallel lines.
Drill: continuous small stepping through the whole turn, to kill park-and-ride.
Setting an edge at the start of the turn and passively waiting for it to finish.
Drill: repeated partial turns across a slope without completing them.
Drill: the lifted inside ski crossed over the outside ski's tip through the turn.
Drill: pivoting the skis 180 degrees within a controlled sideslip, chest facing downhill. The core steeps skill.
Letting the skis slide sideways under control, and stopping the slide at will. The universal escape route.
Drill: sideslipping while drifting forward and back diagonally.
A rapid simultaneous pivot and edge-set to a stop, both directions.
Rhythmic, quick, edge-checked turns down the fall line with a blocking pole plant.
Releasing a turn by flexing the legs and letting the skis pass under the body.
Releasing a turn by moving the body over and across the skis. Correct at lower speeds and gentler pitches.
An abrupt vertical extension used to unload the ski. A dated timing error, distinct from a progressive extension.
A light contact of the pole basket at the transition, used for timing and carrying no weight.
A firmer, blocking pole action that stabilizes the upper body and triggers the release in short-radius and steep skiing.
Flexing to swallow terrain so the upper body travels a level path. The basis of mogul skiing.
The straight-down-the-troughs mogul line: fastest, hardest, and the wrong place to start.
Turning on the uphill faces of moguls. The friendly line, and where speed control lives.
Jumping the skis around in place on very steep or narrow terrain.
A deliberate pivot-then-carve, used to redirect quickly at speed. Racing's answer to a late turn.
Knees converging while the skis stay apart — the inside leg tipped the wrong way.
Sizing a boot with the liner removed, measuring the gap behind the heel. One finger is the target.
The setting at which a binding releases the boot, calculated by a technician from height, weight, boot sole length, age and skier type.
ISO 5355 (alpine), GripWalk and ISO 9523 (touring) are not interchangeable; a mismatch can prevent release.
Visible light transmission — how much light a goggle lens passes. Low for sun, high for flat light.
Deliberately dulling the edge at the tip and tail contact points so the ski does not hook.
Tuning angles that determine how quickly a ski engages and how hard it grips. 0.5-1 degree base, 1-2 side is a recreational carving setting.
The ribbed surface left by a grooming machine.
A narrow, near-flat traverse or service road. The place intermediates most often fall.
The void of loose snow around a tree trunk. A suffocation hazard and the reason for the partner rule.
Snow immersion suffocation — the mechanism behind tree-well and deep-snow deaths.
Skiable, spaced trees.
Ungroomed, unpatrolled terrain accessed from a lift. Backcountry risk with resort convenience, and outside this curriculum's scope.
The classic ACL injury mechanism: off balance backward, weight on the inside edge of the tail of the downhill ski, hips below the knees.
The ten-point skier conduct code published by NSAA (2022 revision), covering control, right of way, stopping, signage, lifts, impairment and collision duties.
Working on exactly one thing per run, named out loud before the run starts.

snow_conditions.description: Freshly groomed snow with a ribbed surface.
snow_conditions.name: Corduroy
snow_conditions.tactics: The best surface for learning edging and for honest feedback from your own tracks. Get there early; it lasts about two hours on a busy run.

snow_conditions.description: Snow compacted by skier traffic but still soft enough to hold an edge easily.
snow_conditions.name: Packed powder
snow_conditions.tactics: Forgiving and grippy. The default assumption for most drills in this curriculum.

snow_conditions.description: Dense, firm, cold snow that still takes an edge but punishes late or abrupt edging.
snow_conditions.name: Hardpack
snow_conditions.tactics: Set the edge progressively and above the fall line. Sharp edges stop being optional.

snow_conditions.description: Refrozen, scraped or rain-crusted surface with little to grip.
snow_conditions.name: Boilerplate / ice
snow_conditions.tactics: Lower edge angle and better balance beat higher edge angle. Ski the edges of the run, where snow survives. Avoid for skill acquisition; use for skill testing.

snow_conditions.description: Low-density fresh snow, typically continental or high-altitude.
snow_conditions.name: Light powder
snow_conditions.tactics: Needs speed to plane and a more even two-footed platform. Rounder, more patient turns.

snow_conditions.description: Dense fresh snow with high water content.
snow_conditions.name: Heavy / maritime powder
snow_conditions.tactics: Resists strongly and grabs the tips. Wider skis, more speed, and less edge than instinct suggests.

snow_conditions.description: Tracked-out, chopped, uneven snow with variable resistance turn to turn.
snow_conditions.name: Crud
snow_conditions.tactics: Two-footed platform, absorb with the legs, keep the upper body quiet. The most common off-piste condition, and the least practised.

snow_conditions.description: A hard surface layer over softer snow that supports the skier intermittently.
snow_conditions.name: Breakable crust
snow_conditions.tactics: The hardest common condition in skiing. Both feet as one platform, rounder and slower turns, and a willingness to go elsewhere.

snow_conditions.description: A thin, glazed surface layer formed by solar radiation, often with soft snow beneath.
snow_conditions.name: Sun crust
snow_conditions.tactics: Predictable once identified. Aspect and time of day tell you where it is.

snow_conditions.description: Snow redistributed and compacted by wind, with abrupt changes in density and support.
snow_conditions.name: Wind slab / wind-affected snow
snow_conditions.tactics: In-bounds it is a technique problem; out of bounds it is an avalanche problem. Expect the resistance to change without warning.

snow_conditions.description: Loose, rounded spring granules that soften predictably through the morning.
snow_conditions.name: Corn
snow_conditions.tactics: Excellent skiing in a narrow time window. Follow the sun around the mountain: east aspects first, west last.

snow_conditions.description: Wet, heavy, saturated snow late in a warm day.
snow_conditions.name: Deep slush
snow_conditions.tactics: Grabby and tiring; a real injury risk when a tip catches. Stop earlier than you want to.

snow_conditions.description: Yesterday's slush, frozen solid into a rutted, uneven surface.
snow_conditions.name: Spring refreeze
snow_conditions.tactics: Wait for the sun. Skiing it before it softens is the classic way to lose an edge and a season.

glossary.definition: 靠踝、膝、髋的弯折造出刃角，上身保持相对直立。中文教学里也说「折胯」「顶膝」，但两者指的是不同关节，本课程统一用「折角」。
整个身体向弯内侧倒，用来对抗离心力。速度高时必须有，但只靠它不够——缺了折角就成了整体内倾。
有内倾而没有折角——就是「往里倒」的毛病版本：内板被压上，刃反而抓不住。中文常说的「压肩」「整个人躺进弯里」多半指的是它。
两板从旧刃换到新刃的那一刻。同步换刃是平行式的定义性特征：不同步的换刃，本质上就是外八字。
把一只板推出一个角度来起弯或造平台。中文也叫「蹬板」「推刃」。第一层级里是合法工具，从 st-06 起就是毛病。
板头并、板尾分。最早的控速与转弯工具。口语里也叫「八字」「披萨」，对孩子讲「披萨」最好用。
以犁式起弯、在后半段把两板并成平行式的转弯。中文也叫「犁式并腿转弯」，是犁式到平行式之间唯一必经的过渡台阶。
在弯的过程中把内板收到与外板平行。中文也叫「收板」「并腿」。并得越早，弧线越干净；并得多早，就是半犁式的进度表。
两个弧线之间压力最低的一段，两板在此经过平放。与转弯阶段 tp-transition 是同一件事，只是这里当术语用。
某一点上最陡、最直接向下的那条线。中文也叫「滚落线」。它不是固定方向：坡面一转，落线也跟着转。
弧线的几何形态。圆润的 C 形控速，Z 形是刹车。整套课程里最省事的一句诊断：看雪痕是 C 还是 Z。
弧线有多紧。小回转、中回转、大回转是主动选择，不是被动结果——只会一种尺寸，说明地形在替你选。
沿雪板长度方向的平衡：偏前还是偏后。
身体质量压在双脚中部，小腿与靴舌有轻而均匀的接触。注意不是「前倾」：弯腰前倾反而会把髋推到脚后面去。
弧线外侧那只板——也就是山下侧的板，应该承担绝大部分负荷。中文常说的「主力板」「受力板」就是它。
弧线内侧那只板，也就是山上侧的板。要立上刃、要平行，但要轻——「轻」不等于「不管」。
脚的外侧刃。把新内脚倒到这一侧，就是现代转弯的起点：先有小脚趾侧刃，才有整个弯。
脚的内侧刃——转弯中外板真正咬雪的那条刃。中文也说「内刃」，但要说清是哪只板的内刃，否则一定会被误解。
负荷在两只板之间怎么分，常用 80/20 这样的比例来表达。比例随雪质变：硬雪偏外板，深雪要接近对半。
上身与腿、板朝向不同的方向。中文也叫「上下身分离」。它是一个结果，不是一个动作：腿转得动，分离自然出现。
主动把上身朝向弯的外侧，让腿能在稳定的躯干下面转动。与「分离」的差别在于主动：分离是看到的，反向是做出来的。
侧向的调整动作，在大刃角下把身体质量维持在外板上方。与「反向」不同：反向管旋转，它管侧倾。
雪板沿着刃走线、不横向打滑的转弯：板尾走过板头走过的地方。中文也直接叫 carving 或「切」；雪痕是两条细线，不是抹痕。
雪板在前进的同时也横向漏走的转弯。与侧滑的区别是：侧滑基本横着走，搓雪是一边走弧一边漏。它是一种工具，不只是毛病。
练习：只立刃、不转向，在雪面上留下两条细细的平行线。中文也叫「铁轨印」。细线是立刃，抹痕是旋转，雪痕不会说谎。
练习：整个弯里持续小幅踏步，让「站死」在物理上不可能发生。板几乎不离雪面，换刃瞬间也不许停。
在弯的开头把刃立好，然后被动地等它自己走完。看起来很稳，其实弧线后半段完全交给了地形。
练习：在横切山坡的过程中反复做半个弯，不把弯做完。
练习：把抬起的内板横过外板板头，整个弯保持这个姿势。
练习：在可控侧滑中把双板原地转过 180 度，胸口始终朝山下。陡坡技术的核心。
让雪板可控地横向下滑，并能随时叫停。全山通用的退路：任何地形，只要还能侧滑下来，就不算被困住。
练习：一边侧滑，一边斜向前后漂移。
双板同时快速转体加立刃止住的停法，两个方向都要会。只会一侧，等于只有一半的刹车。
沿落线做的有节奏、快速、带压刃止速的连续小回转，配阻挡式插杖。
靠屈腿解开一个弯，让雪板从身体下方穿过去。速度快、坡度陡、节奏紧时用它，因为身体不必再走一趟远路。
靠身体越过雪板来解开一个弯。在较慢的速度和较缓的坡上是正确做法。它与收腿换刃是一对选项，不是新旧关系。
用一次突然的向上伸展来卸载雪板。这是过时的时机错误，与渐进伸展不是一回事。
换刃瞬间杖篮轻触雪面，只用于计时，不承任何重量。是「点」，不是「插」——这个区别贯穿整个课程。
更实、带阻挡作用的杖动作，用来稳住上身，并在小回转和陡坡上触发解刃。
用屈腿把地形「吞」掉，让上身走一条平的轨迹。雪包技术的基础：腿在动，脑袋不动。
沿雪包沟槽直下的线：最快、最难，也是最不该拿来入门的线。绝大多数人卡在雪包上，就是因为一上来就选了它。
在雪包的上坡面上转弯。这是友好的线，控速就住在这里。
在极陡或极窄的地形上，把双板原地跳着转过来。
刻意先枢转再刻滑，用于高速下快速改变方向。竞速界对「弯起晚了」的答案。
双板分开而双膝相互靠拢——内侧那条腿倒错了方向。中文也叫「内扣」。教了几次还在，就该去找靴技师查对线。
取出内胆量鞋壳：脚趾抵住壳前端，量后跟与壳之间的间隙。目标是一根手指。买靴只有壳测算数，试穿时的舒适感不算。
固定器松开雪靴的设定值，由技师依身高、体重、靴底长度、年龄和滑行类型计算。不要自己拧：调高会不脱离，调低会误脱离，两边都伤人。
ISO 5355（高山）、GripWalk 与 ISO 9523（登山）互不通用；配错可能导致固定器无法脱离。
镜片能透过多少可见光。晴天用低值，平光、阴天用高值。
刻意把板头板尾接触点的刃磨钝一点，让板不至于自己挂住往里咬。
决定雪板咬入快慢和抓地强弱的打磨角度。底 0.5-1 度、侧 1-2 度是大众刻滑的设定。
压雪机留下的灯芯绒状纹路雪面。
窄而接近水平的横切道或作业道。中级滑雪者摔得最多的地方：速度不高，但站姿一后座就没有退路。
树干周围那圈松雪形成的空洞，从上方几乎看不出来。是窒息危险，也是「必须有同伴且保持目视」这条规则的由来。
Snow immersion suffocation，雪埋窒息——树坑与深雪致死事故背后的机制。
树距可以通行、能滑的林地。
由缆车进入、未压雪也无巡逻的地形。风险等同野雪，方便性等同雪场，且在本课程范围之外。
经典的 ACL 损伤机制：向后失去平衡，体重压在山下侧板板尾的内刃上，髋低于膝。已经在摔了就别挣扎着站起来，手臂保持在前。
NSAA 发布的十条滑雪者行为准则（2022 年版），涵盖控速、优先权、停靠、标识、缆车、状态与碰撞责任。
一趟只练一件事，而且出发前先把它说出声。同时改三件事，等于一件都没改。

snow_conditions.description: 刚压过的雪面，带一条条灯芯绒似的纹路。
snow_conditions.name: 压雪纹
snow_conditions.tactics: 学立刃最好的雪面，也是能从自己雪痕里得到诚实反馈的雪面：回头看一眼，是细线还是抹痕，答案就在雪上。要早去，热门雪道上大约只能维持两小时。

snow_conditions.description: 被人流压实、但仍然软得容易咬住刃的雪。
snow_conditions.name: 压实粉雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 宽容、抓得住。本课程大多数练习默认的就是这种雪。

snow_conditions.description: 密实、坚硬、低温的雪，还能咬住刃，但会惩罚立刃太晚或太突然。
snow_conditions.name: 硬雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 刃要渐进地立、并且在落线以上就立好。这时候刃锋利不再是可选项。

snow_conditions.description: 再冻、被刮净或被雨结壳的雪面，几乎没有可抓的东西。
snow_conditions.name: 冰面／镜面
snow_conditions.tactics: 降低刃角、把平衡做好，胜过一味加大刃角。走雪道两侧，那里还有雪。不要在这种雪上学新东西，只用它检验旧东西：在冰面上还成立的技术，才是真的会了。

snow_conditions.description: 密度很低的新雪，多见于内陆型气候或高海拔。
snow_conditions.name: 轻粉雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 需要速度才能浮起来，也需要更均匀的双脚平台。弯要更圆、更有耐心。

snow_conditions.description: 含水量高、密度大的新雪。
snow_conditions.name: 重粉雪／海洋型粉雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 阻力大、还会抓板头。板要更宽、速度要更快、刃要比直觉少立一些。

snow_conditions.description: 被滑乱、切碎、高低不平的雪，每个弯的阻力都不一样。
snow_conditions.name: 乱雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 两脚当一个平台，用腿去吸收，上身保持安静。最常见的野雪状况，也是练得最少的一种。

snow_conditions.description: 软雪之上盖着一层硬壳，时而托住人、时而塌下去。
snow_conditions.name: 易碎壳雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 滑雪里最难的常见雪况。两脚当成一个平台，弯更圆、速度更慢，并且要有「换个地方滑」的觉悟。

snow_conditions.description: 太阳辐射在表面形成的一层薄而发亮的壳，下面往往还是软雪。
snow_conditions.name: 日晒壳雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 认出来之后其实很好预测：坡向和时间就能告诉你它在哪里。

snow_conditions.description: 被风搬运、压实过的雪，密度和支撑力会突然改变。
snow_conditions.name: 风板雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 在场内它是技术问题，出了场界就是雪崩问题。阻力会毫无预告地变化，做好准备。

snow_conditions.description: 春季松散的圆颗粒雪，整个上午会按规律逐渐变软。
snow_conditions.name: 玉米雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 在一个很窄的时间窗里非常好滑。跟着太阳绕山走：先东坡，最后西坡。

snow_conditions.description: 暖天后段又湿又重、含水饱和的雪。
snow_conditions.name: 深烂雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 抓板、耗体力；板头一被抓住就是真实的受伤风险。要比你想收工的时间更早收工。

snow_conditions.description: 昨天的烂雪冻成硬块，表面全是车辙般的坑洼。
snow_conditions.name: 春季再冻雪
snow_conditions.tactics: 等太阳。软之前就下去滑，是丢掉一次刃、也丢掉一个雪季的经典方式。

hard_rules: Never leave the scene of a collision. Stop, give assistance, exchange contact details, and report it to a ski area employee.
The uphill skier has the duty to avoid. There is no argument that transfers it downhill.
en.heading: FIS rules of conduct, and collision duties

hard_rules: Do not stop below a blind crest, a roll, or a narrow trail exit.
Look uphill and yield before entering a trail or starting downhill, every time.
Never ski directly above a stopped group. Name a regroup point instead.
en.heading: Right of way, stopping and merging in practice

hard_rules: Never move an injured skier, and never remove their helmet.
Always mark the scene uphill before anything else.
en.heading: If someone is hurt

hard_rules: Report a missing child immediately and say 'lost child' to a ski area employee. Do not spend fifteen minutes looking first.
One adult stays stationary and reachable by phone throughout.
en.heading: Lost-child protocol

hard_rules: Worsening symptoms, confusion, unsteady walking or breathlessness at rest mean descend now and seek medical care.
A child who turns uncharacteristically irritable, refuses food and sleeps badly at altitude is assessed for AMS, not told to keep skiing.
en.heading: Altitude, sun, cold and hydration

hard_rules: Never ski deep snow, glades or trees alone. Solo is the factor common to most snow immersion fatalities.
One at a time, in visual contact, watching your partner's whole descent.
If a partner does not arrive, return to where you last saw them and call patrol.
en.heading: Tree wells and snow immersion suffocation

hard_rules: 绝不要离开碰撞现场。停下、提供救助、交换联系方式，并向雪场员工报告。
山上方的滑雪者负有避让义务。没有任何理由能把这项义务推给山下方的人。
zh.heading: FIS 行为规则与碰撞后的义务

hard_rules: 不要停在盲坡沿、坡度变化处或狭窄雪道出口的下方。
进入一条雪道或起滑向下之前，每一次都要向山上看并让行。
绝不要在停下的一组人正上方滑行。改为约定一个集合点。
zh.heading: 优先权、停靠与汇入的实际做法

hard_rules: 绝不要移动受伤的滑雪者，也绝不要取下他的头盔。
先在上方标示现场，再做其他任何事。
zh.heading: 有人受伤时

hard_rules: 孩子失联要立刻报告，并对雪场员工说出「孩子走失（lost child）」。不要先自己找十五分钟。
全程要有一个成人固定在原地、手机随时接得到。
zh.heading: 孩子走失处置流程

hard_rules: 症状加重、意识混乱、走路不稳或静息时呼吸困难，意味着立即下降海拔并就医。
在高海拔变得异常烦躁、拒食、睡不安稳的孩子，要按急性高山病来评估，而不是被要求继续滑。
zh.heading: 海拔、日照、低温与补水

hard_rules: 绝不要独自滑深雪、林间雪道或树林。单独行动是多数雪埋窒息死亡事故的共同因素。
一次一个人，保持目视，看完同伴的整趟下滑。
同伴没有到达，就回到你最后看见他的地方，并呼叫巡逻队。
zh.heading: 树坑与雪埋窒息

adjustments: The day is play on the flat: slide to a target, step over a pole, ski through a gate of gloves.
Test two things: does the child stop where told, and get up alone.

criteria_modifications.change: Replace the push test with an observation that hands stay forward and eyes stay up; a 30-second static hold is not testable at this age.

do_not: Do not ski the child between your legs or holding their hands. It teaches nothing and removes both parties' ability to bail out.
equipment_notes: Boots must fit this season, not next. Oversized boots make the day physically impossible.

adjustments: Lighter, shorter skis and a boot bendable while cold change today's outcome more than any cue.
Two short sessions rather than one long one; volume costs balance and adds nothing.

criteria_modifications.change: Standing window extended to 60 seconds, count reduced to 2 falls per side. The gate is not skipped: recovery matters more here, not less.

adjustments: Fit the boot first: calf volume and a narrow heel often leave a rental cuff tight at the top and loose at the ankle, and heel lift destroys the shin contact ac-01-01 tests.
For a lighter skier a shorter, softer ski is an upgrade, not a concession.

criteria_modifications.change: Standard unchanged. Where low mass keeps the wedge from braking, shorten the ski rather than widen the stopping window.

adjustments: Give the escape route before asking for commitment: dr-01-07 precedes the first straight run.
Never say it is easy. Ask the two real questions: is the run-out safe, and would a fall here be serious?

en.core_question: Can I stand, glide and stop in this equipment?

drills.name: Flex ladder in boots
drills.purpose: Calibrates shin contact at both ends of its range.
drills.setup: Boots buckled to skiing tension, skis off, flat snow.
steps: Stand tall until the shins leave the tongues, then flex until they push back.
Settle halfway, light and even on both shins, 30 seconds.
Repeat with eyes closed, with skis on, then gliding.
drills.success_indicator: The same light even contact found twice running, eyes closed.

drills.name: One-ski scooter
drills.purpose: Builds balance on one gliding ski before two-footed coordination.
drills.setup: One ski on, one boot free, near-flat snow.
steps: Push off with the free boot and glide, hands forward.
Ride each push out before adding another.
Swap sides and match the count.
drills.success_indicator: Ten pushes per side, no windmilling, no looking down.

drills.name: Step in, step out, on the pitch
drills.purpose: Makes binding entry on a slope automatic before the first fall.
drills.setup: Across the fall line on a 4-6 degree pitch.
steps: Lay both skis across the slope, downhill one below; clear both soles.
Clip in the downhill ski, stand on it, then the uphill one.
Release the uphill ski first, holding it so it cannot run.
drills.success_indicator: Both skis on, from standing, under 45 seconds.

drills.name: Side-step and herringbone ladder
drills.purpose: Trains edge awareness while climbing: the cheapest edging lesson there is.
steps: Facing across a 5-8 degree pitch, roll both ankles in, step up ten steps.
Turn uphill and climb ten herringbone steps, tips out, on the inside edges.
Side-step back down the same track.
drills.success_indicator: Ten side-steps with no slip, no crossed tails in the herringbone.

drills.name: Straight run to a target
drills.purpose: Proves that flat parallel skis go straight and stop themselves.
drills.setup: Shallow pitch, long run-out, glove 15 metres past the bottom.
steps: Point both skis down the fall line and let them run.
Hold the dr-01-01 stance all the way and coast to a stop.
Repeat until the skis stop in the same place twice running.
drills.success_indicator: Eight runs, hands in view, no steering, spacing unchanged.

drills.name: Wedge on command
drills.purpose: Makes the wedge an adjustable brake, not a panic position.
drills.setup: Same pitch, glove two thirds down.
steps: Straight run to the glove, then push both tails out to a stop.
Next run, hold a narrow wedge from the top and feel the difference.
Alternate wide and narrow, naming which one before you start.
drills.success_indicator: Both tails move out together and both inside edges bite at once.

drills.name: Fall, slide, reassemble, stand
drills.purpose: Makes the first fall a decision rather than an accident.
drills.setup: Soft snow, shallow pitch, nobody above.
steps: From a slow glide, sit down sideways and downhill, arms forward.
Bring both skis below the body and across the slope, then stand over the downhill ski.
Repeat on the other side, and once with the uphill ski off.
drills.success_indicator: Standing again inside 30 seconds, unaided, either side.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ask the skier to lift their toes while gliding. Shins already off the tongues confirms it.

cues: Shins touching all the way down.
Move with the skis, not behind them.
fix.equipment_check: Shell gap, flex rating and buckle tension produce this identically.

faults.looks_like: A chair-sitting shape, flat skis running away underneath, arms trailing.
faults.name: Sitting back
root_causes: Fear of the fall line, expressed as pulling away from it.
Boots that will not flex, or buckled too tight to close.
faults.symptom: Hips behind the heels within metres of any slide; burning quads.

faults.diagnosis_test: Have the skier stand and touch their knees. If that is also their skiing shape, the fold is at the waist.

cues: Close the ankle, not the waist.
Stand tall and press the shins.
fix.equipment_check: A softer flex, or a heel shim where ankle mobility is the limit.

faults.looks_like: Head low, hips back, tail-heavy skis, an ankle that never moves.
faults.name: Bending at the waist
root_causes: 'Lean forward' taken literally.
Ankle mobility too limited to close the boot, so the waist substitutes.
faults.symptom: The skier folds at the hips, reaching for the tongues with the chest.

faults.diagnosis_test: Read the tracks: a working wedge scrapes two edge lines, a flat one leaves smooth bands.

cues: Push the tails out, not the knees in.
Stand on the inside edge of each foot.

faults.looks_like: Tails wide, knees rolled together, both skis riding on their bases.
faults.name: Flat-ski wedge
root_causes: Knees pointed in instead of the tails pushed out.
Boots too large, so the ankle cannot transmit edge pressure.
faults.symptom: A wide wedge that does not slow the skier down at all.

faults.diagnosis_test: Build a wedge from a standstill. One tail moving first or further confirms it.

cues: Both tails, same time, same distance.
Even pressure under both arches.

faults.looks_like: An asymmetric wedge, one nearly straight ski, the body twisted.
faults.name: One-legged wedge
root_causes: One dominant leg working, the other passive.
Weight parked on the strong ski, so the weak one cannot steer.
faults.symptom: Only one tail is pushed out, so the skier drifts and stops crookedly.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ask for a deliberate sideways sit-down (dr-01-07). A skier who cannot do it on purpose will not under pressure.

cues: If you are going down, go down.
Arms forward, sit sideways.
fix.equipment_check: Release values set for current weight; non-release does the damage in slow twisting falls.

faults.looks_like: Arms thrown back, body rotating, one ski loaded on its inside edge behind the hips.
faults.name: Fighting the fall
root_causes: An untrained recovery reflex on a surface it does not suit.
Never having fallen on purpose, so falling is unrehearsed.
faults.symptom: The skier keeps trying to stay up after the fall is decided, and lands twisted.

faults.diagnosis_test: Measure the tip gap in the skier's normal wedge. Under a hand's width crosses under load.

cues: A hand's width between the tips.
Widen the tails, not the tips.
fix.equipment_check: Ski length: chin height or below for a first-timer.

faults.looks_like: A wedge pinched almost shut at the front, one tip over the other.
faults.name: Crossed tips
root_causes: Wedge width copied from a demonstration, never felt.
Skis too long, narrowing the tip gap at any wedge angle.
faults.symptom: The tips touch or override and the skier is pitched forward.

en.goal: Stand in balance in ski boots, move around a learning area unaided, glide straight, and stop in a wedge.
en.one_line: Equipment that works, a stance that works, and a slide that ends where you meant it to end.
safety_notes: A helmet certified to ASTM F2040 or EN 1077, no gap between goggle and brow. Equipment without a technician-set release value is today's largest avoidable risk.
Flat ground below a slope is a collision zone, not a rest area.

cues: Both shins touching, the same amount.
Look where you are going, not at your skis.
skills.description: Feet hip-width, both shins resting lightly and evenly on the tongues, hips over mid-foot, hands in view.
misconceptions: That 'lean forward' produces it. Leaning bends the waist and pushes the hips back; closing the ankle brings the hips over the feet.
skills.name: Athletic stance with shin contact
skills.why: Every later stage measures fore/aft balance against this. A skier who never felt it has nothing to return to under pressure.

cues: Downhill ski first, then stand on it.
Kick the snow off before you step in.
skills.description: Across the fall line, clip in the downhill ski, stand on it, then the uphill ski. Reverse to come out.
skills.name: Bindings on a slope, downhill ski first
skills.why: A ski clipped on above the skier slides away and takes the morning with it; on a real pitch it endangers people below.

cues: Set the uphill edges, then step.
Tips out, tails close, push off the inside edges.
skills.description: Sliding forward on the flat, climbing sideways on the uphill edges, climbing tips-out in a herringbone.
skills.name: Moving under your own power
skills.why: How a skier retrieves a dropped ski or escapes a flat spot. Without it, later stages need rescuing.

cues: Let it run and stand still.
Hands in view, eyes on the bottom.
skills.description: Both skis flat and parallel down a shallow pitch, gliding to a natural stop: no steering, no braking, no looking down.
skills.name: The straight run
skills.why: The baseline every later fore/aft error is measured against. Skiers who skip it never stop bracing, and bracing is the back seat.

cues: Push the tails out, keep the tips apart.
Squeeze slowly; do not stamp.
skills.description: Both tails pushed out, both inside edges biting evenly, tips a hand's width apart, so speed drops progressively.
misconceptions: That the wedge is made by pointing the knees together. Knees in flattens the skis and removes the braking edges.
skills.name: The gliding wedge
skills.why: The first speed control the skier owns. st-02 turns its width into a speed dial; learned as a rigid position it will not open into a turn.

cues: If you are going down, go down.
Skis below you and across the hill, then stand.
skills.description: Down sideways and downhill, arms forward, no recovery mid-slide; then skis below the body and across the slope.
skills.name: Falling safely and getting up
skills.why: The classic knee injury is a slow twisting backward fall the skier fights. Getting up unaided makes later stages practicable alone.

tactics: Ski the first 90 minutes with no technical goal. Cold hands, bad boots and altitude are the real obstacles.
Stop at the edge of the learning area, never below a roll.
End one run early. The last run of a first day produces most of a first day's injuries.

avoid: Any pitch where the skis run away before a wedge exists.
A run-out ending at a lift line, fence or road.
terrain.ideal_description: Thirty metres of flat ground, then a 3-6 degree slope 40 metres wide with a long uphill run-out, served by a conveyor.

en.why_it_matters: Nothing later recovers cheaply from a bad first day. A back-seat stance learned today is still on video at st-06, and today's equipment decisions decide what later stages can reach.

adjustments: 这一天在平地上玩：滑到一个目标、跨过一根杖、从两只手套的门里穿过去。
只考两件事：叫停的时候停不停得住，摔了能不能自己起来。

criteria_modifications.change: 把推一下的测试换成观察：手一直在前吗，眼睛一直抬着吗。静态保持在这个年龄测不出来。

do_not: 不要把孩子夹在两腿之间滑，也不要牵着手滑。教不了东西，还让双方都无法脱身。
equipment_notes: 雪靴要合今年的脚，不是明年的脚。靴子过大，这一天物理上就无法完成。

adjustments: 更轻更短的板，加上冷天也压得动的靴子，比任何口令都更影响今天的结果。
两个短时段，不要一个长时段；量会吃掉平衡，什么都换不回来。

criteria_modifications.change: 起身时间放宽到一分钟，每侧减到两次。这一关不跳过：恢复能力在这个年龄更重要。

adjustments: 先解决靴子适配：小腿围大加后跟偏窄，常让租来的靴筒上口紧、踝部松，而后跟一提起来就没有贴靴感觉。
对体重较轻的人，更短更软的板是升级，不是妥协。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。若因体重偏轻犁式刹不住，要换更短的板，不是放宽停止窗口。

adjustments: 先给退路，再要求投入：dr-01-07 排在第一次直滑降之前。
永远不要说「这很简单」。要问那两个真问题：出口安全吗？在这里摔一下严重吗？

zh.core_question: 穿着这套装备，我站得住、滑得动、停得下来吗？

drills.name: 压靴阶梯
drills.purpose: 在活动范围的两端校准小腿与靴舌的接触。
drills.setup: 搭扣扣到滑行的紧度，不穿板，站平地。
steps: 站直到小腿离开靴舌，再压到靴舌顶回来。
停在中间，两条小腿轻而均匀，保持 30 秒。
闭眼再做一次，再穿板做，最后滑起来做。
drills.success_indicator: 连续两次找到同样轻、同样均匀的接触，闭着眼也行。

drills.name: 单脚滑步
drills.purpose: 在两脚协调之前，先建立单板滑行的平衡。
drills.setup: 只穿一只板，另一只脚只穿靴，近乎平地。
steps: 用空着的脚蹬出去滑行，双手在前。
每一蹬滑到快停了再蹬下一次。
换边，做同样的次数。
drills.success_indicator: 每侧 10 蹬，手不乱划，不看板。

drills.name: 坡上穿脱板
drills.purpose: 在第一次摔倒之前，把坡上进固定器练成自动。
drills.setup: 在 4–6 度的坡上横对落线。
steps: 两只板横放坡上，下坡那只在下方；两只靴底都清干净。
扣下坡板，站上去，再扣上坡板。
先脱上坡板，手一直握着别让它跑。
drills.success_indicator: 从站着开始，两只板都穿好，45 秒以内。

drills.name: 横步与人字步上坡阶梯
drills.purpose: 在上坡里练立刃意识：最便宜的一堂立刃课。
steps: 横对 5–8 度的坡，两只踝往山里倒，往上迈 10 步。
转成面朝山上，板头外张踩内刃，人字步 10 步。
沿同一条痕迹横步下来。
drills.success_indicator: 10 步横步不打滑，人字步里板尾不交叉。

drills.name: 直滑降到指定点
drills.purpose: 证明放平的平行雪板走直线，也会自己停下来。
drills.setup: 缓坡、长出口，坡底往前 15 米放一只手套。
steps: 两板对准落线，让它自己滑。
全程保持 dr-01-01 的站姿，滑到自然停住。
重复到连续两次停在同一位置。
drills.success_indicator: 8 趟，手在视野里，不转向，两板间距不变。

drills.name: 口令犁式
drills.purpose: 把犁式变成可调的刹车，不是应急姿势。
drills.setup: 同一段坡，手套放在三分之二处。
steps: 直滑降到手套，两个板尾一起推出去，停住。
下一趟从顶上就保持窄犁式，体会区别。
宽窄交替，出发前先报出这趟做哪一个。
drills.success_indicator: 两个板尾一起出去，两侧内刃同时咬住。

drills.name: 摔、滑、收板、站起
drills.purpose: 让第一次摔倒是一个决定，不是一次事故。
drills.setup: 软雪、缓坡、上方没人。
steps: 从慢速滑行中往侧面、往山下坐，手臂在前。
把板收到身体下方、横对山坡，再站到下坡板上。
换另一侧做一次，再脱掉上坡板做一次。
drills.success_indicator: 两侧都能在 30 秒内自己站起来。

faults.diagnosis_test: 让他在滑行中把脚趾往上勾。小腿早就离开靴舌，就是它。

cues: 从上到下，小腿一直贴着。
跟着板走，不要落在板后面。
fix.equipment_check: 壳测间隙、硬度和搭扣紧度，做出来的样子一模一样。

faults.looks_like: 像坐椅子的形状，板放平在身下往前跑，手臂拖在后面。
faults.name: 后座
root_causes: 怕落线，表现为往后躲。
靴子压不动，或者搭扣紧到踝根本收不了。
faults.symptom: 只要开始滑，几米之内髋就落到脚跟后面；大腿灼烧。

faults.diagnosis_test: 让他站着摸膝盖。如果那也是他滑雪的形状，折点就在腰。

cues: 收踝，不是弯腰。
站高一点，把小腿压出去。
fix.equipment_check: 换软一档的硬度；踝背屈是硬限制时，加后跟垫片。

faults.looks_like: 头低、髋后、板尾吃重，踝关节整段不动。
faults.name: 从腰上折
root_causes: 把「前倾」听成了字面意思。
踝背屈不够，压不动靴子，只好用腰代替。
faults.symptom: 人在髋关节处对折，用胸口去找靴舌。

faults.diagnosis_test: 看雪痕：有效的犁式刮出两条刃痕，平板犁式留下两条光滑带子。

cues: 推板尾，别扣膝盖。
站在每只脚的内侧刃上。

faults.looks_like: 板尾张得很开，两个膝盖并在一起，两只板都骑在板底上。
faults.name: 平板犁式
root_causes: 膝盖往里扣，而不是把板尾推出去。
靴子过大，踝关节传不出立刃的力。
faults.symptom: 犁式开得很宽，却一点也不减速。

faults.diagnosis_test: 站着不动做一个犁式。哪个板尾先动、动得更多，就是它。

cues: 两个板尾，同时出去，出去一样多。
两只脚足弓下面的压力一样。

faults.looks_like: 不对称的犁式，一只板几乎是直的，身体是拧着的。
faults.name: 单腿犁式
root_causes: 一条优势腿在干活，另一条是被动的。
体重压死在强的那只板上，弱的那只没法转向。
faults.symptom: 只有一个板尾被推出去，人一边漂一边歪着停下来。

faults.diagnosis_test: 让他故意往侧面坐下去（dr-01-07）。故意都做不出来，情急之下更做不出来。

cues: 要倒就倒下去。
手臂在前，往侧面坐。
fix.equipment_check: 脱离值按当前体重设定；缓慢扭转摔倒里，是不脱离造成伤害。

faults.looks_like: 手臂往后甩，身体在转，一只板在髋后方吃着内刃。
faults.name: 挣扎着不摔
root_causes: 没练过的救回反射，用在不适合它的表面上。
从来没有故意摔过，摔倒这件事没有排练过。
faults.symptom: 摔已经定了还在硬撑，最后拧着落地。

faults.diagnosis_test: 量一下他平时犁式的板头间距。不到一掌宽，一吃力就会交叉。

cues: 板头之间留一掌宽。
把板尾张开，不是把板头收拢。
fix.equipment_check: 板长：初学者选下巴高度或者更短。

faults.looks_like: 犁式前端几乎捏死，一个板头压在另一个上面。
faults.name: 板头交叉
root_causes: 犁式宽度是照着示范抄来的，从来没有自己体会过。
板太长，任何犁式角度下板头间距都会变窄。
faults.symptom: 两个板头碰上或者叠起来，人被向前掀出去。

zh.goal: 穿着雪靴站得住，在教学区里能自己走动，能直滑降，能用犁式停住。
zh.one_line: 装备对，站姿对，滑出去以后停在你打算停的地方。
safety_notes: 头盔要符合 ASTM F2040 或 EN 1077，雪镜与额头不留缝。没有技师设定脱离值的装备，是今天最大的可避免风险。
坡底那片平地是碰撞区，不是休息区。

cues: 两条小腿都贴住，力道一样。
看你要去的地方，别看板。
skills.description: 两脚与髋同宽，两条小腿轻而均匀地搭在靴舌上，髋在脚掌中部上方，双手在视野里。
misconceptions: 以为「前倾」能做出它。前倾会弯腰、把髋推到后面；要做的是收踝。
skills.name: 运动站姿与小腿贴靴舌
skills.why: 后面每一级的前后平衡都以这个站姿为尺子。没体会过它的人，一有压力就没处可退。

cues: 先下坡板，扣完先站上去。
踩掉靴底的雪再进固定器。
skills.description: 横对落线，先扣下坡板并站上去，再扣上坡板。脱板顺序相反。
skills.name: 在坡上穿板，先穿下坡板
skills.why: 扣在身体上方的那只板会自己溜走，把一上午带走；在真坡上还危及下方的人。

cues: 先把山上侧刃立住，再迈步。
板头外张，板尾靠近，蹬内刃。
skills.description: 平地上蹬滑前进，用山上侧刃横步上坡，板头外张做人字步上坡。
skills.name: 靠自己移动
skills.why: 掉了一只板怎么捡回来、卡在平地怎么脱身，全靠它。没有它后面每一级都要人来救。

cues: 让它自己滑，你站着别动。
手在视野里，眼睛看坡底。
skills.description: 两板放平、保持平行，沿缓坡滑到自己停：不转向、不刹车、不看板。
skills.name: 直滑降
skills.why: 后面所有前后平衡的错误都以它为基线。跳过它的人一直「顶」着滑，顶着就是后座。

cues: 推板尾，板头别合上。
慢慢挤，不要跺。
skills.description: 两个板尾同时推出，两侧内刃均匀咬住雪面，板头留一掌宽，速度一点点降下来。
misconceptions: 以为犁式是靠两个膝盖并进去做的。膝盖内扣会把板放平，刹车要用的刃就没了。
skills.name: 滑行犁式
skills.why: 第一件真正属于自己的控速工具。st-02 会把它的宽度变成速度旋钮。

cues: 要倒就倒下去。
板放到身体下方、横对山坡，再站。
skills.description: 往侧面、往山下坐下去，手臂在前，滑动中不挣扎；停住后把板收到身体下方、横对山坡。
skills.name: 安全地摔和自己起来
skills.why: 典型的膝伤是一次缓慢的向后扭转摔倒，人还在硬撑。能自己起来，后面才可能一个人练。

tactics: 前 90 分钟不设技术目标。手冷、靴子不对、海拔，才是真正的障碍。
停在教学区边上，永远不要停在坡坎下方。
少滑一趟收工。第一天的伤，大多出在最后一趟。

avoid: 坡度大到犁式还没成形、雪板就跑掉的地方。
出口尽头是缆车排队区、围栏或马路的雪道。
terrain.ideal_description: 30 米平地，接一段 3–6 度、40 米宽的缓坡，出口是长长的上坡缓冲，坡下有魔毯。

zh.why_it_matters: 第一天留下的东西，后面每一级都要花大代价才还得回来；今天的装备也决定后面走得到哪一级。

adjustments: Children reach green terrain long before they own the stop. Terrain confidence is not evidence of a pass.
Use targets rather than distances: stop at the sign, between the gloves, before I count three.

criteria_modifications.change: Replace the timed descents with a slow-race on the same section: the slow run must take a third longer.

do_not: Do not coach out the wide stance; correct the back seat instead.
Do not add poles because the terrain got bigger.

adjustments: Thigh burn here is usually a static wedge, not weak legs. Fix the width variation before adding strength work.
Spread the stopping volume; 40 stops in one afternoon degrades the pattern.

criteria_modifications.change: May be split into morning and afternoon blocks. Counts unchanged.

adjustments: Greater mass and leg strength make a wide braking wedge work longer than it should, hiding ft-02-02 until st-03.
Insist on the narrow-wedge glide and the video check for ac-02-03; strength passes eyes and fails gates.
A ski too soft for the skier's mass folds under a braking wedge and washes out, mimicking a technique fault exactly.
Stopping distance scales with mass. Keep the 5-metre standard; build it on a shallower pitch rather than relaxing it.
equipment_notes: Release values set by a technician; pre-release destroys confidence faster than any fall.

en.core_question: Can I stop where I choose, every time?

drills.name: Wedge width ladder
drills.purpose: Turns wedge width into a continuous variable, not two settings.
drills.setup: A consistent green pitch, timed between two fixed lines.
steps: Descend in the narrowest wedge you can control; note the time.
Descend again at medium width, then maximum, timing each.
Then cycle narrow-medium-wide every ten seconds down one run.
drills.success_indicator: Three clearly different times, and smooth speed change in the cycling run.

drills.name: Stop on the call
drills.purpose: Removes the delay between deciding to stop and stopping.
steps: A partner below calls 'stop'; stop fully within 5 metres of every call.
Mix early and late calls, so fatigue is included.
Solo: pick a feature beforehand and stop level with it.
drills.success_indicator: Eight stops inside 5 metres, no sit-back, no sideways drift.

drills.name: Thigh-turn wedge
drills.purpose: Isolates leg steering by forbidding a width change.
drills.setup: Medium wedge, hands on the thighs to feel them rotate.
steps: In a gliding wedge, rotate both thighs about 30 degrees, then back.
The wedge must be exactly as wide at the end as the start.
Alternate directions across the run, calling each out.
drills.success_indicator: Direction changes with width unchanged and both feet turning together.

drills.name: Traverse and hold
drills.purpose: Trains edge hold and downhill-ski balance without a turn.
drills.setup: Edge of a green run, skis across the hill, parallel.
steps: Traverse the full width in a straight line, tips a few degrees downhill.
Stop, step around, traverse back on the other edges.
Then traverse in a wedge, to feel the flat uphill ski contribute nothing.
drills.success_indicator: A straight track with no downhill drift, both directions.

drills.name: Stop-and-go descent
drills.purpose: Makes each stop a chosen place rather than a rescue.
drills.setup: Pick five features before starting: a sign, a seam, a tree.
steps: Ski to each in turn and stop level with it, at the side.
Look uphill before every restart.
Repeat until the legs know the volume.
drills.success_indicator: Twenty stops, all within a ski length of the chosen feature.

drills.name: Pull out and rejoin
drills.purpose: Makes leaving and rejoining traffic a rehearsed sequence.
drills.setup: A green run with a clear edge and no fence.
steps: From mid-run, traverse to the side and stop above a rise, facing across.
Look uphill, wait for a gap, rejoin without crossing the middle.
Repeat at four points down the run.
drills.success_indicator: Every stop at the edge and visible, every restart after an uphill look.

drills.name: Surface lift rehearsal
drills.purpose: Rehearses the loading sequence, which is where the falls happen.
drills.setup: Watch three riders load, then rehearse standing still.
steps: Skis straight in the track, hands free, eyes up the line.
Take the pull at the hips, knees soft, standing tall.
If you fall, roll clear of the track and get up outside it.
drills.success_indicator: Five consecutive rides standing, no sit-back, track never blocked.

faults.diagnosis_test: Time two descents, narrowest and widest. Under two seconds apart means one wedge.

cues: Wider to slow, narrower to go.
Change size every few seconds.

faults.looks_like: A fixed A-shape held from top to bottom, whole body braced.
faults.name: One-width wedge
root_causes: The wedge learned as a position, not a brake.
Fear of narrowing it, because narrow means faster.
faults.symptom: The wedge is the same size at every speed and pitch.

faults.diagnosis_test: Thigh-turn wedge (dr-02-03) at fixed width. If the width will not hold, the turn is a push.

cues: Turn the thigh bones, keep the wedge the same size.
Steer, do not push.

faults.looks_like: An asymmetric wedge growing through each change, snow spraying off one tail.
faults.name: Tail-push steering
root_causes: Steering not yet coming from the femurs.
Speed above comfort, so every turn doubles as a brake.
faults.symptom: Direction changes by shoving one tail out; the wedge widens each turn.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ski with hands flat on the thighs. If the direction change vanishes, the shoulders were doing it.

cues: Point both feet, not your shoulders.
Eyes on where you want to arrive.

faults.looks_like: Shoulders and arms swinging ahead of the skis, chest across the hill.
faults.name: Shoulder-led direction change
root_causes: Legs not yet rotating independently at this speed.
Looking at the skis rather than at the target.
faults.symptom: The skier twists the torso to change direction; the skis follow late.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ask for a ten-second narrow-wedge glide. Refusal or instant widening confirms it.

cues: Glide, brake, glide.
Stop and rest instead of braking the whole way.

faults.looks_like: Maximum wedge held continuously, body static, snow off both tails.
faults.name: Permanent braking wedge
root_causes: Terrain above the skier's speed tolerance.
No trust that a stop is available on demand.
faults.symptom: The whole descent is one long brake; the thighs give out early.

faults.diagnosis_test: Watch the hips over the first ten metres. Behind the boots confirms it.

cues: Let it pull you; do not sit down.
Stand tall, knees soft.

faults.looks_like: Hips behind the heels, weight hanging on the lift, skis wandering.
faults.name: Sitting down on the surface lift
root_causes: Treating the lift as a seat, not a tow.
Taking the pull with the arms instead of standing against it.
faults.symptom: The skier sits back onto the bar and is pulled off balance or off the track.

faults.diagnosis_test: Look uphill from where you stopped. If you cannot see 50 metres, they cannot see you.

cues: Off to the side, above the roll.
Stop where you can see uphill.

faults.looks_like: A stationary skier mid-piste with traffic funnelling around them.
faults.name: Stopping in the blind spot
root_causes: Stopping when the legs give out, not at a chosen place.
No habit of reading a run for sightlines.
faults.symptom: The skier stops mid-run, or just below a roll where nobody above can see them.

en.goal: Control speed with wedge width on green terrain, stop on command inside a set distance, hold a traverse, ride a surface lift.
en.one_line: Speed becomes a dial rather than a switch, and the stop happens where you decided it would.
safety_notes: Right of way belongs to the skier below. Stopping where you are visible from above is the mechanism, not the etiquette. See mod-safety.
A fall on a surface lift blocks the track: roll clear, then stand up outside it.

cues: Wider to slow, narrower to go.
Change the width, not your whole body.
skills.description: Width changed continuously through a descent, wider to slow and narrower to run, tips never closer than a hand's width.
misconceptions: That wider is always safer. Past a point the tails skid flat, braking stops improving, and the knees take the load.
skills.name: Wedge width as a speed dial
skills.why: Speed control must be adjustable before it can be replaced. At st-03 the same dial becomes turn shape; one fixed width converts to nothing.

cues: Tails out and squeeze until you are still.
Shins on the tongues as you slow.
skills.description: From a moving descent, a full stop inside a named distance: tails out, edges progressively engaged, hips over the feet throughout.
skills.name: The wedge stop on command
skills.why: Everything from here is taught on shared terrain. Without an on-command stop nobody can give this skier permission to go faster.

cues: Turn the thigh bones, keep the wedge the same size.
Point both feet, not your shoulders.
skills.description: Direction changed by rotating both thigh bones in the hip sockets, wedge width constant, so the skis pivot rather than get pushed.
misconceptions: That the wedge turns because one ski is pushed out. A wider wedge brakes; it does not steer.
skills.name: Steering the wedge from the femurs
skills.why: The single skill st-03 is built from. Pushing tails or twisting the torso caps a skier at the wedge, because neither scales to parallel skiing.

cues: Stand on the downhill ski and hold the line.
Uphill edges gripping, tips slightly downhill.
skills.description: Skis held across the hill on their uphill edges, a straight line at a chosen angle, body stacked over the downhill ski.
skills.name: The traverse
skills.why: How a skier crosses to the side of a run, escapes a crowd, and later learns the st-04 sideslip. Without it the only exit is a turn.

cues: Off to the side, above the roll.
Look uphill before you move.
skills.description: Stopping at the side of a run, above a rise rather than below it, with an uphill look before restarting.
skills.name: Stopping where you are visible
skills.why: Right of way belongs to the skier below. This habit is what keeps a slow learner from being hit, and it must be automatic before speeds rise.
