cues: Let it pull you; do not sit down.
Skis straight in the track, eyes up.
skills.description: Skis straight up the track, knees soft, standing tall, taking the pull at the hips instead of sitting into it.
skills.name: Riding a surface lift
skills.why: Surface lifts serve most beginner terrain, and a fall blocks the track for everyone behind. Chairlifts arrive at st-03 on this habit.

tactics: Read the run from the lift: where it steepens, narrows, merges.
Ski the edges of a green run; the traffic and the ice are both in the middle.
Plan the stop before the descent, not when the legs complain.

avoid: Narrow green cat tracks, where a wedge cannot be widened.
Green runs with a steep pitch change hidden over a roll.
terrain.ideal_description: A wide green run of 6-12 degrees, 30 metres across, consistent pitch, clear run-out, served by a surface lift. Moderate traffic, no narrow sections.

en.why_it_matters: A skier who can stop anywhere can be taught anything. On-command speed control is what makes st-03 possible without fear, and what separates a learner from a hazard on a shared run.

adjustments: 孩子到得了绿道地形，远早于他拥有制动。地形自信不是通过的证据。
用目标代替距离：停在牌子那里、停在两只手套之间、数到三之前停住。

criteria_modifications.change: 把计时下降换成同一段路的「慢速比赛」：慢的那趟必须多花三分之一时间。

do_not: 不要把宽站姿教掉；要纠正的是后座。
不要因为地形变大了就加雪杖。

adjustments: 这一级的大腿灼烧通常是静止不变的犁式，不是腿没力。先解决宽度变化，再谈加力量。
把制动的量摊开；一个下午做几十次停车只会练坏动作。

criteria_modifications.change: 可拆成上午和下午两段。次数不变。

adjustments: 体重和腿部力量更大，会让宽的刹车犁式撑得比它该撑的更久，把 ft-02-02 藏到 st-03。
ac-02-03 的窄犁式滑行和录像检查不能省；力量过肉眼，过不了关卡。
对这个体重太软的板，在刹车犁式下会被压塌、失控外滑，症状和技术毛病一样。
制动距离随体重变长。ac-02-02 的距离标准不动；换更缓的坡建立它，不放宽标准。
equipment_notes: 脱离值由技师设定；误脱离摧毁信心比任何摔倒都快。

zh.core_question: 我能不能每一次都停在自己选的地方？

drills.name: 犁式宽度阶梯
drills.purpose: 把犁式宽度变成连续变量，不是两个档位。
drills.setup: 一段坡度均匀的绿道，在两条固定线之间计时。
steps: 用你能控住的最窄犁式滑下来，记时间。
再用中等宽度滑一趟，再最大宽度，各自计时。
然后一趟里每十秒循环一次窄—中—宽。
drills.success_indicator: 三个明显不同的时间，循环那趟速度变化平滑。

drills.name: 喊停就停
drills.purpose: 把「决定停」和「停住」之间的延迟去掉。
steps: 下方的同伴喊「停」；每次都在 5 米内完全停住。
早喊晚喊混着来，把疲劳也算进去。
一个人练：先选好参照物，停在与它齐平的位置。
drills.success_indicator: 八次都在 5 米内停住，不后座，不侧向漂。

drills.name: 大腿转向犁式
drills.purpose: 用「不许改宽度」这条规矩把腿部转向隔出来。
drills.setup: 中等犁式，双手放在大腿上感受它们转动。
steps: 在滑行犁式里把两条大腿转过约 30 度，再转回来。
结束时犁式的宽度必须和开始时一模一样。
在雪道上左右交替，每次先报出方向。
drills.success_indicator: 方向变了，宽度没变，两只脚一起转。

drills.name: 横切并保持
drills.purpose: 在没有转弯的情况下练持刃和下坡板平衡。
drills.setup: 绿道边缘，雪板横对山坡，两板平行。
steps: 用一条直线横切整个道宽，板头比横向再朝下几度。
停住，转身，换另一侧刃横切回来。
然后用犁式横切一次，体会放平的山上侧板没贡献。
drills.success_indicator: 两个方向的雪痕都是直的，没有往山下漂。

drills.name: 停停走走式下降
drills.purpose: 让每次停都是选好的地方，不是抢救。
drills.setup: 出发前先选五个参照物：一块牌子、一条压雪缝、一棵树。
steps: 依次滑到每一个，停在与它齐平的位置，靠边停。
每次起步前都往山上看。
重复到两条腿记住这个量。
drills.success_indicator: 二十次停车，都落在选定参照物一个板长内。

drills.name: 撤到边上再汇入
drills.purpose: 把离开人流和汇回人流练成排练过的流程。
drills.setup: 一条边缘干净、没有围栏的绿道。
steps: 从半坡横切到边上，停在一个坡坎上方，横对雪道。
往山上看，等一个空档，不穿越雪道中间就汇回去。
在这条道上找四个点各做一次。
drills.success_indicator: 每次都停在边上、上方看得见；起步前都往山上看过。

drills.name: 牵引缆车预演
drills.purpose: 预演上车流程，摔倒都发生在那里。
drills.setup: 先看三个人上车，然后站着不动排练一遍。
steps: 板在轨道里走直，手空出来，眼睛看着上方的线。
用髋去接那股拉力，膝盖放松，人站高。
真摔了就滚出轨道，在轨道外面站起来。
drills.success_indicator: 连续五趟都站着坐完，不后座，没堵过轨道。

faults.diagnosis_test: 计时两趟，最窄和最宽。差不到两秒就只有一个犁式。

cues: 开宽就慢，收窄就走。
每几秒钟就改一次大小。

faults.looks_like: 一个固定的 A 形从上撑到下，全身绷着。
faults.name: 只有一个宽度的犁式
root_causes: 犁式是当姿势学的，不是当刹车学的。
不敢收窄，因为窄就意味着更快。
faults.symptom: 任何速度、任何坡度，犁式都是同一个大小。

faults.diagnosis_test: 定宽做大腿转向犁式（dr-02-03）。宽度保不住就是推出来的。

cues: 转大腿骨，犁式大小不变。
转过去，不要推出去。

faults.looks_like: 不对称的犁式，每次变向都在长大，一个板尾喷雪。
faults.name: 推板尾式转向
root_causes: 转向还没有从大腿骨来。
速度超出舒适区，每个转弯都兼职当刹车。
faults.symptom: 靠把一个板尾杵出去改变方向；每转一次就变宽。

faults.diagnosis_test: 双手平放在大腿上滑。方向变化消失了，就是肩膀在做。

cues: 用两只脚指方向，不是用肩膀。
眼睛看你想到达的地方。

faults.looks_like: 肩膀和手臂跑在板前面，胸口横对山坡。
faults.name: 肩膀带头改变方向
root_causes: 这个速度下，腿还不能独立转动。
眼睛盯着雪板，不是盯着目标。
faults.symptom: 用拧躯干改变方向；雪板跟得很晚。

faults.diagnosis_test: 要他用窄犁式滑十秒。不肯或立刻变宽，就是它。

cues: 滑、刹、滑。
停下来休息，不要一路刹到底。

faults.looks_like: 最大犁式一路撑着，身体僵住，两个板尾都喷雪。
faults.name: 一直刹着的犁式
root_causes: 地形超出他的速度容忍度。
不相信随时都能停下来。
faults.symptom: 整段下降就是一次长长的刹车；大腿很早就塌。

faults.diagnosis_test: 看头十米里髋的位置。在靴子后面就是它。

cues: 让它拉着你走，不要坐下去。
站高，膝盖放松。

faults.looks_like: 髋在脚跟后面，体重挂在缆车上，板到处乱走。
faults.name: 在牵引缆车上坐下去
root_causes: 把缆车当椅子，不当拖曳。
用手臂去接拉力，不是站着顶住它。
faults.symptom: 人往后坐到杆子上，被拉得失衡或拉出轨道。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从你停的位置往山上看。看不到 50 米，别人也看不到你。

cues: 靠边停，停在坡坎上面。
停在你能看到山上的地方。

faults.looks_like: 一个不动的人站在雪道中间，人流从两边绕。
faults.name: 停在盲区里
root_causes: 腿撑不住了才停，不是停在选好的地方。
没有读雪道视线的习惯。
faults.symptom: 停在雪道中间，或刚好停在坡坎下面，上方看不见。

zh.goal: 在绿道上用犁式宽度控速，听到口令能在距离内停住，能保持横切线，能坐牵引式缆车。
zh.one_line: 速度从开关变成旋钮，停车停在你决定的位置。
safety_notes: 优先权属于下方的滑雪者。停在上方看得见处是机制，不是礼貌。见 mod-safety。
在牵引缆车上摔倒会堵住整条轨道：先滚出去，再在轨道外站起来。

cues: 开宽就慢，收窄就走。
改宽度，不要动整个身体。
skills.description: 整段下降里连续改变宽度，要慢就开宽，要走就收窄，板头不小于一掌宽。
misconceptions: 以为越宽越安全。过了某个点板尾会平着搓出去，刹车不再变好，负荷上膝盖。
skills.name: 把犁式宽度当速度旋钮
skills.why: 控速工具要先可调，才可能被替换掉。到 st-03 它变成弧线形状。

cues: 板尾出去，挤到人不动为止。
减速的时候小腿贴住靴舌。
skills.description: 从滑行中在指定距离内完全停住：板尾推出，刃逐渐吃住，髋在脚上方。
skills.name: 口令下的犁式制动
skills.why: 从这里往后都在共用雪道上教。没有随叫随停，没人能允许他更快。

cues: 转大腿骨，犁式大小不变。
用两只脚指方向，不是用肩膀。
skills.description: 靠两根大腿骨在髋窝里转动改变方向，宽度不变；板是被转过去的，不是被推出去的。
misconceptions: 以为犁式是因为一只板被推出去才转的。开宽是刹车，不是转向。
skills.name: 用大腿骨转动犁式
skills.why: st-03 就是从这一项技术长出来的。推板尾或拧躯干会把人永久封在犁式里，长不到平行式。

cues: 站在下坡板上，把这条线走住。
山上侧刃咬住，板头略微朝下。
skills.description: 雪板横对山坡吃住山上侧刃，按选定角度走一条直线，身体叠在下坡板上。
skills.name: 横切
skills.why: 横到雪道边上、从人群里脱身，以及 st-04 的侧滑，都从它来。没有它只能靠转弯。

cues: 靠边停，停在坡坎上面。
起步前先往上看。
skills.description: 停在雪道侧边、坡坎上方而非下方，起步前先往山上看。
skills.name: 停在别人看得见的地方
skills.why: 优先权属于下方的滑雪者。这个习惯就是让慢学员不被撞的机制，必须尽早自动化。

cues: 让它拉着你走，不要坐下去。
板在轨道里走直，眼睛往上看。
skills.description: 板对着轨道走直，膝盖放松，人站高，用髋接那股拉力，不是坐进去。
skills.name: 乘坐牵引式缆车
skills.why: 初学地形多半靠牵引式缆车。一次摔倒会堵住整条轨道。到 st-03 坐吊椅靠同一个习惯。

tactics: 从缆车上读这条道：哪里变陡、变窄、汇流。
滑绿道的两边；人流和冰都在中间。
下降前先计划好在哪里停，别等腿抗议。

avoid: 窄的绿色猫道：犁式在那里没法开宽。
坡坎后面藏着陡段的绿道。
terrain.ideal_description: 一条 6–12 度、宽 30 米的绿道，坡度均匀，出口干净，坡下有牵引式缆车。人流中等，不变窄。

zh.why_it_matters: 能随处停住的人，什么都教得会。随叫随停的控速，是 st-03 不带恐惧进行的前提。

adjustments: The stage this band lives in, taught as games: ski around the gloves, make an S and look back at it.
Assess two things: turns both ways on request, and stopping where told. The counted gates mean nothing at this age.

criteria_modifications.change: Replace 15 counted turns with following a leader for a full run; a child cannot count and ski at once.

do_not: Do not add poles.
Do not measure the day in runs or vertical.
equipment_notes: Edge connectors only for a child who physically cannot hold a wedge, removed as soon as they can.

adjustments: Track inspection and video persuade this band; adult opinion does not.
A wide stance is correct at this age. Correct the back seat, not the width.
do_not: Do not plant gates or objects on a public run.
Do not compare children in the group out loud.

adjustments: Spread the 2:1 weak-side work across sessions; repetitions after fatigue train the compensation instead.
Hip mobility, not strength, is the usual limiter here. Test it off snow before adding cues.

criteria_modifications.change: The 3 runs may be split across two blocks. Counts unchanged.

adjustments: Outside-ski loading appears here, and with it the inward-tracking knee. Angulation cues beat 'lean in more'; a persistent A-frame is a fitting question.
For a lighter skier a shorter, softer ski makes ac-03-02 reachable; an unbendable ski holds no arc.

criteria_modifications.change: Standard unchanged. Where low mass prevents the ski bending, change the ski, not the gate.

en.core_question: Can I steer both legs together and link turns without stopping?

drills.name: J-turns
drills.purpose: Trains one complete turn at a time, finished across the hill.
drills.setup: Pointed down the fall line on a shallow green, space below.
steps: Straight run in a narrow wedge, then steer both legs one way to a stop.
The track should read as a J: straight, rounding, then across the hill.
Walk back, repeat the other way, inspect both tracks.
drills.success_indicator: A rounded J ending across the slope, the skis stopping themselves.

drills.name: Fan progression
drills.purpose: Introduces the fall line in increments rather than all at once.
drills.setup: From a traverse, one direction at a time.
steps: Turn from a shallow traverse, so the skis barely cross the fall line.
Each repetition starts steeper, ending in the fall line.
Back off a step the moment the wedge widens.
drills.success_indicator: The steepest start angle that is still steered is known.

drills.name: Wedge garlands
drills.purpose: Repeats the turn start many times without committing to the fall line.
drills.setup: Traverse at a shallow angle in a gliding wedge.
steps: Steer both legs until the skis point slightly downhill.
Steer back to the traverse without completing the turn.
Repeat 8 times, then switch direction.
drills.success_indicator: Eight identical initiations, wedge width unchanged.

drills.name: Inside-ski feather
drills.purpose: Proves the outside ski carries the load by taking the inside one out.
drills.setup: Linked wedge turns, easier side first.
steps: Once the arc is established, take all pressure off the inside ski.
Slide that ski forward and back mid-turn to prove it is unloaded.
Then lift it 2 cm and see whether the arc changes.
drills.success_indicator: Turn shape unchanged when the inside ski is unloaded or lifted.

drills.name: Corridor turns with a count
drills.purpose: Builds rhythm and forces speed control by shape.
drills.setup: An 8-metre corridor down the fall line, groomer seams as edges.
steps: Ski 15 linked turns inside it, counting each aloud.
The wedge stays one width; only the arc changes.
Leaving the corridor or stopping restarts the count.
drills.success_indicator: 15 counted turns, even tempo, steady speed, inside the corridor.

drills.name: Two-to-one weak side sets
drills.purpose: Closes the left-right gap by spending practice where it is needed.
drills.setup: Identify the weaker side from tracks or video, not from feel.
steps: Sets of three: two weak-side turns, one strong.
Compare the tracks for radius and roundness.
Finish with even turns and check whether the gap narrowed.
drills.success_indicator: Both directions leave similar radii.

drills.name: Fixed-width descent
drills.purpose: Removes wedge width as a speed control, leaving only shape.
drills.setup: A green with one pitch change and a clear run-out.
steps: Set a narrow wedge at the top and never change it.
Control speed only by carrying each arc further across.
Any widening or check ends the attempt.
drills.success_indicator: A whole descent at steady speed, wedge unchanged, arcs rounder where it steepens.

faults.diagnosis_test: Wedge garlands (dr-03-03) at fixed width. If the width will not hold, it is a push.

cues: Steer the wedge round; do not push it wider.
Both feet turn together.

faults.looks_like: A wedge pulsing wider at each initiation, snow off the outside tail.
faults.name: Turning by widening the wedge
root_causes: Steering not yet coming from both femurs.
The turn used as a brake because speed is above comfort.
faults.symptom: Each turn starts by pushing a tail out, so the wedge grows.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ski with both hands flat on the thighs. If the turn vanishes, the shoulders made it.

cues: Turn your feet, not your shoulders.
Eyes on where you want to arrive.

faults.looks_like: Chest and arms leading, then a skidded second half.
faults.name: Shoulder-led turn
root_causes: Legs not rotating independently at this speed.
Late initiation, so the fastest-moving body part starts the turn.
faults.symptom: The turn starts with a shoulder swing and runs out of steering.

faults.diagnosis_test: Inside-ski feather (dr-03-04). If the arc straightens when it is unloaded, this is it.

cues: Stand on the downhill ski through the turn.
Little foot light, big foot loaded.

faults.looks_like: Hips inside the turn, uphill ski flat and loaded, outside ski skidding.
faults.name: Weight on the inside ski
root_causes: Body leaning in instead of standing on the outside ski.
Inside leg not shortening, so it takes load.
faults.symptom: The turn will not hold and the skier is pulled to the inside.

faults.diagnosis_test: Read the track: sharp tops and smeared bottoms mean an abandoned arc.

cues: Keep steering until the skis face across the hill.
Draw a C, not a Z.

faults.looks_like: A Z-shaped track with corners instead of arcs.
faults.name: Unfinished turns
root_causes: Steering stops once the direction has changed.
Fear of pointing across the hill toward the trees.
faults.symptom: Each turn is released at the fall line, so speed builds.

faults.diagnosis_test: Inspect 10 turns of track and compare left and right radius.

cues: Two on the bad side for every one on the good.
Same shape both ways.

faults.looks_like: Two different track shapes, and a drift toward the weak side.
faults.name: One-sided turning
root_causes: A dominant leg steering while the other follows.
Practice split evenly, which preserves the gap.
faults.symptom: Turns one way are round; the other becomes a traverse.

faults.diagnosis_test: Count turns aloud. A broken count means the rhythm is not there.

cues: Count out loud: one turn per count.
Finish this turn into the next one.

faults.looks_like: Turn, traverse, stop, turn: a staircase rather than a rhythm.
faults.name: Stopping between turns
root_causes: Each turn negotiated as a separate decision.
Speed control by pause instead of by shape.
faults.symptom: Every turn is followed by a traverse or pause.

en.goal: Link continuous wedge turns down a green run, steering both legs together, speed governed by turn shape rather than wedge width.
en.one_line: Both legs steer together, the outside ski takes the load, and turn shape starts doing the braking.
safety_notes: Chairlifts arrive here: bar down, packs off before loading, nothing retrieved mid-ride. See mod-lifts.
Linked turns cross the whole width of a run, so the uphill check is now compulsory rather than polite.

cues: Both feet turn together, same speed.
Steer the wedge round; do not push it wider.
skills.description: Both femurs rotating the same direction at the same rate, so the wedge pivots as one shape and neither ski leads.
misconceptions: That the inside ski is passive. It steers as hard as the outside ski, and simply carries less load.
skills.name: Simultaneous steering of both legs
skills.why: The st-06 parallel turn is this movement without the wedge. Turns made by pushing one ski must be dismantled later, which is why intermediates plateau.

cues: Stand on the downhill ski through the turn.
Little foot light, big foot loaded.
skills.description: Load moving progressively onto the outside ski as the arc develops, so it bends and grips while the inside ski stays light.
misconceptions: That weighting the outside ski means leaning over it. The load goes into it while the body stays upright.
skills.name: Pressure to the outside ski
skills.why: Only the outside ski holds a platform to steer from. Every stage from st-05 measures it; a skier balanced between both has nothing to steer against.

cues: To slow down, turn further; do not push harder.
Draw a C, not a Z.
skills.description: Speed regulated by how far each arc is carried across the hill, wedge width held constant throughout.
misconceptions: That slowing down means turning less. Less turn means more fall line, which means more speed.
skills.name: Turn shape as the brake
skills.why: Braking has a ceiling and shape does not. A skier who controls speed by width can never ski anything steeper than their legs are strong.

cues: Keep steering until the skis face across the hill.
Finish this turn before you start the next.
skills.description: Steering continued past the fall line until the skis point across the slope, not released at the direction change.
skills.name: Finishing the turn across the hill
skills.why: An unfinished turn arrives at the next one too fast, forcing a brake. Every later speed problem, steeps included, is an arc abandoned early.

cues: Count out loud: one turn per count.
No stopping between turns.
skills.description: One turn flowing into the next with no traverse, pause or check, at a tempo the skier chooses.
skills.name: Linking turns with rhythm
skills.why: Rhythm makes a turn a pattern rather than a decision. Without it each turn is negotiated separately, and st-06 pole timing has nothing to attach to.

cues: Two on the bad side for every one on the good.
Name your weak side out loud before the run.
skills.description: The weaker direction trained at twice the volume, until shape and radius match both ways.
skills.name: Working the weaker side
skills.why: Every skier is asymmetric here, and the gap widens each stage unless worked. Most one-sided intermediate faults were born at st-03.

tactics: One cue per run, said aloud before pushing off.
Inspect your tracks every third run; snow is a more honest coach than memory.
Ski the weak side while the legs are fresh, not last.

avoid: Narrow runs, where turn shape cannot be widened to control speed.
Flat run-outs mid-run, which kill the rhythm being built.
terrain.ideal_description: A wide green of 8-15 degrees, 30 metres across, long enough for 15 turns without stopping, served by a slow chair.

en.why_it_matters: Here the idea the curriculum rests on first appears: speed comes from shape, not braking. Every later stage refines that trade; skiers who never make it brake their way up the mountain and stall.

adjustments: 这一档就活在这一级，教法是游戏：绕着手套滑、画个 S 再回头看。
只考两件事：往两边转都转得出来，叫停就停在那里。数出来的关卡在这个年龄没意义。

criteria_modifications.change: 把数转弯换成跟着一个人滑完整趟；孩子没法边数边滑。

do_not: 不要加雪杖。
不要用趟数或落差来衡量这一天。
equipment_notes: 板头连接器只给撑不住犁式的孩子，能撑住就拆。

adjustments: 看雪痕和看录像能说服这一档；大人的评语不行。
这个年龄宽站姿是对的。要纠正的是后座，不是宽度。
do_not: 不要在公共雪道上插旗门或摆放物体。
不要在小组里当众把孩子们互相比较。

adjustments: 二比一的弱侧练习要摊到多次上雪；疲劳后的重复练的是代偿。
这一级的限制常是髋部灵活度，不是力量。加口令前先在陆地上测。

criteria_modifications.change: 那几趟可以拆到两个时段里。次数不变。

adjustments: 压外板从这一级出现，膝盖内扣跟着来。折角口令比「再多倒一点」有效；A 形腿教不掉就是适配问题。
对体重较轻的人，更短更软的板让 ac-03-02 可达；压不弯就刻不出弧。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。体重偏轻压不弯板，换板，不改关卡。

zh.core_question: 我能不能两条腿一起转，不停下来把弯连起来？

drills.name: J 形转弯
drills.purpose: 一次只练一个完整的、收到横对山坡的弯。
drills.setup: 在缓绿道上对准落线，下方留出空间。
steps: 用窄犁式直滑降，再两条腿一起往一侧转到停住。
雪痕应该读成一个 J：先直，转圆，最后横对山坡。
走回去，换另一侧做一次，两条雪痕都看一遍。
drills.success_indicator: 一个圆润的 J，收在横对山坡的方向，板自己停。

drills.name: 扇形进阶
drills.purpose: 把落线一点一点引进来，不是一次全给。
drills.setup: 从横切出发，一次只做一个方向。
steps: 从很浅的横切起转，让板刚好越过落线一点。
每次重复都从更陡的角度开始，最后从落线开始。
犁式一变宽，立刻退回上一档。
drills.success_indicator: 知道自己「还转得住」的最陡起始角度。

drills.name: 犁式花环
drills.purpose: 在不投入落线的前提下，把起弯重复很多次。
drills.setup: 以浅角度在滑行犁式里横切。
steps: 两条腿一起转，转到板头略微朝下。
不完成转弯，转回横切。
重复 8 次，然后换方向。
drills.success_indicator: 八次一模一样的起弯，犁式宽度不变。

drills.name: 内板羽化
drills.purpose: 把内板拿掉，证明外板在承担负荷。
drills.setup: 连续的犁式转弯，先从容易的一侧开始。
steps: 弧线建立后，把内板上的压力全部卸掉。
在弯中把那只板前后滑动，证明它是空的。
然后把它抬起 2 厘米，看弧线会不会变。
drills.success_indicator: 内板卸载或抬起时，弧线形状不变。

drills.name: 带数数的走廊转弯
drills.purpose: 建立节奏，并逼出形状控速。
drills.setup: 沿落线画一条 8 米宽的走廊，压雪缝当边界。
steps: 在里面做 15 个连续转弯，每个都数出声。
犁式保持一个宽度；变的只有弧线。
出了走廊或停下来，数字从头开始。
drills.success_indicator: 15 个数出来的转弯，节奏均匀，速度稳定，都在走廊。

drills.name: 弱侧二比一组合
drills.purpose: 把练习花在需要的地方，缩小左右差距。
drills.setup: 用雪痕或录像找出弱侧，别靠感觉。
steps: 三个一组：两个弱侧转弯，一个强侧。
比较两边雪痕的半径和圆度。
最后用左右均匀的转弯收尾，看差距缩小没有。
drills.success_indicator: 两个方向留下的半径接近。

drills.name: 定宽下降
drills.purpose: 把犁式宽度这个控速手段拿掉，只留形状。
drills.setup: 一条带一处坡度变化、出口干净的绿道。
steps: 在顶上定好一个窄犁式，全程不改。
只靠把每条弧线带得更横来控速。
任何一次变宽或压刃放速，这趟作废。
drills.success_indicator: 整趟速度稳定，犁式没变，坡陡处弧线更圆。

faults.diagnosis_test: 定宽做犁式花环（dr-03-03）。宽度保不住就是在推。

cues: 把犁式转圆，不要把它推宽。
两只脚一起转。

faults.looks_like: 犁式在每次起弯时鼓一下变宽，外侧板尾喷雪。
faults.name: 靠把犁式开宽来转弯
root_causes: 转向还没有从两根大腿骨来。
速度超出舒适区，转弯被当成刹车用。
faults.symptom: 每个转弯都从杵出一个板尾开始，犁式于是长大。

faults.diagnosis_test: 双手平放在大腿上滑。转弯消失了就是肩膀做的。

cues: 转脚，不转肩。
眼睛看你想到达的地方。

faults.looks_like: 胸口和手臂领先，后半个弯是搓出来的。
faults.name: 肩膀带头的转弯
root_causes: 这个速度下，腿还不能独立转动。
起弯太晚，只好由移动最快的部位来起弯。
faults.symptom: 用甩肩膀起弯，转弯的余量就用完。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做内板羽化（dr-03-04）。一卸掉内板弧线就被拉直。

cues: 整个转弯都站在下坡那只板上。
小脚轻，大脚重。

faults.looks_like: 髋在弯内，山上侧板放平吃重，外板在搓雪。
faults.name: 重心压在内板上
root_causes: 身体往里倒，而不是站在外板上。
内腿没有收短，于是吃上了负荷。
faults.symptom: 转弯抓不住，人被拉进弯里。

faults.diagnosis_test: 读雪痕：顶上尖、底下糊，就是被放弃的弧线。

cues: 一直转到板横对山坡。
画 C，不要画 Z。

faults.looks_like: 一条 Z 形雪痕，有拐角，没有弧线。
faults.name: 没做完的转弯
root_causes: 方向一变过来，转向就停了。
不敢把板指向横切、朝着树的方向。
faults.symptom: 每个弯在落线上就松掉，速度累积。

faults.diagnosis_test: 看 10 个转弯的雪痕，比较左右半径。

cues: 坏的一侧做两个，好的一侧做一个。
两边同一个形状。

faults.looks_like: 两种不同的雪痕形状，人还往弱侧漂。
faults.name: 只会往一边转
root_causes: 一条优势腿在转，另一条跟着走。
练习量左右平分，差距被原样保留。
faults.symptom: 一个方向的弯是圆的，另一个变成横切。

faults.diagnosis_test: 把转弯数出声。数字断掉就是节奏不在。

cues: 数出声：一个数一个弯。
把这个弯收进下一个弯里。

faults.looks_like: 转、横切、停、转：楼梯，不是节奏。
faults.name: 转弯之间要停一下
root_causes: 每个弯都被当成一个单独的决定。
用停顿控速，而不是用形状。
faults.symptom: 每个转弯后都跟着一段横切或一次停顿。

zh.goal: 在绿道上把犁式转弯连起来，两条腿一起转，速度由弧线形状而不是宽度决定。
zh.one_line: 两条腿一起转，外板吃住负荷，形状开始接过刹车。
safety_notes: 吊椅从这一级开始：护栏放下，背包上车前取下，掉的东西不捡。见 mod-lifts。
连续转弯会横跨整条雪道，往山上看现在是义务，不是客气。

cues: 两只脚一起转，速度一样。
把犁式转圆，不要把它推宽。
skills.description: 两根大腿骨同方向、同速率转动，犁式作为整体被转过去，没有板领先。
misconceptions: 以为内板是被动的。它转得和外板一样用力，只是负荷少。
skills.name: 两条腿同步转向
skills.why: st-06 的平行式转弯就是这个动作去掉犁式。靠推板做出来的转弯以后必须拆掉。

cues: 整个转弯都站在下坡那只板上。
小脚轻，大脚重。
skills.description: 随着弧线展开，负荷渐进移到外板上，让它压弯、咬住，内板保持轻。
misconceptions: 以为压外板就是身体往外板上倒。负荷进到板里，身体直立。
skills.name: 把压力给到外板
skills.why: 只有外板能给出可以转向的平台。从 st-05 起每一级都在量它；平摊就没处借力。

cues: 想慢就多转一点，不要推得更狠。
画 C，不要画 Z。
skills.description: 速度由每条弧线横切山坡的程度调节，宽度全程不变。
misconceptions: 以为想慢就该少转。转得少意味着更多落线，也就更快。
skills.name: 用弧线形状当刹车
skills.why: 刹车有上限，形状没有。用宽度控速的人，滑不了比腿力更陡的地形。

cues: 一直转到板横对山坡。
把这个弯做完，再开下一个。
skills.description: 过了落线继续转，一直转到板横对山坡，不是方向刚变就松掉。
skills.name: 把转弯做完到横对山坡
skills.why: 没做完的转弯会以过快的速度进入下一个，逼你去刹。后面的速度问题都是提前放弃的弧线。

cues: 数出声：一个数一个弯。
两个弯之间不许停。
skills.description: 一个弯流进下一个弯，中间没有横切、停顿、压刃放速，节奏自己定。
skills.name: 有节奏地把转弯连起来
skills.why: 有节奏，转弯才是模式，不是决定。没有它 st-06 的点杖时机也无处可挂。

cues: 坏的一侧做两个，好的一侧做一个。
出发前先把你的弱侧说出来。
skills.description: 弱的那个方向用两倍的量练，直到两边形状和半径一致。
skills.name: 专门练弱侧
skills.why: 每个人在这一级都不对称，不去练差距每级都会拉大。中级的单侧毛病大多生于此。

tactics: 一趟一个口令，出发前说出声。
每三趟看一次雪痕；雪比记忆更诚实。
趁腿还新鲜练弱侧，别放到最后。

avoid: 窄道：弧线开不到足以控速的大小。
半坡上的平缓路段：会把节奏杀掉。
terrain.ideal_description: 一条 8–15 度、宽 30 米的绿道，长到能不停做 15 个转弯，坡下有慢速吊椅。

zh.why_it_matters: 整套课程赖以成立的想法在这里第一次出现：速度来自形状，不来自刹车。走不到这里的人只能刹着往上爬。

adjustments: Not developmentally meaningful: these children control speed with a wedge and with terrain, and cannot grade an edge release.
Teach the outcome instead — stop where I stop. The sideslip arrives at 7 or 8 with nothing lost.
Frame it as a target game: slide to the glove, stop on the line. The movement transfers; the vocabulary does not.
A light child's skis may not slide sideways on soft snow; find firmer snow rather than coaching harder.

criteria_modifications.change: Two stopping distances, long and short: fine gradation needs mass they do not have.

adjustments: The highest-value stage in the progression here: it turns an unexpected pitch from a fall into an inconvenience.
Volume down, quality up; ankle mobility work before the session changes what is available.

criteria_modifications.change: Run-in of 15 m rather than 20-25 m, stopping tolerance unchanged.

adjustments: Solve heel hold first: heel lift makes the forward drift of the falling leaf unavailable, whatever the cue.
Where the knee tracks inward under load, the uphill-edge release comes late on one side; cue the hip out and downhill.
Teach this earlier than the classic sequence suggests: an adult who can stop from anywhere will attempt what they would otherwise refuse.
Name the fear precisely — is the run-out safe, and would a fall here be serious?

en.core_question: Can I release, slide, and re-grip on demand — my escape route from anywhere?

drills.name: Slide and grip on the spot
drills.purpose: Isolates the edge release: no speed, no direction change.
drills.setup: Across the fall line on 15-20 degrees, uphill edges gripping.
steps: Flatten both ankles until the skis drift, counting out loud: one, two, three.
Roll knees and ankles back toward the hill until the drift stops.
Repeat without turning the skis: five cycles each way.
drills.success_indicator: Slide starts and stops on your count; the skis never pivot.

drills.name: Stop-on-command sideslip
drills.purpose: Puts the stop on someone else's timing.
drills.setup: A partner below and to the side calls 'slide' and 'stop' unpredictably.
steps: Start and stop on the call, without watching your partner.
Every stop complete inside two ski lengths.
Vary intervals: some slides half a second, some five.
drills.success_indicator: Every stop lands within two ski lengths, both directions.

drills.name: Falling leaf
drills.purpose: Trains fore/aft control inside a slide, with no turning to hide behind.
drills.setup: A wide 15-20 degree pitch and an imaginary 3 m corridor.
steps: Sideslip, then press both shins into the tongues; the skis drift diagonally forward.
Ease back to mid-foot; the drift reverses and the skis travel backward.
Reverse six times inside the corridor, then face the other way.
drills.success_indicator: The skis zigzag down the hill while still pointing across it.

drills.name: Three stopping distances
drills.purpose: Makes the stopping distance the target, not the stop.
drills.setup: Three references below the start: roughly 5 m, 2 m, half a metre.
steps: Stop at the 5 m mark using the slowest edge build you can manage.
Repeat to 2 m, then half a metre, adding edge faster each time.
Run the ladder both directions; note which end you cannot reach.
drills.success_indicator: All three distances hit within a ski length, on purpose.

drills.name: Hockey stops to a line
drills.purpose: Makes the stop accountable to a place, and exposes the weak side.
drills.setup: A visible line across the run, clear space above and below.
steps: Straight run in, pivot both feet across, build edge, boots on the line.
Chest keeps facing downhill: the feet swing, the shoulders do not.
Five stops each direction; move the start uphill once both sides match.
drills.success_indicator: Both directions stop within a ski length and throw the same snow.

drills.name: Uphill turn to a stop
drills.purpose: Proves speed can be removed by direction change alone.
drills.setup: A traverse with open space above you.
steps: Steer both skis gradually up the hill; hold the steering until you stop.
No edge set, no tail push; if you braked, the turn started late.
Both directions, stopping shorter by steering further, not harder.
drills.success_indicator: A complete stop facing uphill with no spray of snow.

drills.name: Unfamiliar-pitch protocol
drills.purpose: Makes new terrain a procedure rather than an act of courage.
drills.setup: A run one grade above comfort, quiet, partner in sight.
steps: Enter from the side in a traverse; do not point the skis downhill.
Sideslip 5 m, stop, and note what the snow did on release.
Only then turn, finishing uphill; repeat every 10-15 turns.
drills.success_indicator: You can say what the snow does on release before committing.

faults.diagnosis_test: Have someone push you gently downhill at the hip. If the skis slide at once, the fault is stance.

cues: Hips downhill, over the skis.
Stand on the downhill ski, then flatten.

faults.looks_like: Knees pressed into the slope, skis high on edge, shoulders tipped uphill.
faults.name: Locked uphill edge
root_causes: Mass over the uphill ski, still loading the edge that should release.
Release attempted at the ankles while the hips lean into the hill.
faults.symptom: The skier stands across the hill and nothing happens; the skis refuse to slide.

faults.diagnosis_test: Sideslip and try to lift the uphill ski. If you cannot, your mass is on the wrong ski.

cues: Downhill hand forward and low.
Belly button over the downhill boot.

faults.name: Leaning into the hill
root_causes: The instinct to move away from the drop, which is backwards on skis.
Inclination with no angulation: the body tips instead of the joints bending.
faults.symptom: Head and shoulders tip toward the slope; the downhill ski unweights and catches.

faults.diagnosis_test: Look back: a sideslip leaves a sideways band, a pivot leaves an arc.

cues: Skis keep pointing across the hill.
Flatten, don't twist.

faults.name: Pivoting instead of sliding
root_causes: Upper-body rotation supplying the release instead of the ankles.
Uneven flattening, so one ski lets go before the other.
faults.symptom: Every release becomes a turn: the tips dive toward the fall line and speed builds.

faults.diagnosis_test: Three stopping distances (dr-04-04): if 5 m and half a metre take the same distance, this is it.

cues: Squeeze the edge on over three counts.
Name the distance before you go.

faults.name: One edging speed
root_causes: Edging treated as a switch rather than a range.
Stiff ankles, so edge angle comes from the whole leg at once.
faults.symptom: Every stop is abrupt: the ski grabs, the body jolts, the edge chatters.

faults.diagnosis_test: Five hockey stops per side (dr-04-05). Compare distance and snow thrown, not feel.

cues: Weak side first, every run.
Same terrain, twice the reps.

faults.looks_like: One direction pivots less, finishes lower, throws less snow.
faults.name: A one-directional skier
root_causes: Volume accumulated on the comfortable side, widening the gap every run.
A real asymmetry in hip rotation range or boot alignment.
faults.symptom: Sideslips and hockey stops work one way and are unreliable, or refused, the other.

faults.diagnosis_test: Falling leaf (dr-04-03): backward drift easy and forward drift impossible confirms an aft stance.

cues: Shins on the tongues, both of them.
Feel the whole foot.
fix.equipment_check: Shell fit and flex: a boot two sizes too big makes forward drift unreachable.

faults.name: Back seat in the slide
root_causes: A defensive retreat from the downhill side, sending the hips back instead of out.
Boots too large, or impossible to flex.
faults.symptom: The tails slide faster than the tips, and the falling leaf only travels backward.

en.goal: Release both edges on demand, sideslip a chosen distance, and stop the slide where you decide, both directions, on green and easy blue.
en.one_line: Skiing's escape route: let the edges go, slide sideways under control, re-grip where you choose.
safety_notes: This stage leaves you stationary and sideways mid-run. Look uphill before every repetition and stop where you are visible from above.
Never practise above a drop, a lift line, a snow gun or a road; pick a run-out you would happily slide.
Leaning into the hill (ft-04-02) catches the downhill ski, and that fall breaks thumbs and wrists.

cues: Flatten the ankles until it slides.
Roll the knees back up the hill.
skills.description: Roll both ankles downhill until the skis let go and drift sideways; roll back uphill to re-grip, tips still across the hill.
skills.name: Static sideslip: flatten to slide, tip to stop
skills.why: Without it there is no exit from a turn. St-09's pivot slip is this movement with the skis pivoting.

cues: Squeeze the edge on, don't slam it.
Choose the stopping distance first.
skills.description: Grip arrives on a dial, not a switch: three seconds of tipping stops the ski in five metres, an instant stops it in one.
skills.name: Progressive edging versus the edge set
skills.why: One edging speed means braking at every turn finish and no grip on firm snow.

cues: Shins on the tongues to go forward.
Ease off the tongues to drift back.
skills.description: Pressure to the tips drifts the skis forward, pressure to the tails drifts them back, without changing where they point.
skills.name: Falling leaf: fore/aft control inside the slide
skills.why: The only test of fore/aft balance with turning removed, and how a skier later traverses sideways on steeps.

cues: Chest down the hill, feet swing across.
Pivot first, then edge.
skills.description: From a straight run, pivot both skis across the fall line with the legs, chest facing downhill, then build edge to a stop.
skills.name: Hockey stop, both directions
skills.why: The emergency brake blue terrain requires, and the first leg rotation under a stable upper body.

cues: Keep steering uphill until the speed is gone.
Stand on the downhill ski.
skills.description: From a traverse, steer both skis up the hill and keep steering until gravity stops them. No push, no edge set.
skills.name: Uphill turn to a stop
skills.why: First proof that speed is spent by shape rather than friction, which is the argument of st-06.

cues: Test the exit before the entrance.
Slide it first, then ski it.
skills.description: On unfamiliar pitch: traverse in from the side, sideslip a few metres, stop, and only then turn.
skills.name: Proving the escape route before committing
skills.why: Fear of a pitch is fear of not being able to stop on it. Skip this and tier 2 is skied defensively.

tactics: Enter unfamiliar pitch from the side in a traverse, never from the top pointing downhill.
Sideslip the first metres of any run whose snow you have not felt.
Make the uphill turn, not the hockey stop, your default bail-out.
A sideslip session occupies the run rather than passing down it; pick your spot.

avoid: Soft or deep snow, where the skis will not slide sideways and the drill teaches nothing.
Narrow runs and traverses, where a slide runs out of space before it runs out of speed.
Boilerplate while learning; it belongs at the testing end of the stage, not the acquisition end.
terrain.ideal_description: A smooth, quiet pitch of 15-20 degrees, wide enough to slide 10 m sideways, with a clean flat run-out below and snow firm enough that the skis actually slide sideways. The packed edge of a cat track is not a substitute for a real pitch.

en.why_it_matters: Every turn is a bet that you can get out of it, and the sideslip pays out. Skiers who own it commit to unfamiliar pitch; skiers who do not brake and stem for years. Pivot slips and steep traverses are this skill under pressure.

adjustments: 发育上没有意义：这一档靠犁式和地形控速，也无法把解刃分出等级。
教结果就好——我停哪儿你停哪儿。侧滑七八岁再来，什么都不会少。
包装成打靶游戏：滑到手套、停在线上。动作能迁移，术语不能。
体重轻的孩子在软雪上板横不动；去找更硬的雪，别加大口令力度。

criteria_modifications.change: 只做长短两种停止距离：细分等级需要他们还没有的体重。

adjustments: 整套进阶里对这一档回报最高的一级：意外的陡坡从摔倒变成麻烦。
降量保质；上雪前先做踝灵活度，能用的东西不一样。

criteria_modifications.change: 助滑改为 15 米，不必 20–25 米；停止的容差不变。

adjustments: 先解决后跟固定：后跟一提起，落叶飘的往前漂就没了，口令补不回来。
受力时膝盖内扣的人，有一侧山上侧刃总解得晚；口令给「髋往外、往山下」。
比经典顺序更早教：从哪儿都能停下来的成年人，会去试本来会拒绝的东西。
把恐惧问准确——出口安全吗？摔一下严重吗？

zh.core_question: 解刃、侧滑、再咬住，随叫随做——我从任何地方都撤得出来吗？

drills.name: 原地一滑一咬
drills.purpose: 把解刃单独拎出来：没有速度，没有方向改变。
drills.setup: 在 15–20 度坡上横着站，山上侧刃咬住。
steps: 两踝一起放平，放到板开始漂，出声数：一、二、三。
膝和踝一起往山上滚回去，滚到漂停下。
全程不许转板；每个方向 5 个循环。
drills.success_indicator: 滑和停都落在你数的拍子上；板从不转向。

drills.name: 听口令停的侧滑
drills.purpose: 把「停」的时机交到别人手上。
drills.setup: 同伴在下方偏侧，不规律地喊「滑」和「停」。
steps: 听口令起、听口令停，不许盯着同伴看。
每次停都在 2 个板长内完成。
间隔要变：有的滑半秒，有的滑 5 秒。
drills.success_indicator: 每次都在 2 个板长内停住，两个方向都是。

drills.name: 落叶飘
drills.purpose: 在侧滑里练前后控制，没有转向可以躲。
drills.setup: 一片宽阔的 15–20 度坡，想象一条 3 米走廊。
steps: 先侧滑，再把两条小腿压进靴舌；板斜着往前漂。
松回脚掌中部；漂移反向，板往后走。
在走廊里换向 6 次，再换一个朝向。
drills.success_indicator: 板一路 Z 字下坡，朝向始终横着山坡。

drills.name: 三种停止距离
drills.purpose: 把停止距离当靶子，不是把「停住」当靶子。
drills.setup: 起点下方三个参照：约 5 米、2 米、半米。
steps: 用你能做到的最慢立刃，停在 5 米那个点上。
再停 2 米、再停半米，每次立刃更快一点。
两个方向都跑这个梯子；记下哪一端到不了。
drills.success_indicator: 三个距离都刻意打到，误差在一个板长内。

drills.name: 对线横向急停
drills.purpose: 让停止对一个地点负责，也把弱侧照出来。
drills.setup: 雪道上一条看得见的横线，上下留空。
steps: 直行进入，双脚同时转过去，立刃，靴子停在线上。
胸口一直朝山下：脚甩过去，肩不动。
每个方向 5 次；两侧一样了再把起点往上移。
drills.success_indicator: 两个方向都在一个板长内停住，甩雪一样多。

drills.name: 上山转弯停止
drills.purpose: 证明速度可以只靠改变方向就花掉。
drills.setup: 一段横切，上方留出空间。
steps: 把两板渐渐转向山上；保持转动，转到停下。
不压刃、不推板尾；刹了，就是弯起得太晚。
两个方向都做；想停更短是转更多，不是转更狠。
drills.success_indicator: 完全停住、板头朝山上，没有雪雾溅出。

drills.name: 陌生坡面流程
drills.purpose: 把新地形变成流程，而不是一次勇气。
drills.setup: 比舒适坡度高一档、人少的雪道，同伴在视线内。
steps: 从侧面横切进入；不要把板头指向山下。
侧滑 5 米，停住，记下解刃那一刻雪的反应。
然后才转弯，弯收向山上；每 10–15 个弯重复。
drills.success_indicator: 投入之前，你能说出解刃时雪的反应。

faults.diagnosis_test: 让人在髋部往山下轻推你一把。板立刻就滑，问题在站姿。

cues: 髋往山下，压到板上方。
先站到山下那只板上，再放平。

faults.looks_like: 膝盖顶进坡里，板立得很高，肩膀往山上歪。
faults.name: 山上侧刃锁死
root_causes: 体重压在山上侧板上，还压着那条本该松开的刃。
想用踝解刃，髋却倒向山里。
faults.symptom: 人横着站在坡上，什么也没发生；板拒绝滑动。

faults.diagnosis_test: 侧滑中试着抬起山上侧板。抬不起来，就是压错了板。

cues: 山下侧的手放前、放低。
肚脐压在山下侧靴子上方。

faults.name: 往山里倒
root_causes: 躲开落差的本能——在雪板上恰恰是反的。
有内倾没有折角：整个身体倒过去，关节不弯。
faults.symptom: 头和肩往坡里歪；山下侧板被卸载，然后被挂住。

faults.diagnosis_test: 回头看雪痕：侧滑留下一条横带，转板留下一段弧。

cues: 板头始终横着山坡。
放平，不要扭。

faults.name: 转板代替侧滑
root_causes: 用上身旋转解刃，而不是用踝。
两板放平不同步，一只先松开。
faults.symptom: 每次解刃都变成一个弯：板头扎向落线，速度起来了。

faults.diagnosis_test: 三种停止距离（dr-04-04）：5 米和半米停出来一样长，就是它。

cues: 用三拍把刃挤上去。
出发前先把距离说出来。

faults.name: 只有一种立刃速度
root_causes: 把立刃当开关用，不当范围用。
踝僵，刃角只能整条腿一次给完。
faults.symptom: 每次停都生硬：板一口咬住，身体一顿，刃在抖。

faults.diagnosis_test: 每侧 5 次横向急停（dr-04-05）。比停止距离和甩雪量，不比感觉。

cues: 每趟都从弱侧开始。
同样的坡，两倍的次数。

faults.looks_like: 一个方向转得少、停得更靠下、甩出的雪更少。
faults.name: 单向滑雪者
root_causes: 次数全堆在舒服那侧，每趟都把差距拉大。
髋旋转范围或靴子对线上真实的不对称。
faults.symptom: 侧滑和横向急停一侧好用，另一侧不稳，甚至不做。

faults.diagnosis_test: 落叶飘（dr-04-03）：往后漂轻松、往前漂做不到，就是后座。

cues: 两条小腿都贴住靴舌。
感觉整个脚掌。
fix.equipment_check: 壳测与硬度：大两号的靴子让往前漂做不出来。

faults.name: 侧滑里的后座
root_causes: 对山下侧的防御性退让，髋往后送而不往外送。
靴子过大，或者根本压不动。
faults.symptom: 板尾比板头滑得快，落叶飘只能往后走。

zh.goal: 绿道与缓蓝道上随叫随做：解开两侧刃、侧滑一段自定的距离、在自定的位置停住，两个方向都成立。
zh.one_line: 滑雪的退路：把刃松开，可控地横向下滑，在你选定的地方重新咬住。
safety_notes: 这一级让你横着停在道中间。每次重复前往上看，停在上方看得见处。
绝不在断崖、缆车线、造雪机或公路上方练；出口选你愿意滑下去的。
往山里倒（ft-04-02）会挂住山下侧板，那一摔专断拇指和手腕。

cues: 踝一起放平，放到它开始滑。
膝盖往山上滚回去。
skills.description: 两踝一起往山下倒，倒到板松开、横向漂走；再往山上倒回去咬住，板头始终横着坡。
skills.name: 静态侧滑：放平就走，立刃就停
skills.why: 没有它，弯就没有出口。st-09 的枢转侧滑就是它加上双板转动。

cues: 刃是挤上去的，不是砸上去的。
先定要停多远，再动。
skills.description: 抓地是旋钮，不是开关：立刃 3 秒，5 米停住；一瞬间立满，1 米就停。
skills.name: 渐进立刃，对上一记压刃
skills.why: 只有一种立刃速度，等于每个收弯都在刹车，硬雪也抓不住。

cues: 小腿贴靴舌，往前走。
松开靴舌，往后漂。
skills.description: 压向板头，板斜着往前漂；压向板尾，往后漂——朝向一点不变。
skills.name: 落叶飘：侧滑里的前后控制
skills.why: 唯一一个摘掉转向、只考前后平衡的测试；也是日后陡坡横向挪动的办法。

cues: 胸口对着山下，脚从底下甩过去。
先转，再立刃。
skills.description: 从直行开始，用腿把两板同时转过落线，胸口朝山下，再把刃立到停住。
skills.name: 两个方向的横向急停
skills.why: 蓝道要求的那把急刹，也是第一次在稳定上身下做腿部转动。

cues: 一直往山上转，转到速度没了。
站在山下那只板上。
skills.description: 从横切开始，把两板一路转向山上，转到重力把它停下。不推板，不压刃。
skills.name: 上山转弯停止
skills.why: 第一次证明速度是被形状花掉的，不是被摩擦——这正是 st-06 的论点。

cues: 先测出口，再进入口。
先滑一段，再滑它。
skills.description: 上生坡：从侧面横切进去，侧滑几米，停住，然后才转弯。
skills.name: 先验证退路，再投入
skills.why: 怕一段坡，怕的是在它上面停不住。跳过这一步，第二层级都在防御性地滑。

tactics: 上生坡从侧面横切进入，绝不从坡顶把板头指向山下。
任何一条你还没摸过雪的道，头几米先侧滑一段。
把上山转弯而不是横向急停，设成默认的撤出动作。
练侧滑是占着一段雪道，不是路过；先挑好地方。

avoid: 软雪或深雪：板横不动，练习教不了东西。
窄道与横切道：侧滑还没滑掉速度，先滑没了空间。
学的阶段避开冰面；它属于检验端，不是习得端。
terrain.ideal_description: 平整安静的 15–20 度坡面，宽到能横滑 10 米，下方有干净平缓的出口，雪硬到板真会横着走。猫道边沿代替不了一段真坡。

zh.why_it_matters: 每个弯都是一次赌注：赌你出得来。侧滑就是那份赔付——有它的人敢上生坡，没有的人刹十年车。st-09 的枢转侧滑，就是它在压力下的样子。

adjustments: Children this age commonly arrive at a wide, matched, skiddy turn by imitation, none of it taught. Let it happen; do not formalize it.
Assess two things only: stopping on request, and turning where asked.
do_not: Do not add poles because the skis are now sometimes parallel.

adjustments: Light skiers match easily and hold an edge poorly: expect ac-05-01 early and ac-05-03 a season later.
Do not coach out the wide stance that follows the match; correct the back seat instead.

criteria_modifications.change: The fore-aft slide replaces the lift entirely: a light child lifts the inside ski on balance alone, proving nothing.

adjustments: Volume down, standard unchanged: six clean christies per side beat thirty tired ones.
A shorter, softer ski bends at this skier's mass, which is what lets the inside ski be spared.

criteria_modifications.change: The 12 turns may be taken as two sets of 6 with one traverse between; the count and the one-check tolerance are unchanged.

adjustments: The A-frame (ft-05-02) is the fault to watch: a wider pelvis relative to knee spacing tends to send the inside knee inward under load.
Where it persists after coaching, treat it as alignment — cuff, canting, footbeds — not another cue.

criteria_modifications.change: None to the standard. If the outside ski will not bend enough to carry the turn, change the ski.

en.core_question: Can I free the inside ski and finish the turn with both skis parallel?

drills.name: Christie garlands
drills.purpose: Repeats the match many times without committing to the fall line.
drills.setup: A shallow traverse with a light wedge held.
steps: Wedge into a partial turn toward the fall line, match the inside ski, return to the traverse.
Eight times across the run, then switch direction.
If the wedge widens at the match, stop and restart.
drills.success_indicator: The inside ski arrives alongside quietly; the outside ski's path is unchanged.

drills.name: Feather the inside ski
drills.purpose: Proves the inside ski is light, which the skier cannot feel.
drills.setup: Quiet, gentle terrain; normal christies at low speed.
steps: In the second half of each turn, slide the inside ski a few centimetres fore and aft.
A ski carrying pressure cannot be slid; a light one can.
Once it slides freely, add a 2 cm lift for a turn.
drills.success_indicator: The inside ski slides freely and the turn shape does not change.

drills.name: Matching-point ladder
drills.purpose: Makes the matching point a movable target, not an accident.
drills.setup: A consistent pitch, 20 turns long; call the matching point out loud.
steps: Run one: match deliberately late, at the very end of every arc.
Run two: match at the fall line, skis pointing straight down.
Run three: match just above the fall line; note where the wedge began widening.
drills.success_indicator: You can nominate a matching point and hit it, both directions.

drills.name: Tall-short, said out loud
drills.purpose: Attaches the flex-extend cycle to the arc so pressure is managed.
drills.setup: Medium turns on a consistent pitch.
steps: Say 'tall' at each initiation and 'short' through each finish, out loud, for a run.
The words mark the arc; they do not trigger a hop.
Then ski a run silently and check the rhythm survived.
drills.success_indicator: No bump at the finish, and the match arrives on the 'short'.

dose.notes: Double volume on the weak side.

drills.name: Weak side first
drills.purpose: Removes the asymmetry that otherwise gets rebuilt in every later stage.
drills.setup: Identify the weaker direction on video or with a partner.
steps: Ski ten single turns to a stop, weak side only.
Then alternate weak and strong side, matching at the same point.
Finish every session with the weak side.
drills.success_indicator: Matching point and turn shape indistinguishable between directions on video.

drills.name: Little-toe tipping
drills.purpose: Fixes the A-frame by giving the inside leg a job other than collapsing.
steps: As the inside leg lightens, tip that foot onto its little-toe edge instead of dropping the knee in.
Feel the inside ski's edge angle match the outside ski's rather than oppose it.
Check the tracks: two bands tipped the same way.
drills.success_indicator: Knees and skis tip the same way; the inside ski holds its edge.

drills.name: Read it from the lift
drills.purpose: Turns terrain from a surprise into a plan.
drills.setup: Any lift with a view of the run you are about to ski.
steps: From the chair, name where the pitch changes, where snow is scraped, where traffic merges.
Decide where you will match early and where late.
Ski it, then check the predictions.
drills.success_indicator: Two of three predictions correct, and the plan executed.

faults.diagnosis_test: Garlands (dr-05-01) with a partner watching the outside ski's track. A widening track is the fault.

cues: Get light on the inside foot.
The outside ski stays where it is.

faults.name: Matching by pushing the outside ski
root_causes: The inside ski still carries pressure, so there is nothing available to move.
Pitch above the skier's comfort, where a wide platform feels safer.
faults.symptom: The skis become parallel because the outside ski moved away, not because the inside one came across.

faults.diagnosis_test: Little-toe tipping (dr-05-06): if the ski will not tip while the knee is held out, it is alignment, not habit.

cues: Tip the inside foot, not the knee.
Little toe toward the snow.
fix.equipment_check: Cuff alignment and canting, especially if the A-frame is one-sided.

faults.name: A-frame
root_causes: The inside knee dropped inward instead of the inside foot tipping.
Pelvis and femur geometry, which tends to produce medial knee tracking under load.
faults.symptom: The knees converge while the skis stay apart; the inside ski sits flat or on its wrong edge.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film from the side: a head that rises and falls at every match is hopping, not lightening.

cues: Shorten the inside leg, don't stand up.
Quiet head.
fix.equipment_check: Boot flex too stiff for the skier's mass removes flexion as an option.

faults.name: Hopping the match
root_causes: Whole-body extension used to unweight instead of flexing the inside leg.
No flexion range available, often because the boots cannot be flexed.
faults.symptom: The skis become parallel by way of an up-hop, both leaving the snow at the match.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ten single turns to a stop per side, partner naming each matching point. A gap over half an arc is the fault.

cues: Weak side first, every run.
Same terrain, twice the volume.

faults.name: One-sided christie
root_causes: Reps accumulated on the comfortable side, widening the gap every run.
An asymmetry carried up from the st-04 sideslip and hockey stop.
faults.symptom: One direction matches early and cleanly; the other stays wedged to the end of the arc.

faults.diagnosis_test: Matching-point ladder (dr-05-03): if the fall-line rung is impossible, the match comes after the arc.

cues: Match while you are still turning.
Say where you matched, every turn.

faults.name: Matching after the turn is over
root_causes: Speed controlled by the wedge rather than by turn shape.
The match treated as an end-of-turn tidy-up rather than a phase of the arc.
faults.symptom: The skis are parallel only in the traverse between turns; the arc itself is skied in a wedge.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ask for shin contact at the end of every turn for one run; no contact confirms it.

cues: Close the ankles, hips over the feet.
Shins on the tongues at the finish.
fix.equipment_check: Shell fit and flex first; gear causes this more often than habit.

faults.name: Sitting back through the finish
root_causes: Flexion produced by sitting rather than by closing the ankles.
Boots too large, too soft or too stiff, which look identical from outside.
faults.symptom: The hips retreat behind the heels as the turn completes; quads burn, tails wash out.

en.goal: Link wedge christies on green and easy blue terrain, matching the inside ski to parallel at or before the fall line by lightening it.
en.one_line: The turn still starts in a wedge and finishes parallel — the first time the inside ski is free.
safety_notes: Easy blue brings real closing speed. Right of way belongs to the skier below; stop where you can be seen from above.
The wedge is still the emergency tool here; retiring it as a habit does not mean giving it up as an option.
A back-seat finish on the inside edge of the downhill ski is the classic knee-injury position.

cues: Bring the little ski home.
Finish every turn with the tips level.
skills.description: In the second half of the turn the inside ski comes alongside the outside ski, and both finish the arc parallel, tips level.
skills.name: Matching the inside ski to parallel
skills.why: The entry ticket to st-06: with no matched platform there is nothing to release, so a parallel turn cannot start.

cues: Get light on the inside foot and it will come.
Let the outside ski take everything.
skills.description: The match comes from taking pressure off the inside ski and letting the outside ski carry the load, not from displacing it outward.
skills.name: Lightening, not pushing
skills.why: Pushing the outside ski out is a stem — the fault most likely to survive into st-10 and stop carving happening.

cues: Tall to start, shorter through the turn.
Let the legs breathe with the arc.
skills.description: The legs lengthen through the initiation and shorten through the finish, so pressure builds and releases instead of arriving as a bump.
skills.name: Flexion and extension to manage pressure
skills.why: Otherwise the match is timed by luck: the inside ski only floats while pressure is leaving it.

cues: Say where you matched, out loud, every turn.
Move the match a metre higher each run.
skills.description: The match can happen late, at the end of the arc, or early, at the fall line. Both are acceptable here; the point moves up as balance improves.
misconceptions: An early match is not automatically better: on a pitch that frightens you it becomes a stem.
skills.name: Choosing the matching point
skills.why: Naming the matching point turns 'ski more parallel' into a target, and moving it above the fall line is what st-06 asks for.

cues: Keep steering both feet to the end.
Round it off, don't check it.
skills.description: Once matched, both skis are steered together to the end of the arc with increasing edge, so speed is spent by shape.
skills.name: A parallel, steered finish
skills.why: Where st-04's progressive edging becomes a turn instead of a stop, and the first shape-not-brake skiing.

cues: Name three things about the run before you drop in.
Choose your first three turns from the chair.
skills.description: From the lift, name where the pitch changes, where the snow is scraped, and where you will match early or late.
skills.name: Reading a run before skiing it
skills.why: The first stage with real terrain choices; the alternative to planning is reacting, which rebuilds the security wedge.

tactics: Read the run from the lift and decide where you will match early and where late.
Ski the first run one grade easier and match deliberately late; the early match needs warm legs.
Choose runs with a clean run-out: a christie needs speed, and a flat finish invites braking.

avoid: Flat run-outs, where there is not enough speed for the inside ski to float.
Anything steep enough to make the skier widen the wedge for security.
Crowded beginner slopes; matching needs a corridor, not a slalom through stationary people.
terrain.ideal_description: A wide, consistently pitched 12-18 degree run with a clean run-out, long enough for 20 turns without stopping. Freshly groomed: matching is felt through the soles, and even snow is what makes it legible.

en.why_it_matters: This is the bridge rung, and it forks. Matching by lightening the inside ski becomes st-06's parallel turn; matching by pushing the outside ski away becomes a stem still visible on video ten years later.

adjustments: 这个年龄常靠模仿就滑出又宽又带搓雪的并腿弯，没人教过。让它自然发生，不要形式化。
只评两件事：叫停能停，叫在哪儿转就在哪儿转。
do_not: 不要因为两板有时平行了就加雪杖。

adjustments: 体重轻的人并板容易、持刃差：ac-05-01 会早来，ac-05-03 会晚一个雪季。
并板之后的宽站姿不要教掉；要纠正的是后座。

criteria_modifications.change: 前后滑动完全取代抬板：轻的孩子靠平衡就抬得起内板，什么也证明不了。

adjustments: 降量不降标准：每侧 6 个干净的半犁式，胜过 30 个累出来的。
更短更软的板在这个体重下压得弯，而这正是内板得以免负荷的前提。

criteria_modifications.change: 12 个弯可拆成两组 6 个、中间一次横切；数量与只许 1 次压刃的容差不变。

adjustments: 要盯的毛病是 A 形腿（ft-05-02）：骨盆相对膝间距更宽，受力时容易让内膝往里走。
教过之后仍在，就按对线处理——靴筒、内外倾垫片、鞋垫，不要再叠口令。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。若外板压不弯到能承担这个弯，那就换板。

zh.core_question: 我能把内板解放出来，并以两板平行收完这个弯吗？

drills.name: 半犁式花环
drills.purpose: 不投入落线，就把并板重复很多次。
drills.setup: 浅角度横切，保持一个轻犁式。
steps: 用犁式往落线方向做半个弯，并上内板，再回到横切。
横过雪道做 8 次，然后换方向。
并的瞬间犁式变宽了，就停下重来。
drills.success_indicator: 内板安静地到位；外板的轨迹没变。

drills.name: 羽化内板
drills.purpose: 证明内板是轻的——这一点滑者自己感觉不到。
drills.setup: 安静的缓坡，低速下的正常半犁式。
steps: 每个弯的后半段，把内板前后滑动几厘米。
承压的板滑不动，轻的板滑得动。
能自由滑动之后，某个弯里再抬起 2 厘米。
drills.success_indicator: 内板能自由滑动，弧线形状不变。

drills.name: 并板点梯子
drills.purpose: 让并板点成为一个可移动的靶子，不是意外。
drills.setup: 一段坡度均匀、够 20 个弯的雪道；并板点出声报出来。
steps: 第一趟：刻意晚并，并在每个弧线的最末端。
第二趟：并在落线上，板头正指山下。
第三趟：并在落线略上方；注意犁式从哪里开始变宽。
drills.success_indicator: 你能指定一个并板点并打中它，两个方向都行。

drills.name: 出声说高—矮
drills.purpose: 把屈伸循环挂到弧线上，让压力被管理。
drills.setup: 坡度均匀，中等大小的弯。
steps: 一整趟出声说：起弯「高」，收弯「矮」。
这两个词是给弧线打拍子，不是让你蹦一下。
然后滑一趟不出声，看节奏还在不在。
drills.success_indicator: 收弯处没有一记撞击，并板正好落在「矮」上。

dose.notes: 弱侧的量加倍。

drills.name: 弱侧先行
drills.purpose: 把不对称消掉，否则后面每一级都会把它重建一次。
drills.setup: 用录像或同伴认出弱的那个方向。
steps: 只做弱侧，10 个单弯到停。
然后弱侧强侧交替，并在同一个点上。
每次上雪都以弱侧收尾。
drills.success_indicator: 录像上两个方向的并板点与弧线形状分不出来。

drills.name: 小脚趾立刃
drills.purpose: 给内腿一件除了塌下去以外的事，用来治 A 形腿。
steps: 内腿变轻的同时，把那只脚倒到小脚趾侧刃上，不要让膝盖往里掉。
感觉内板的刃角与外板同向，而不是相反。
看雪痕：两条带子朝同一边倒。
drills.success_indicator: 膝与板倒向同一边；内板守住自己的刃。

drills.name: 在缆车上读它
drills.purpose: 把地形从一个意外变成一个计划。
drills.setup: 任何一条能看见你即将去滑的雪道的缆车。
steps: 在缆车上说出坡度在哪变、雪在哪被刮花、人流在哪汇入。
定下哪里早并、哪里晚并。
滑一遍，再回头核对预测。
drills.success_indicator: 三个预测里对两个，而且计划被执行了。

faults.diagnosis_test: 花环（dr-05-01），让同伴盯外板的雪痕。痕变宽就是这个毛病。

cues: 内脚变轻。
外板留在原地不动。

faults.name: 靠推外板来并板
root_causes: 内板还在承压，没有可以移动的东西。
坡度超出舒适区，宽平台让人觉得更安全。
faults.symptom: 两板变平行，是因为外板挪开了，不是因为内板收了过来。

faults.diagnosis_test: 小脚趾立刃（dr-05-06）：膝盖被顶住时板还立不起来，就是对线，不是习惯。

cues: 倒脚，不是倒膝。
小脚趾往雪面去。
fix.equipment_check: 靴筒对线与内外倾垫片，尤其是只有一侧出现 A 形腿时。

faults.name: A 形腿
root_causes: 内膝往里掉，而不是内脚往外倒。
骨盆与股骨的几何关系，受力时容易让膝盖内扣。
faults.symptom: 双膝相互靠拢而双板分开；内板平放，或者立在反的那条刃上。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从侧面拍：每次并板脑袋都起落一次，那是在跳，不是在变轻。

cues: 收短内腿，不要站起来。
脑袋安静。
fix.equipment_check: 靴子硬度对这个体重太硬，屈曲就不再是一个选项。

faults.name: 跳着并板
root_causes: 用全身伸展去卸载，而不是屈内腿。
没有可用的屈曲范围，常因为靴子压不动。
faults.symptom: 两板靠一次上蹬变平行，并的瞬间双板同时离雪。

faults.diagnosis_test: 每侧 10 个单弯到停，同伴报出每次的并板点。差超过半个弧线就是它。

cues: 每趟都从弱侧开始。
同样的坡，两倍的量。

faults.name: 单侧半犁式
root_causes: 次数堆在舒服那一侧，每趟都把差距拉大。
从 st-04 侧滑与横向急停带上来的不对称。
faults.symptom: 一个方向又早又干净地并上；另一个方向一路犁到弧线末端。

faults.diagnosis_test: 并板点梯子（dr-05-03）：落线那一档做不出来，并板就在弧线之后。

cues: 还在转的时候就并。
每个弯都报出你在哪儿并的。

faults.name: 弯结束之后才并板
root_causes: 速度靠犁式管，不靠弧线形状管。
把并板当收尾的整理，不当弧线的一个阶段。
faults.symptom: 只在两弯之间的横切里平行；弧线本身是犁着滑的。

faults.diagnosis_test: 一整趟要求每个弯末端都有小腿接触；没有接触就确认是它。

cues: 收踝，髋压在脚上方。
收弯时小腿贴靴舌。
fix.equipment_check: 先查壳测与硬度；这件事装备的责任比习惯大。

faults.name: 收弯时坐下去
root_causes: 屈曲是坐出来的，不是收踝收出来的。
靴子过大、过软或过硬——从外面看一模一样。
faults.symptom: 弯收完时髋退到脚跟后面；大腿灼烧，板尾被甩出去。

zh.goal: 在绿道与缓蓝道上连续做半犁式：靠把内板变轻，在落线处或之前把它并成平行。
zh.one_line: 弯还是从犁式起、以平行式收——内板第一次被解放出来。
safety_notes: 缓蓝道有真实的接近速度。下方滑雪者有优先权；停在上方看得见处。
犁式在这里仍是应急工具；作为习惯退役，不等于作为选项放弃。
后座、又压在山下侧板内刃上收弯，是经典的膝伤姿势。

cues: 把小板收回家。
每个弯都以板头齐平收尾。
skills.description: 弯的后半段内板收到外板旁边，两板平行、板头齐平地收完弧线。
skills.name: 把内板并成平行
skills.why: 进 st-06 的门票：没有并好的平台，就没有东西可解，平行式的弯起不来。

cues: 内脚一变轻，它自己就回来。
让外板承担全部。
skills.description: 并板来自把压力从内板拿走、让外板承担，不是把内板挪出去。
skills.name: 变轻，不是推出去
skills.why: 把外板推出去就是外八字——最可能活到 st-10、并且让刻滑无法发生的毛病。

cues: 起弯站高，过弯变矮。
让腿跟着弧线呼吸。
skills.description: 起弯时腿伸长、收弯时腿收短，压力于是渐进上来、渐进下去，不是一记撞上来。
skills.name: 用屈伸管理压力
skills.why: 否则并板的时机全靠运气：内板只在压力正离开它的那一瞬浮得起来。

cues: 每个弯都出声报出你在哪儿并的。
每趟把并板点往上挪一米。
skills.description: 并板可以晚到弧线末端，也可以早到落线。这一级两者都合格；随平衡进步，这个点往上移。
misconceptions: 早并不自动更好：在一段让你害怕的坡上，它会变成外八字。
skills.name: 选择并板点
skills.why: 把「滑得更平行」变成一个能瞄的目标；把它移到落线以上，正是 st-06 的要求。

cues: 两只脚一直转到底。
把它收圆，不要压一下刹。
skills.description: 并上之后两板一起被转到弧线末端，刃角持续增加，速度由形状花掉。
skills.name: 平行、带转向的收弯
skills.why: st-04 的渐进立刃在这里从「停」变成「弯」，也是第一次用形状而不是刹车滑雪。

cues: 出发前先说出这条道的三件事。
在缆车上就选好头三个弯。
skills.description: 在缆车上说出坡度在哪里变、雪在哪里被刮花、哪里你会早并、哪里晚并。
skills.name: 滑之前先把这条道读出来
skills.why: 第一个有真实地形选择的级别；不计划就只能反应，而反应会把保命的犁式重新造出来。

tactics: 在缆车上把这条道读一遍，定好哪里早并、哪里晚并。
第一趟降一档地形并刻意晚并；早并要热开的腿。
选出口干净的雪道：半犁式需要速度，平坦的收尾会招来刹车。

avoid: 平坦出口：速度不够，内板浮不起来。
陡到让人为了安全把犁式张大的坡。
拥挤的初学坡；并板需要一条走廊，不是在人堆里绕旗门。
terrain.ideal_description: 宽阔、坡度均匀的 12–18 度雪道，出口干净，长到能不停做 20 个弯。刚压过雪：并板靠脚底感觉，均匀的雪面才让它读得出来。

zh.why_it_matters: 这是过桥的那一级，而且是个岔路口。靠减轻内板并上，长成 st-06 的平行式；靠把外板推出去并上，就是十年后录像里还看得见的外八字。

adjustments: Rhythm and confidence arrive before edge-hold and strength. Treat ac-06-04 as a game: a light skier passes it on balance alone.
A wide stance is appropriate at this age; correct the back seat, not the width.
One cue per run. A back-seat child is usually oversized boots before it is technique.
Poles from 8-9 only, and only once the parallel turn is established; a younger child runs this stage and st-07's tempo work without them.

criteria_modifications.change: Skip the end-of-day comparison; a child's afternoon is fatigue and blood sugar, not fore/aft.

do_not: No poles simply because parallel skiing has arrived; age 8-9 at the earliest.

adjustments: Spread new patterns across more days rather than more repetitions in one day; recovery is the limiter.
Prioritise dryland eccentric quad strength and ankle mobility; they change more here than any cue.
A skier who cannot flex the boot in the shop will not find a centred stance on snow.
Shorter, softer, lighter skis materially improve outcomes; equipment choice here is a technique intervention.
Volume down, quality up: 4 focused runs beat 8 degraded ones, and every gate here is quality.

criteria_modifications.change: The feathered version (zero pressure, ski on the snow) passes; the 2-5 cm lift is not required.

adjustments: Fit is the highest-leverage intervention: calf volume, calf-insertion height and heel width often make a standard boot the wrong tool.
A wider pelvis relative to knee spacing tends to produce inward knee tracking under load, seen as the A-frame in ft-06-01.
Where alignment problems persist after coaching, refer to a bootfitter rather than adding cues.

criteria_modifications.change: None to the standard. Where lower mass makes long-radius turns hard to drive, choose a shorter, softer ski.

adjustments: Greater average mass and upper-body strength make it easy to force a turn with rotation, which passes the eye test and fails ac-06-01.
Where strength substitutes for technique, the fault surfaces two stages later on ice and in bumps.

en.core_question: Can I start and finish every turn parallel, controlling speed with shape alone?

drills.name: Thousand steps
drills.purpose: Makes freezing mid-turn impossible and forces continuous pressure transfer.
drills.setup: One grade easier than your comfort terrain; no poles at first.
steps: Ski normal turns while stepping in place, 3-5 small steps per turn, both directions.
The ski barely leaves the snow; stepping never stops at the transition.
Then step only through the shaping phase, to find where you were static.
drills.success_indicator: The turn feels continuously made, with no moment of holding.

drills.name: Railroad tracks
drills.purpose: Isolates tipping from steering: thin lines mean edging, smears mean rotation.
drills.setup: Very gentle, freshly groomed, no traffic.
steps: From a straight run, tip both feet the same way, inside foot first, and let the skis run.
Do not steer, push the tails, or complete the turn.
Inspect your tracks after every run.
drills.success_indicator: Two pencil-width lines in the corduroy, no widening at the tails.

drills.name: Outside-ski-only turns
drills.purpose: Trains outside-ski balance by removing the inside ski as an option.
steps: Start the turn normally, then lift the inside ski 2-5 cm through the shaping phase.
Set it down at the transition and lift the new inside ski.
Keep the lift small; if you cannot hold it, lighten the ski instead.
drills.success_indicator: Turn shape does not change while the inside ski is up.

drills.name: Pole across the body
drills.purpose: Gives the torso a reference line, making rotation visible.
drills.setup: One pole held horizontally across the body, at hip height.
steps: Ski medium turns, keeping the pole pointed across the fall line.
Notice how much it wants to swing at the initiation: that is your rotation.
Then ski a run with the pole pointed continuously down the hill.
drills.success_indicator: The pole holds its line while the legs turn beneath it.

drills.name: Parallel garlands
drills.purpose: Repeats the release many times per run without committing to the fall line.
drills.setup: Traverse at a shallow angle.
steps: Release both edges and tip into a new turn, only until the skis point slightly downhill.
Return to the traverse without finishing the turn; repeat 6-10 times, then switch sides.
Every release must be simultaneous; if a stem appears, stop and restart.
drills.success_indicator: Both skis change edge at once, quietly, with no tail push.

drills.name: Constant-speed run
drills.purpose: Forces speed regulation through shape by removing braking as an option.
drills.setup: A blue with a pitch change and a clear run-out.
steps: Ski top to bottom at one speed; the only adjustment is how far each arc crosses the hill.
Steeper pitch, rounder and longer turns; flatter pitch, open toward the fall line.
No checks, no hockey stops, no traverses; time two descents within 10%.
drills.success_indicator: Speed feels unchanged across pitch changes; difficulty shows as shape, not velocity.

dose.notes: 24 turns minimum per run.

drills.name: Corridor turns, three sizes
drills.purpose: Separates turn size from turn quality, making size a choice.
drills.setup: An imagined corridor down the fall line: 12-15 m, 7-8 m, 4-5 m.
steps: Ski 8 round turns in the wide corridor, finishing each arc across the hill.
Without stopping, 8 in the medium and 8 in the narrow, same speed.
Repeat in both directions of size; note which size degrades first.
drills.success_indicator: All three sizes stay round, at one speed, same stance.

faults.diagnosis_test: Try to lift the inside ski mid-arc (dr-06-03); if you cannot, you are banking.

cues: Long outside leg, short inside leg.
Hip in, chest over the outside ski.

faults.name: Banking
root_causes: Inclination without angulation: no lateral bend at hip or knee.
Chasing edge angle before outside-ski balance exists.
faults.symptom: The whole body leans in; the inside ski takes load; grip fails on firm snow.

faults.diagnosis_test: Pole across the body (dr-06-04): if the pole swings at every initiation, the torso is steering.

cues: Turn your feet, not your shoulders.
Chest down the hill.

faults.name: Upper-body rotation
root_causes: Legs not yet independent enough to rotate on their own at this speed.
Late initiation, so the skier reaches for the turn with the torso.
faults.symptom: The turn starts by twisting the shoulders; steering runs out halfway through the arc.

faults.diagnosis_test: Feel for boot-tongue contact at the end of every turn; no contact is this fault.

cues: Shins on the tongues at the transition.
Hips over the feet as the skis come around.
fix.equipment_check: Shell fit, flex and ski length: most often a gear fault.

faults.name: Back seat at the turn finish
root_causes: Fore/aft not managed at pitch changes.
Boots too soft, too stiff or too large, or skis too long for the weight.
faults.symptom: Turns finish with the hips behind the feet; quads burn; the tails wash out.

faults.diagnosis_test: Parallel garlands (dr-06-05) at steeper and steeper traverse angles; where the stem appears is your terrain limit.

cues: Release both feet together.
Tip the little toe, don't push the big toe away.

faults.looks_like: From below, a momentary A-shape at every transition, often one-sided.
faults.name: Residual stem at initiation
root_causes: Non-simultaneous edge change: the defining fault of this stage.
The stem used as security on steeper pitches or in traffic.
Weight given to the new outside ski too late, so the platform is stepped onto.
faults.symptom: The skis flare into a brief wedge, or the uphill ski steps out, before an otherwise parallel turn.

faults.diagnosis_test: Constant-speed run (dr-06-06): if you cannot finish one without a check, this fault owns your skiing.

cues: If you need to slow down, turn further.
Draw a C, not a Z.

faults.name: Z-shaped braking turns
root_causes: Speed controlled by braking rather than by shape.
Turns started late and finished abruptly, beyond current shape control.
faults.symptom: Each turn ends with a deliberate sideways push; the descent is a series of stops.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ski a run trying to see both hands; if you must look for one, it is behind you.

cues: Both hands where you can see them.
Carry a tray.
fix.equipment_check: Pole length: 5 cm shorter rather than longer for an intermediate.

faults.name: Hands dropping, poles as crutches
root_causes: Poles introduced without a session on carrying them.
A fore/aft problem showing in the hands, which follow the hips.
faults.symptom: One or both hands drift back and down; the pole is leaned on, not touched.

en.goal: Ski linked parallel turns on blue groomed terrain, initiated by releasing and tipping rather than stemming, with speed regulated entirely by turn shape.
en.one_line: Both skis point the same way from the first instant of the turn to the last, and speed comes from turn shape.
safety_notes: Blue terrain brings real closing speeds. Right of way belongs to the skier below, and stopping where you are visible from above prevents collisions.
A backward, twisting fall on the inside edge of the downhill ski is the classic knee-injury mechanism (ft-06-03). Arms forward, and do not fight it.
Fatigue injuries cluster in the last run. Stop with a run in reserve.

cues: Let both feet go flat at the same time.
Roll the new little toe toward the snow.
skills.description: Both skis leave their old edges and reach the new ones at the same moment, led by tipping the new inside foot.
misconceptions: The turn does not start with the outside ski; it starts by releasing both feet.
skills.name: Simultaneous edge release, led by the new inside foot
skills.why: A non-simultaneous edge change is the stem, and every later skill inherits it.

cues: Stand on the downhill ski and let the other come along.
Little foot light, big foot loaded.
skills.description: Most of the load sits on the outside ski through the shaping phase, around 80/20 on firm snow; the inside ski stays parallel but light.
skills.name: Outside-ski dominance
skills.why: The outside ski bends, holds and steers; without that platform the skier rotates and skids.

cues: Turn your feet, not your shoulders.
Chest down the hill, legs underneath you.
skills.description: Direction change comes from rotating the femurs in the hip sockets while chest and hands face down the hill.
skills.name: Leg rotation with a quiet upper body
skills.why: Torso rotation is self-limiting: once turned it cannot turn again, so steering runs out mid-arc.

cues: Finish the turn across the hill, then start the next.
To slow down, turn further; don't push harder.
skills.description: Speed comes from how far the arc is carried across the hill, not from pushing the skis sideways: a C, not a Z.
skills.name: Round turn shape as the primary speed control
skills.why: Braking has a ceiling; shape works wherever the edges hold.

cues: Shins on the tongues at the lip of every roll.
Move with the hill, not after it.
skills.description: As the slope steepens the skier moves forward to stay centred; as it flattens, back to centre. Small, continuous, from the ankles.
misconceptions: 'Lean forward' is not the fix: leaning bends the waist and pushes the hips back. Close the ankle instead.
skills.name: Fore/aft management through pitch changes
skills.why: Faults here that look like missing skill are usually fore/aft errors at a pitch change, and the backward twisting fall is the classic knee injury.

cues: Both hands where you can see them.
Touch, don't plant.
skills.description: Hands forward, hip-width and hip-height, in peripheral vision. A light basket touch at the transition marks rhythm: no weight, no swing.
skills.name: Basic pole use: quiet hands and a timing touch
skills.why: A dropped hand means a body that is late or back; discipline built now prevents the st-07 crutch habit.

tactics: Choose rolling pitch over uniform pitch; pitch changes build fore/aft skill and expose it.
Stop above a rise, at the side, visible from above, and look uphill before rejoining.
Read the run from the chairlift: pitch changes, ice, merges.

avoid: Narrow cat tracks and traverses, which reward the defensive static stance this stage removes.
Crowded end-of-day runs, where traffic forces reactive skiing.
Terrain steeper than the skier's sideslip confidence, which turns every drill into speed management.
terrain.ideal_description: A wide, consistently pitched blue groomer, 20-25 degrees, with one rolling pitch change and a clear run-out. Long enough for 25-30 turns without stopping, because rhythm cannot be learned in 8-turn fragments.

en.why_it_matters: Here skiing becomes repeatable technique: carving, bumps and powder are all variations on the parallel turn. A residual stem carried out of this stage is why intermediates plateau for a decade.

adjustments: 节奏与地形自信早于持刃和力量。ac-06-04 当游戏：体重轻的孩子靠平衡就能通过。
这个年龄宽站姿是合适的；要纠正的是后座，不是宽度。
一趟一个口令。后座的孩子通常先是靴子过大，才是技术。
雪杖最早 8–9 岁，且须等平行式稳定之后；更小的孩子不带杖完成本级与 st-07 的节奏训练。

criteria_modifications.change: 跳过收工对比：孩子的下午由疲劳和血糖决定，不是前后平衡。

do_not: 不要因为「会平行式了」就加雪杖；最早 8–9 岁。

adjustments: 新动作分散到更多天，而不是一天做更多次；限制因素是恢复。
优先陆地训练：离心股四头肌力量与踝灵活度，比任何口令改变更大。
在店里就压不动靴子的人，雪上也做不出中立站姿。
更短、更软、更轻的板实质改善结果；装备选择在这里是技术干预。
降量保质：4 趟专注优于 8 趟退化，本级所有关卡都是质量关卡。

criteria_modifications.change: 「羽化」版本（压力为零、板不离雪）可判通过；不要求抬起 2–5 厘米。

adjustments: 适配回报最高：小腿围、小腿肌起点高度、后跟宽度，常让标准鞋型成为错误工具。
骨盆相对膝间距更宽，受力时容易膝盖内扣，表现为 ft-06-01 里的 A 形腿。
对线问题在教学后仍存在，应转给靴技师，不要叠加口令。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。若因体重较轻难以驱动大回转，应换更短更软的板。

adjustments: 更大的体重与上肢力量容易用旋转「拗」出一个弯：能过肉眼，过不了 ac-06-01。
当力量替代技术时，问题会在两级之后的冰面和雪包里暴露。

zh.core_question: 每个弯的开始和结束都平行，且只靠形状控速？

drills.name: 千步走
drills.purpose: 让「弧线中途站死」在物理上不可能，并强迫持续压力转移。
drills.setup: 比舒适坡度低一档的雪道；先不用雪杖。
steps: 滑正常大小的弯，全程原地小幅踏步：每弯 3–5 步，两侧都做。
板几乎不离雪面；换刃瞬间也不许停。
然后只在造型期踏步，定位原来在哪里站死。
drills.success_indicator: 转弯变成「一直在做」，找不出「憋住」的一刻。

drills.name: 铁轨
drills.purpose: 把立刃从转向中剥离：细线是立刃，抹痕是旋转。
drills.setup: 非常平缓、刚压过雪、无人流。
steps: 从直行开始两脚同时倒向一侧，内脚先倒，让板自己走。
不要转向、不要推板尾、不要把弯做完。
每趟结束回头看雪痕。
drills.success_indicator: 压雪纹上两条铅笔宽的细线，尾部不变宽。

drills.name: 单外板转弯
drills.purpose: 取消「内板」这个选项，训练外板平衡。
steps: 正常起弯，把内板抬离雪面 2–5 厘米，保持到造型期结束。
换刃瞬间放下，再抬起新的内板。
幅度要小；抬不住就改成减压不离雪。
drills.success_indicator: 内板离雪期间，弧线形状不变。

drills.name: 横持雪杖
drills.purpose: 给躯干一条参考线，让上身旋转看得见。
drills.setup: 双手横持一根雪杖于身前，约髋高。
steps: 滑中等大小的弯，全程让杖身横切落线。
注意起弯瞬间它多想跟着转：那就是你在用的上身旋转。
然后滑一趟让杖身持续指向山下。
drills.success_indicator: 杖的指向不变，腿在稳定的躯干下面转。

drills.name: 平行式花环
drills.purpose: 一趟里重复大量「解刃」，而不必真的进入落线。
drills.setup: 以较浅的角度横切山坡。
steps: 解开两侧旧刃倒向新方向，做到板头略指向山下就停。
不完成转弯，回到横切；重复 6–10 次后换方向。
每次解刃都必须同步；一出现外八字就停下重来。
drills.success_indicator: 两板同时换刃，动作安静，没有推板尾。

drills.name: 恒速下降
drills.purpose: 取消刹车这个选项，强迫用形状调节速度。
drills.setup: 一条带坡度变化、出口开阔的蓝道。
steps: 从顶到底保持一个速度，唯一可调的是弧线横切山坡多远。
坡陡就把弯做得更圆更长，坡缓就往落线方向打开。
不许压刃刹、急停或横切放速；计时两趟，相差在 10% 以内。
drills.success_indicator: 坡度变化处速度感觉不变；难度体现在形状，不在速度。

dose.notes: 每趟至少 24 个转弯。

drills.name: 三种尺寸的走廊转弯
drills.purpose: 把尺寸从质量里分离，让尺寸成为主动选择。
drills.setup: 沿落线想象一条走廊：12–15 米、7–8 米、4–5 米。
steps: 宽走廊里滑 8 个圆润的弯，每个弧线都横切完成。
不停顿，接着中走廊 8 个、窄走廊 8 个，同一速度。
由大到小、由小到大各做一遍，记下哪个尺寸最先崩。
drills.success_indicator: 三种尺寸都圆润、同速、同一站姿。

faults.diagnosis_test: 弧线中段试着抬起内板（dr-06-03）；抬不起来就是内倾。

cues: 外腿长，内腿短。
髋进弯内，胸口压在外板上。

faults.name: 整体内倾（banking）
root_causes: 只有内倾没有角度：髋与膝没有横向折角。
外板平衡还没建立就去追更大刃角。
faults.symptom: 整个身体往弯内倒；内板承重；硬雪上抓不住。

faults.diagnosis_test: 横持雪杖（dr-06-04）：每次起弯杖身都跟着甩，就是躯干在转向。

cues: 转脚，不转肩。
胸口对着山下。

faults.name: 上身旋转
root_causes: 这个速度下腿的独立性不足以自己完成转动。
启动太晚，只好用躯干去抓转弯。
faults.symptom: 用扭肩启动转弯；弯做到一半就「转没了」。

faults.diagnosis_test: 感受每个弯末端靴子前部的接触；没有接触就是它。

cues: 换刃瞬间小腿贴靴舌。
板绕过来时把髋带到脚上方。
fix.equipment_check: 壳测间隙、硬度、板长：这多半是装备问题。

faults.name: 收弯时后座
root_causes: 坡度变化处没有管理前后平衡。
靴子过软、过硬或过大，或板长相对体重过长。
faults.symptom: 收弯时髋在脚后面；大腿灼烧；板尾被甩掉。

faults.diagnosis_test: 在越来越陡的横切角度上做花环（dr-06-05）；外八字出现的角度就是地形上限。

cues: 两只脚一起放开。
倒小脚趾，不要把大脚趾推出去。

faults.looks_like: 从下方看，每次换刃都有一瞬间的 A 形，通常只在某一侧。
faults.name: 启动时残留外八字
root_causes: 换刃不同步：本级的核心毛病。
在陡坡或人流中把外八字当安全动作用。
重心交给新外板太晚，靠「踩」而不是靠立刃造平台。
faults.symptom: 其余部分平行，但起弯瞬间双板短暂张成犁式，或山上侧板先踩出。

faults.diagnosis_test: 恒速下降（dr-06-06）：一趟撑不到不刹车，它就主导你的滑行。

cues: 想慢就多转一点。
画 C，不要画 Z。

faults.name: Z 形刹车式转弯
root_causes: 用刹车而不是用形状控速。
起弯太晚、收弯太急，地形超出当前形状控制能力。
faults.symptom: 每个弯都以刻意的横向推板减速；整趟是一串「停」。

faults.diagnosis_test: 全程试着同时看见两只手；需要「找」的那只就在你身后。

cues: 两只手都在看得见的地方。
像端托盘。
fix.equipment_check: 杖长：中级宁可短 5 厘米，不要长。

faults.name: 手掉下去、把雪杖当拐杖
root_causes: 引入雪杖时没有专门练过怎么端它。
前后平衡问题在手上显形——手跟着髋走。
faults.symptom: 一只或两只手往后下方漂；点杖变成「靠」在杖上。

zh.goal: 在蓝道压雪面上连续做平行式转弯：以解刃立刃启动而非外八字，速度完全由弧线形状调节。
zh.one_line: 从起弯第一瞬间到收弯，两只板始终朝同一方向；速度来自弧线形状。
safety_notes: 蓝道意味着真实相对速度。下方滑雪者有优先权；停在上方看得见处就是防碰撞机制。
在下坡板内刃上向后失衡并扭转的摔倒是典型膝伤机制（ft-06-03）。手臂保持在前，不要挣扎。
疲劳相关受伤集中在最后一趟；留一趟在口袋里再收工。

cues: 两只脚同时放平。
新内脚小脚趾，往雪面倒下去。
skills.description: 两板同时离开旧刃、同时落到新刃，由新内脚倒向小脚趾刃引导。
misconceptions: 转弯不是从外板开始，而是从「同时松开两只脚」开始。
skills.name: 同步解刃换刃，由新内脚引导
skills.why: 不同步的换刃就是外八字，后面每一项技术都会继承它。

cues: 站在下坡那只板上，让另一只跟着走。
小脚轻，大脚重。
skills.description: 造型期绝大部分负荷在外板上，硬雪面约 80/20；内板平行但很轻。
skills.name: 外板主导
skills.why: 外板才是能压弯、能咬住、能引导的板；没有它只能靠旋转和侧滑。

cues: 转脚，不转肩。
胸口对着山下，腿在身体下面转。
skills.description: 方向改变来自大腿骨在髋窝内转动，胸口与双手朝向山下。
skills.name: 腿部转动 + 安静的上身
skills.why: 上身旋转自我封顶：躯干转过去就不能再转，弯做一半就「转没了」。

cues: 把这个弯横切完，再开下一个。
想慢就多转一点，不要推得更狠。
skills.description: 速度来自弧线横切山坡的程度，不是推板的力度：画 C，不是画 Z。
skills.name: 以圆弧形状作为主要控速手段
skills.why: 刹车有上限；只要刃咬得住，形状控速在任何坡上都成立。

cues: 每个坡沿处，小腿贴住靴舌。
跟着坡走，不要等坡到了才动。
skills.description: 坡变陡时前移保持中立位，坡变平时回到中立。幅度小、连续，来自踝关节。
misconceptions: 「前倾」不是解法：前倾会弯腰、把髋推到后面。要做的是收踝。
skills.name: 坡度变化中的前后平衡管理
skills.why: 这一级看似「技术不行」的问题多半出在坡度变化处的前后错误；扭转式后倒是典型膝伤机制。

cues: 两只手都在你看得见的地方。
是「点」，不是「插」。
skills.description: 双手前置、与髋同宽同高、在余光内。换刃瞬间杖篮轻点雪面标记节奏，不承重不甩臂。
skills.name: 基础杖法：安静的手与计时点杖
skills.why: 手掉下去说明身体慢了或后座；现在建立纪律，可避免卡在第 7 级的拐杖习惯。

tactics: 优先选起伏坡：坡度变化既锻造前后平衡，也照出问题。
停在坡凸起之上、雪道侧边、上方看得见的位置，出发前向上观察。
从缆车上读线：坡度在哪里变、哪里结冰、哪里汇入人流。

avoid: 窄猫道与横切道：奖励这一级要消灭的防御性僵硬站姿。
临近关门的拥挤雪道：人流逼出被动反应式滑行。
陡到超出侧滑信心的坡：每个练习都会退化成速度管理。
terrain.ideal_description: 宽阔、坡度均匀的蓝道压雪面，20–25 度，带一处坡度变化，出口开阔。长度够连续做 25–30 个弯：节奏学不会于「8 个弯一段」。

zh.why_it_matters: 刻滑、雪包、粉雪都是平行式的变体，这一级是分水岭。带着残留外八字离开，正是中级停滞十年的原因。

adjustments: Tempo work suits this band and can be taught as follow-the-leader long before range of motion is physically available.
Light mass makes retraction nearly weightless, so it is learned as a shape rather than a release against pressure.

criteria_modifications.change: Scale 15 cm to roughly 10 percent of standing height; 15 cm is a different demand on a 130 cm skier.
Test on blue, 12 turns not 24: a coordination gate here, not a pressure gate.

do_not: Do not introduce the blocking plant before st-06's timing touch is automatic.

adjustments: Eccentric strength decline is the direct limiter here; the dryland block decides whether ac-07-01 is reachable.
Spread retraction work across sessions rather than drilling to fatigue - tired retraction produces ft-07-05.

criteria_modifications.change: The 24-turn set may be split into two sets of 12; the gate tests timing, not endurance.

adjustments: Prioritise cross-over over retraction: lower impact, and it works at the speeds this band chooses.
Reduce volume, not standards. Three focused corridor sets beat a day of degraded rhythm work.

criteria_modifications.change: 12 cm passes where measured joint range makes 15 cm unavailable; the timing requirement is unchanged.

adjustments: Lower average mass leaves less pressure to flex against, so retraction is harder to feel. Build it at speed on a steeper groomed pitch.
Hamstring and single-leg eccentric strength serve twice: they produce the range and protect against the ft-07-05 mechanism.

criteria_modifications.change: No change to the standard. Where a stiff cuff prevents the range, change the boot, not the number.

adjustments: High pressure at the finish makes retraction natural and cross-over the release needing deliberate work.
A ski too soft for the skier's mass folds at the finish and mimics ft-07-06.

en.core_question: Can I ski in rhythm, with range of motion and functional pole use?

drills.name: Flex-to-release garlands
drills.purpose: Isolates retraction: the edge change happens because the legs shorten.
drills.setup: Traverse a consistent blue, tall on both legs.
steps: Flex both legs sharply; the skis flatten and slide under you.
Lengthen onto the same edges and resume the traverse, without turning.
After 8 releases per side, link them into turns, head on a level line.
drills.success_indicator: The skis unload with no rise in the body; the transition is low and quiet.

dose.notes: One set per run, 10 turns minimum.

drills.name: Two-release contrast run
drills.purpose: Makes both releases distinguishable by feel, and exposes up-unweighting by contrast.
drills.setup: One long blue with a steeper lower pitch.
steps: 10 turns by cross-over: hips diagonally across the skis, legs long.
10 by retraction: legs shorten, body path level. Then 10 deliberately up-unweighting.
10 choosing the release each pitch deserves, named aloud.
drills.success_indicator: You can name the release you just used, correctly, unprompted.

dose.notes: One tempo per run, same marked section.

drills.name: Metronome turns
drills.purpose: Fixes the beat and lets turn shape absorb the pitch change.
drills.setup: A run with two distinct pitches; count aloud or use a metronome at 50-70 bpm.
steps: One edge change per beat for the whole run, counting aloud.
Where it steepens, carry the arc further across rather than turning sooner.
Repeat 20 percent faster, then slower, counting turns on one marked section.
drills.success_indicator: Turn count on the marked section repeats within one turn per tempo.

drills.name: Blocking plant in a corridor
drills.purpose: Builds the plant at the tempo that needs it, where torso stability matters.
drills.setup: A 3-4 m corridor down the fall line, ideally a groomer seam.
steps: 12 short-radius turns in the corridor, planting the downhill pole firmly at each finish.
Plant ahead of the boot and slightly downhill, then ski past the pole.
Alternate 12 planting and 12 touching; shoulders stay square to the fall line.
drills.success_indicator: The upper body stays quiet at a tempo where it used to swing.

drills.name: Javelin turns
drills.purpose: Forces outside-ski balance by crossing the inside ski over the outside tip.
drills.setup: A moderate, empty blue, skied fresh.
steps: Start a turn, lift the inside ski and cross it over the outside ski's tip.
Hold the crossing through the shaping phase; set it down at the transition.
4 turns per side, then 4 normal turns holding the same hip position.
drills.success_indicator: Turn shape and speed unchanged with the inside ski crossed and airborne.

drills.name: Three-count edge build
drills.purpose: Divides the arc into three deliberate stages of edge angle.
drills.setup: Fresh corduroy on a consistent pitch.
steps: Count 'one' at initiation with least edge, 'two' at the fall line, 'three' at the finish.
An uneven count means the edge was set, not built.
12 turns counting aloud, 12 silent, then inspect the track.
drills.success_indicator: The track narrows continuously, with no sudden change of width.

drills.name: Skid and grip on command
drills.purpose: Makes skidding a tool by requiring the drift to start and stop at named points.
drills.setup: Two references about 20 m apart on a consistent pitch.
steps: At the first reference, release edge angle enough to drift sideways.
At the second, rebuild edge angle progressively and stop the drift without a check.
6 pairs per direction, halving the drift distance each pair.
drills.success_indicator: Drift starts and stops within 2 m of the references, with no spray.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film from the side and track the helmet: a saw-tooth path is up-unweighting, a level path is either correct release.

cues: Move across the skis, not up off them.
Lengthen into the new turn.

faults.looks_like: A pop at every edge change, chattering or airborne skis, then a hard landing.
faults.name: Up-unweighting
root_causes: Extension used to unload the ski rather than to build pressure.
A turn finished so hard the only escape is upward.
faults.symptom: An abrupt vertical extension unloads the skis at the transition; the skiing feels bouncy.

faults.diagnosis_test: 12 turns planting, then 12 touching only. If tempo collapses without the pole, the pole was doing the skiing.

cues: Plant ahead of your boot, then ski past it.
Wrist, not shoulder.
