fix.equipment_check: Pole length: cut 5 cm rather than adding it.

faults.looks_like: A bending pole, a dipped inside shoulder, a plant behind the boot.
faults.name: Pole plant as a crutch
root_causes: The plant introduced before st-06's timing touch was reliable.
Poles too long, forcing the plant back and the shoulder up.
faults.symptom: The pole carries weight, arrives late, or drags the shoulder into the turn.

faults.diagnosis_test: Read the track below the pitch change: even spacing with sharp corners is the fault, round arcs the skill.

cues: Same beat, rounder arc.
Finish across the hill, then take the beat.

faults.looks_like: An evenly spaced Z-shaped track, snow sprayed each turn, an upper body pulsing on the beat.
faults.name: Rhythm without shape
root_causes: Beat held by flattening turn shape rather than changing turn size.
A steeper pitch answered by turning sooner, not finishing further across.
faults.symptom: Turns arrive on the beat, but each is a braking check; the descent feels jarring.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film from the side and measure hip height across a turn. Under roughly 10 cm of travel means no range.

cues: Shortest at the finish, tallest in the middle.
Breathe out as the legs shorten.

faults.looks_like: A body tracing an unvarying line, tense shoulders, nothing visible at the transition.
faults.name: Flat-line skiing
root_causes: Range of motion never trained; st-06 rewarded stability and the skier kept it.
Too little eccentric strength to flex under load and lengthen again.
faults.symptom: One height all descent: the legs never shorten or lengthen, and pressure is absorbed by the joints.

faults.diagnosis_test: Check the transition frame from the side: heels under hips is retraction, hips behind heels is collapse.

cues: Feet under your hips, not hips behind your feet.
Ankles close as knees bend.

faults.looks_like: Hips low and back at the transition, light tips, tails washing out.
faults.name: Retraction into the back seat
root_causes: Flexing at the hip only, not ankle, knee and hip together.
Retraction applied after the pressure has gone rather than against it.
faults.symptom: Flexing to release drops the hips behind the heels; the new turn starts late, from the tails.

faults.diagnosis_test: Read the track: sharp entry with a widening exit is an abrupt set; a narrowing arc is a build.

cues: Squeeze the edge on all turn.
Least edge at the top, most at the finish.

faults.looks_like: A sharp bite at the top of the arc, a wide smear below it, an audible scrape.
faults.name: Abrupt edge set
root_causes: Edge angle treated as a position to reach, not a quantity to grow.
Grip sought with the knee instead of built from ankle and hip.
faults.symptom: The edge is stamped on at initiation; the ski grips, then breaks loose below the fall line.

en.goal: Link parallel turns on blue and groomed black with deliberate flexion and extension, a working pole plant, and a tempo held on command.
en.one_line: The parallel turn gains vertical range, a working pole, and a tempo the skier chooses rather than inherits from the hill.
safety_notes: Higher tempo on groomed black means higher closing speed. Corridor drills need an empty run, not a quiet one.
A retraction release that collapses backward is the phantom-foot position under load. Fix ft-07-05 before adding pitch.
A pole caught behind the skier is a shoulder injury; a late plant puts it there.

cues: In a retraction turn: shortest at the end, tallest through the middle.
Lengthen into the new turn, never out of the old one.
skills.description: Pressure peaks in the shaping phase, is released by flexing at the finish, then rebuilt by lengthening into the new turn.
skills.name: Range of motion through the turn
skills.why: No vertical range means pressure has nowhere to go: st-08 chatters, st-13 bumps bounce the skier off line.

cues: Hips across the skis, diagonally down the hill.
Travel with the skis; don't stand up off them.
skills.description: The body moves over and across the skis while the legs stay long. The release for lower speed and gentler pitch.
misconceptions: That cross-over is up-unweighting. Cross-over moves mass across the skis; up-unweighting throws it upward and unloads the ski abruptly.
skills.name: Cross-over release
skills.why: Cross-over still works when pressure is low. A skier who only retracts cannot start a turn on flat, slow terrain.

cues: Suck the feet under you; let the skis cross beneath.
Head travels straight; the legs do the work.
skills.description: Both legs flex so the skis pass under a body travelling a level path. The release for speed and steeper pitch.
skills.name: Retraction release (cross-under)
skills.why: Retraction keeps the skis on the snow where cross-over would launch them. Steeps and bumps are unavailable without it.

cues: Plant ahead of your boot, then ski past it.
Wrist and forearm plant it; the shoulder stays still.
skills.description: A firm plant, downhill and ahead of the boot, that briefly blocks the torso and triggers the release.
skills.name: Blocking pole plant
skills.why: The blocking plant is the mechanism of short swing, steeps and the bump line. A timing touch alone leaves the torso unsupported at tempo.

cues: Count out loud, one number per edge change.
Steeper pitch: same beat, rounder arc.
skills.description: Turns arrive at an interval the skier sets and holds regardless of pitch, changeable on command.
skills.name: Rhythm and tempo as a choice
skills.why: Bumps, trees and gates impose a tempo. A skier with one speed of turn cannot meet it.

cues: Squeeze the edge on; don't stamp it on.
Let it drift, then take the grip back.
skills.description: Edge angle grows through the arc instead of arriving at once, and a skid starts and stops on command.
misconceptions: That skidding is always a fault. It sheds speed where an arc will not fit; the fault is a skid nobody chose.
skills.name: Progressive edge build and deliberate skidding
skills.why: An abrupt edge set breaks loose on st-08 firm snow, and a skid that cannot be chosen cannot be avoided in st-09 steeps.

tactics: Set the tempo from the top of the run, before the pitch sets it for you.
Read the run's natural rhythm from the lift, then ski a different one.
Choose the release before the pitch: cross-over above, retraction where it steepens.

avoid: Bumped runs, which impose a tempo before the skier owns one.
Narrow trails, where turn size cannot be chosen.
Boilerplate: firm snow belongs to st-08.
terrain.ideal_description: A wide blue of 20-25 degrees for acquisition plus one groomed black of 25-30 degrees for testing, both long enough for 30 uninterrupted turns on a consistent pitch.

en.why_it_matters: St-06 produced a correct turn; this stage produces one that repeats under load. Range of motion is how pressure gets managed rather than endured, and the blocking plant is what makes short swing, steeps and bumps possible.

adjustments: 节奏训练很适合这一档：上下幅度还没有身体条件之前，就能用跟着我滑来教。
体重轻使收腿几乎不费力，学到的是一个形状，不是顶着压力的解刃。

criteria_modifications.change: 把 15 厘米折成身高的约 10%；对 130 厘米的孩子，15 厘米是另一回事。
在蓝道上测，12 个弯而不是 24 个：这里是协调关卡，不是压力关卡。

do_not: st-06 的计时点杖自动化之前，不要引入阻挡式插杖。

adjustments: 离心力量下降是这里最直接的限制；陆地训练做没做，决定 ac-07-01 到不到得了。
收腿要摊到多次上雪，别练到力竭——累出来的收腿就是 ft-07-05。

criteria_modifications.change: 24 个弯可拆成两组 12 个；这一关考时机，不考耐力。

adjustments: 越板换刃优先于收腿换刃：冲击更小，在这一档选的速度下就管用。
降量不降标准。三组专注的走廊练习，胜过一整天退化的节奏训练。

criteria_modifications.change: 关节活动范围实测到不了 15 厘米时，12 厘米可判通过；时机要求不变。

adjustments: 平均体重较低，可顶的压力更少，收腿更难感觉到。到更陡的压雪坡上用速度把它建起来。
腘绳肌与单腿离心力量一份工干两件事：造出幅度，也防住 ft-07-05 的机制。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。若靴筒过硬挡住了这个幅度，改的是靴子，不是数字。

adjustments: 收弯处压力大，收腿换刃自然，反倒越板换刃要刻意练。
对这个体重太软的板在收弯处会折掉，症状和 ft-07-06 一样。

zh.core_question: 我能带着上下幅度和会干活的雪杖成节奏地滑吗？

drills.name: 屈腿解刃花环
drills.purpose: 把收腿换刃单独拎出来：换刃发生是因为腿收短了。
drills.setup: 在坡度均匀的蓝道上横切，两腿都站高。
steps: 两腿猛地一屈；板放平，从身体下面滑过去。
在同一对刃上伸长，回到横切，不转弯。
每侧 8 次解刃之后连成弯，脑袋走平线。
drills.success_indicator: 板被卸载而身体没升起；换刃又低又安静。

dose.notes: 每趟一组，至少 10 个弯。

drills.name: 两种解刃对照趟
drills.purpose: 让两种解刃在感觉上分得开，用对照照出上提减压。
drills.setup: 一条长蓝道，下段更陡。
steps: 10 个弯用越板换刃：髋斜着横过雪板，腿保持长。
10 个用收腿换刃：腿收短，身体走平线。再 10 个刻意上提减压。
10 个按坡度自己选解刃，并出声报出来。
drills.success_indicator: 不用提示就能说出刚用的是哪一种解刃。

dose.notes: 每趟一个速率，同一标记段。

drills.name: 节拍器转弯
drills.purpose: 把拍子固定住，让弧线形状吸收坡度变化。
drills.setup: 一条有两段坡度明显不同的道；出声数或用 50–70 bpm 节拍器。
steps: 一整趟一拍一次换刃，出声数。
变陡的地方把弧线横切得更远，不是更早转。
再快 20%、再慢一档，都在同一标记段里数弯。
drills.success_indicator: 同一速率下，标记段弯数重复误差在 1 个弯内。

drills.name: 走廊里的阻挡式插杖
drills.purpose: 在真正需要它的节奏上练插杖：躯干稳定开始要紧处。
drills.setup: 沿落线一条 3–4 米走廊，最好用压雪机的接缝。
steps: 走廊里 12 个小回转，每次收弯把山下侧杖实实插一下。
插在靴子前方、略偏山下，再滑过这根杖。
12 个插杖与 12 个点杖交替；肩始终正对落线。
drills.success_indicator: 在过去会甩上身的节奏上，上身保持安静。

drills.name: 标枪转弯
drills.purpose: 用内板横过外板板头，逼出外板平衡。
drills.setup: 一条中等坡度、没人的蓝道，趁新滑。
steps: 起弯，抬起内板，把它横过外板板头。
整个造型期保持这个交叉；换刃时放下。
每侧 4 个弯，再 4 个正常弯，保持同样髋位。
drills.success_indicator: 内板交叉着离雪，弧线形状和速度不变。

drills.name: 三拍立刃
drills.purpose: 把弧线分成三段刻意的刃角。
drills.setup: 坡度均匀的新压雪面。
steps: 起弯数「一」，刃最少；落线「二」；收弯「三」。
数得不均匀，就是刃被踩上去，不是长出来。
12 个弯出声数，12 个不出声，然后去看雪痕。
drills.success_indicator: 雪痕连续变窄，宽度没有突变。

drills.name: 听口令搓与咬
drills.purpose: 要求漂移在指定点起止，把搓雪变工具。
drills.setup: 坡度均匀的一段，两个参照相距约 20 米。
steps: 到第一个参照，把刃角松到板开始横漂。
到第二个，渐进把刃角建回来，不许压刃刹。
每个方向 6 对，每一对把漂移距离减半。
drills.success_indicator: 漂移在参照前后 2 米内起止，没有溅雪。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从侧面追头盔：锯齿状轨迹是上提减压，平轨迹是两种正确解刃之一。

cues: 横过雪板走，不要从板上往上走。
伸长是进入新弯。

faults.looks_like: 每次换刃都弹一下，板抖或离雪，然后硬着陆。
faults.name: 上提减压
root_causes: 伸展被用来卸载雪板，而不是建立压力。
弯收得太狠，唯一的出口只剩向上。
faults.symptom: 换刃处一记突然的向上伸展把板卸掉；滑行发颠。

faults.diagnosis_test: 12 个弯插杖，再 12 个只点杖。没杖就崩，说明杖在替你滑。

cues: 插在靴子前面，然后滑过它。
用手腕，不用肩。
fix.equipment_check: 杖长：宁可剪短 5 厘米，不要加长。

faults.looks_like: 杖被压弯、内侧肩下沉、插点落在靴子后面。
faults.name: 把雪杖当拐杖
root_causes: st-06 的计时点杖还不可靠，就引入了插杖。
雪杖过长，把插点逼到后面、肩顶上去。
faults.symptom: 雪杖承重、到得晚，或者把肩拽进弯里。

faults.diagnosis_test: 读坡度变化下方的雪痕：均匀却带尖角是毛病，圆弧才是技术。

cues: 同一个拍子，更圆的弧。
先把弯横切完，再取那一拍。

faults.looks_like: 间距均匀的 Z 形雪痕，每弯溅雪，上身随拍子鼓动。
faults.name: 有节奏没形状
root_causes: 拍子靠压平弧线守住，而不是靠改变弯尺寸。
坡变陡时用提早转弯应付，而不是把弯收得更横。
faults.symptom: 弯都踩在拍子上，但每个都是一记刹车；整趟很颠。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从侧面拍，量一个弯里的髋高变化。不到约 10 厘米就是没有幅度。

cues: 收弯最矮，中段最高。
腿收短时把气呼出去。

faults.looks_like: 身体划出一条不变的线，肩紧，换刃处什么也看不见。
faults.name: 一条平线滑到底
root_causes: 上下幅度从没练过；st-06 奖励稳定，人就把它留了下来。
离心力量不足，撑不住在负荷下屈曲再伸长。
faults.symptom: 整趟一个高度：腿不收短也不伸长，压力全被关节硬吃。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从侧面看换刃那一帧：脚跟在髋下面是收腿，髋在脚跟后面是塌。

cues: 脚在髋下面，不是髋在脚后面。
膝一弯，踝就收。

faults.looks_like: 换刃时髋又低又后，板头轻，板尾外滑。
faults.name: 收腿收成后座
root_causes: 只在髋上屈，不是踝、膝、髋一起屈。
收腿是在压力走掉之后做的，不是顶着压力做的。
faults.symptom: 屈腿解刃把髋掉到脚跟后面；新弯起得晚，从板尾起。

faults.diagnosis_test: 读雪痕：入口锐利、出口变宽是突兀压刃；越走越窄才是渐进。

cues: 整个弯都在把刃挤上去。
上端刃最少，收弯刃最多。

faults.looks_like: 弧线上端一口锐利咬合，下面一片宽抹痕，加刮擦声。
faults.name: 突兀压刃
root_causes: 把刃角当一个要到达的位置，不当要长大的量。
抓地是用膝盖找的，不是从踝和髋建的。
faults.symptom: 起弯就把刃踩上去；板先咬住，落线以下崩开。

zh.goal: 在蓝道与压雪黑道上连续做平行式：带刻意的屈伸、能干活的插杖，并按口令守住节奏。
zh.one_line: 平行式拿到了上下幅度、一根干活的雪杖，以及一个自己选、而不是山坡给的节奏。
safety_notes: 压雪黑道上节奏更快，接近速度也更快。走廊练习要空道，不是安静的道。
收腿换刃塌成后座，就是负荷下的幻足姿势。加坡度前先解决 ft-07-05。
雪杖挂在身后是肩部损伤；插得晚就把它放到那里。

cues: 收腿换刃里：收弯最矮，弧线中段最高。
伸长是进入新弯，不是离开旧弯。
skills.description: 压力在造型期到峰值，收弯期靠屈腿释放，再靠伸长进入新弯建立起来。
skills.name: 整个弯里的上下幅度
skills.why: 没有上下幅度，压力无处可去：st-08 抖刃，st-13 的雪包把人弹出线。

cues: 髋横过雪板，斜着往山下走。
跟着板一起走，不要从板上站起来。
skills.description: 身体越过雪板横送过去，双腿保持伸长。低速与缓坡用这一种。
misconceptions: 越板换刃不是上提减压：前者把质量横过雪板送，后者往上抛、并猛地卸掉板。
skills.name: 越板换刃解开
skills.why: 压力低的时候它照样有效。只会收腿的人，在平缓慢速地形上起不了弯。

cues: 把脚吸到身体下面，让板从底下穿过去。
脑袋走直线，活由腿干。
skills.description: 两腿一起屈，让板从走平线的身体下面穿过去。速度与陡坡用这一种。
skills.name: 收腿换刃解开（板过身下）
skills.why: 越板换刃会把板抛起来的地方，收腿换刃让板留在雪上。没有它，陡坡和雪包拿不到。

cues: 插在靴子前面，然后滑过它。
用手腕和前臂插，肩不动。
skills.description: 在靴子前方、略偏山下的一记实插，短暂挡住躯干并触发解刃。
skills.name: 阻挡式插杖
skills.why: 它是短摆、陡坡和雪包线的机制。只有计时点杖，节奏一上来躯干就没支撑。

cues: 出声数，一次换刃一个数。
坡更陡：同一个拍子，更圆的弧。
skills.description: 弯按滑者自己设定并守住的间隔到来，不随坡度变，且能按口令换。
skills.name: 节奏与速率是一种选择
skills.why: 雪包、树林和旗门都会强加节奏。只有一种转弯速率的人接不住。

cues: 把刃挤上去，别踩上去。
让它漂一段，再把抓地要回来。
skills.description: 刃角在弧线里长出来，不是一次到位；搓雪能随口令起、随口令停。
misconceptions: 搓雪并不总是毛病。弧线放不下的地方，它就是泄速的办法；毛病是没人选的那种。
skills.name: 渐进立刃与刻意搓雪
skills.why: 突兀的压刃在 st-08 的硬雪上会崩掉；选不出来的搓雪，在 st-09 的陡坡上躲不开。

tactics: 从坡顶就把节奏定下来，别等坡替你定。
在缆车上读出这条道天然的节奏，然后刻意滑另一个。
先按坡度选解刃：上段越板换刃，变陡处收腿换刃。

avoid: 起包的雪道：滑者还没拿到节奏，它先强加一个。
窄道：弯的尺寸选不了。
冰面：硬雪属于 st-08。
terrain.ideal_description: 一条 20–25 度宽蓝道用来习得，一条 25–30 度压雪黑道用来检验；两条都长到能在均匀坡度上不间断做 30 个弯。

zh.why_it_matters: st-06 造出一个正确的弯；这一级造出在负荷下还能重复的弯。上下幅度决定压力是被管理还是被硬扛；阻挡式插杖是短摆、陡坡和雪包线的机制。

adjustments: Light mass means a child cannot bend a ski enough to grip boilerplate. Teach the tactics and defer the ice gate.
Blunt fleet skis are the commonest reason a child struggles on firm snow; check edges first.

criteria_modifications.change: Deferred until adolescent mass arrives - physics, not skill. Do not substitute softer snow and call it a pass.
The child gives the verdict, an adult does the tune. The gate is the checking habit.

adjustments: Cold-morning stiffness makes the first two runs unrepresentative; warm up on soft snow before any gate.
Balance-specific dryland work returns more than strength work, since this stage is decided by precision.
Fall consequence dominates. Choose short ice pitches with generous run-outs and treat the tactics as the main content.
Slower balance recovery makes the lower-edge-angle answer more important, not less.

criteria_modifications.change: The pitch may be 60 m at 20-24 degrees. The no-slide and no-check standards are unchanged.

adjustments: Medial knee tracking under load shows sharply on firm snow. Where grip fails on one side only, check alignment before cueing.
Lower mass makes ski choice decisive: a ski that cannot be bent cannot grip ice.

criteria_modifications.change: No change to the standard. Where mass makes the pitch unholdable, change the ski or the tune, not the gate.

adjustments: Greater mass gives more grip and less margin for a late edge set: the error arrives faster and harder.
Edges dull faster, and a ski too soft for the skier's mass washes out exactly like ft-08-03.

en.core_question: Does my skiing survive a cold morning on scraped, refrozen snow?

dose.notes: Every firm-snow morning, then weekly.

drills.name: Morning tune-and-check
drills.purpose: Builds the habit of knowing the edge state before the first run.
drills.setup: Skis on a rack, plus a diamond stone and a gummi stone.
steps: Draw a fingernail across the side edge at shovel, underfoot and tail.
Dress any burrs, and confirm tip and tail contact points are still detuned.
Recheck after two runs to learn how fast your edges dull.
drills.success_indicator: You can predict from the check whether the first turn will grip.

drills.name: Hardpack garlands, early edge
drills.purpose: Repeats the top third of the turn where a late edge is punished.
drills.setup: A cold firm blue, shallow traverse angle, early morning.
steps: Release, tip onto the new edges, and grip before the skis reach the fall line.
Return to the traverse without completing the turn; 8 per side.
Steepen the traverse angle, then link every third garland into a full turn.
drills.success_indicator: The ski grips silently above the fall line, with no scrape at engagement.

drills.name: Half-edge turns
drills.purpose: Caps edge angle and makes balance do the work.
drills.setup: A firm moderate pitch with a clear run-out.
steps: Ski medium turns at roughly half your habitual edge angle, no more.
Make the turn work by standing precisely over the outside foot.
12 turns capped, then 12 at habitual angle; compare which held.
drills.success_indicator: Grip improves at the lower edge angle - the whole lesson of the drill.

drills.name: Two-thirds turn
drills.purpose: Forces the direction change to finish by the fall line, leaving nothing to recover.
drills.setup: A firm blue; pick a reference at the fall line for each turn.
steps: Complete two-thirds of the direction change before the fall-line reference.
Below the fall line add nothing: no steering, no edge, just ride the arc out.
15 turns, then inspect the track for smearing below the fall line.
drills.success_indicator: The lower half of each arc needs no correction and leaves a narrowing track.

drills.name: Margin hunting
drills.purpose: Trains surface reading by requiring each turn finish to land on chosen snow.
drills.setup: A scraped afternoon run with visibly varied surface.
steps: Before pushing off, name three places on the pitch where snow has survived.
Ski it finishing every turn on soft snow, using ice only for transitions.
Count the finishes that landed as intended; aim for 8 of 10.
drills.success_indicator: 8 of 10 finishes land on chosen snow, and the run costs less effort.

drills.name: Chatter or washout
drills.purpose: Separates the two ways a ski loses grip, since the fixes are opposite.
drills.setup: A firm pitch you know, with a partner watching from below.
steps: Ski 10 turns and name each loss of grip: a buzzing edge holding its line, or a tail letting go.
For chatter, reduce edge angle and soften the leg. For washout, move forward and load the outside ski earlier.
Apply one fix at a time over 10 turns and record which worked.
drills.success_indicator: You name chatter or washout in the moment and pick the right fix.

drills.name: Aspect-and-clock route plan
drills.purpose: Turns condition reading into a written prediction that can be checked.
drills.setup: A trail map, the overnight low, the forecast high, the grooming report.
steps: The night before, write where you expect firm snow at 9 a.m., noon and 3 p.m., by aspect.
Route the day to follow the softening snow, and name two runs to avoid.
Mark each prediction right or wrong at the end of the day.
drills.success_indicator: Predictions hold on 4 of 5 sampled runs by the fifth day.

faults.diagnosis_test: Fingernail test at shovel, underfoot and tail. If it slides rather than shaves anywhere, stop coaching and tune.

cues: Check the ski before you change the skiing.
Fingernail first, cue second.
fix.equipment_check: Side and base bevel, rock-strike burrs, and whether the detune has crept underfoot.

faults.looks_like: Symmetrical loss of grip with sound movements, and no response to any cue.
faults.name: Blunt edges misdiagnosed as technique
root_causes: Edges never checked, or checked only at the start of a trip.
A detune or bevel set for soft snow and never reset.
faults.symptom: The skier cannot hold on firm snow and works harder each run, while the edge is the real problem.

faults.diagnosis_test: Hardpack garlands (dr-08-02): if grip only arrives once the skis point downhill, the set is late.

cues: Grip above the fall line.
Engage while still crossing the hill.

faults.looks_like: A clean top third with no edge, then a bite and a smear below the fall line.
faults.name: Late edge set
root_causes: Edge engagement used to slow down rather than to steer.
Fear of committing to the fall line on firm snow.
faults.symptom: Grip is demanded at or below the fall line, arrives with a scrape, and never fully takes.

faults.diagnosis_test: Half-edge turns (dr-08-03). If grip improves at half the edge angle, the extra angle was the problem.

cues: Less edge, more balance.
Hip in, chest over the outside ski.

faults.looks_like: Inclination growing through the arc, shoulders dropping inside, then both edges letting go.
faults.name: Answering ice with more edge angle
root_causes: Edge angle believed to be the source of grip, rather than pressure on a balanced ski.
Panic after the first slip, which makes the second worse.
faults.symptom: Losing grip, the skier tips further in, loses the outside ski entirely, and slides.

faults.diagnosis_test: Two-thirds turn (dr-08-04). If the arc cannot be completed above the fall line, the finish was never the problem.

cues: The skid at the bottom was made at the top.
Win the turn early.

faults.looks_like: A loud edge check at each finish, a Z-shaped track, legs cooked by the third run.
faults.name: Fixing the bottom of the turn
root_causes: The skid is felt where it appears, not where it is created.
A late start leaves the direction change incomplete at the fall line.
faults.symptom: The skid is felt at the finish, so more edge and more effort go there every turn.

faults.diagnosis_test: Margin hunting (dr-08-05): count finishes landing on snow named in advance. Under 5 of 10 is reactive.

cues: Ski the white, not the grey.
Name your next three turn finishes.

faults.looks_like: A line ignoring obvious soft margins, the hardest turns on the most scraped snow.
faults.name: Skiing the fall line regardless of surface
root_causes: Line chosen by habit and traffic rather than by surface.
No practice looking more than one turn ahead.
faults.symptom: The skier takes the centre of the run from habit and fights whatever surface is there.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film 10 turns on hardpack and 10 on packed powder. A visible difference in stance is this fault.

cues: Shins on the tongues, especially when it is icy.
Same stance, different snow.
fix.equipment_check: Boot flex when cold, and whether a soft-snow warm-up removes the fault entirely.

faults.looks_like: A wide static stance, hips behind the heels, tails chattering, hands dropping.
faults.name: Defensive stance on firm snow
root_causes: Fear response to a surface that offers no feedback.
Range of motion abandoned under stress, a relapse of ft-07-04.
faults.symptom: On ice the skier widens the stance, stiffens, and retreats behind the feet.

en.goal: Ski round, linked, controlled turns on hardpack and short boilerplate sections, without braking and without widening the stance.
en.one_line: The same parallel turn, proved on snow that gives nothing back: cold hardpack, scraped groomers, refrozen ice.
safety_notes: A fall on boilerplate slides. Choose pitches with a clean run-out and nothing hard below; consequence decides, not steepness.
Helmets matter more here than anywhere else: the mechanism is head impact against ice.
If you slide, spread out, get your feet below you, and do not stand while still moving.

cues: Fingernail across the edge: it should shave, not slide.
If the first turn scrapes, check the ski before the skiing.
skills.description: The skier checks and maintains edge condition before skiing, and can tell from the first turn whether the tune holds.
skills.name: Edge sharpness as a precondition
skills.why: Every other skill here is unmeasurable on a blunt ski, so tune faults masquerade as technique faults.

cues: Grip early and high, before the fall line.
Squeeze the edge on across the whole arc.
skills.description: The edge engages early, above the fall line, and its angle grows through the arc.
skills.name: Progressive edge set above the fall line
skills.why: An abrupt set is what breaks loose on firm snow; st-10 carving is only a fully progressive one.

cues: Less edge, more balance.
Stand quietly on the whole outside foot.
skills.description: On boilerplate the skier reduces edge angle and stands more precisely over the outside ski instead of tipping further.
misconceptions: That ice is skied by getting aggressive. Force finds no purchase on boilerplate; precise balance over the working ski does.
skills.name: Lower edge angle, better balance
skills.why: A skier who answers ice with more edge angle banks, loses the outside ski, and keeps that reflex.

cues: The turn is won above the fall line.
Slow the top down; the bottom looks after itself.
skills.description: The first third of the arc is patient and complete, because the skid felt at the bottom was created at the top.
skills.name: Rounding the top of the turn
skills.why: Firm snow punishes a late turn with an unrecoverable skid, and st-09 steeps punish it harder.

cues: Ski the white, not the grey.
Aim each turn finish at snow you can see.
skills.description: The skier picks a line where snow survives - run edges, shaded strips, the pile beside a groomer seam.
skills.name: Skiing the margins
skills.why: Tactics outperform technique on ice, and reading a surface before committing is what keeps st-14 safe.

cues: East first, south at midday, west last.
Check the overnight low before choosing the first run.
skills.description: The skier predicts where firm snow will be from aspect, sun, overnight temperature and grooming, and routes accordingly.
skills.name: Reading aspect and time of day
skills.why: This converts a bad morning into a good afternoon. Without it, later off-piste stages run on luck.

tactics: First run of a cold morning on easy terrain, as a surface test rather than a warm-up.
Follow the sun: east aspects early, south at midday, west in the afternoon.
On a scraped run, ski the margins and the strips beside groomer seams.

avoid: Long ice pitches with a bad run-out; a slide does not stop where it starts.
Rutted or bumped firm snow, which is st-13 with added consequence.
Crowded runs, where a sliding fall involves someone else.
terrain.ideal_description: A blue of 18-25 degrees skied at 9 a.m. before it softens, plus a groomed black with scraped patches at the fall line. Ideally a run with soft margins to retreat to.

en.why_it_matters: A skier who has only skied soft groomers has an unfalsified technique. Ice defeats intermediates for reasons unrelated to the parallel turn: blunt edges, late edging, and a line chosen without reading the snow.

adjustments: 体重轻，压不弯板，也压不住冰面。战术照教，冰面那关往后放。
租板队伍里的钝刃是孩子在硬雪上吃力的第一号原因；先查刃。

criteria_modifications.change: 推迟到青春期体重到来之后——这是物理问题，不是技术问题。不要拿软雪替代当通过。
判断由孩子给出，磨刃由成年人做。这关考的是查刃这个习惯。

adjustments: 冷早晨僵硬让头两趟不具代表性；任何关卡前先在软雪上热开。
针对平衡的陆地训练回报高于力量：这一级由精准度决定。
摔倒的后果占主导。选短冰坡、宽裕出口，把战术当本级主要内容。
平衡恢复更慢，「降刃角」因此更重要，不是更不重要。

criteria_modifications.change: 坡段可放宽到 60 米、20-24 度。不滑动、不压刃这两条标准不变。

adjustments: 受力时膝盖内扣在硬雪上格外明显。只有一侧抓不住，先查对线。
体重较轻使板的选择成为决定性因素：压不弯的板抓不住冰面。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。若因体重这段坡持不住，改板或改磨刃，不改关卡。

adjustments: 体重大，抓地更强，但晚立刃的容错更小：错误更快更狠。
刃钝得更快；对这个体重过软的板甩尾时，与 ft-08-03 一样。

zh.core_question: 在一个刮净又再冻的冷早晨，我的滑行还站得住吗？

dose.notes: 每个硬雪早晨都做，之后每周一次。

drills.name: 早班查刃
drills.purpose: 养成第一趟之前就知道刃是什么状态的习惯。
drills.setup: 板架上的雪板，一块金刚石锉，一块橡胶石。
steps: 指甲横刮侧刃的板头段、脚下段、板尾段。
磨掉毛刺，确认板头板尾接触点仍是钝的。
滑两趟后再查一次，摸清自己的刃钝得多快。
drills.success_indicator: 查完就能预判第一个弯咬不咬得住。

drills.name: 硬雪花环：提前立刃
drills.purpose: 反复练弯的上三分之一：硬雪最不容忍晚立刃。
drills.setup: 低温硬实的蓝道，横切角度浅，清早。
steps: 解刃、两脚同时倒上新刃，板头到落线前就咬住。
不把弯做完，回到横切；每侧 8 次。
逐步加大横切角度，每第三个花环接成完整的弯。
drills.success_indicator: 落线以上刃安静地咬住，那一刻没有搓雪声。

drills.name: 半刃角转弯
drills.purpose: 给刃角设上限，逼平衡去干活。
drills.setup: 一段硬实的中等坡度，出口清楚。
steps: 用习惯刃角的一半左右滑中回转，不许更多。
靠精准站在外脚上方，让这个弯自己成立。
先限角滑 12 个弯，再用习惯刃角滑 12 个，比哪组抓得住。
drills.success_indicator: 刃角更小反而抓得更牢——这就是本练习的全部。

drills.name: 三分之二转弯
drills.purpose: 把方向改变逼到落线之前完成，下半段就没什么可救。
drills.setup: 硬实的蓝道；每弯在落线处先找一个参照点。
steps: 在落线参照点之前完成方向改变的三分之二。
落线以下什么都不加：不转向、不加刃，让弧线走完。
滑 15 个弯，看雪痕在落线以下有没有被抹开。
drills.success_indicator: 下半段不需要修正，雪痕越走越细。

drills.name: 找雪
drills.purpose: 要求每个收弯都落在选定的雪上，以此练读雪面。
drills.setup: 一条下午被刮过、雪面明显参差的道。
steps: 出发前先在这段坡上点出三处还留着雪的地方。
滑下来，每弯都收在软雪上，冰面只用来过渡。
数收弯落在预定位置的次数；目标 10 次里 8 次。
drills.success_indicator: 10 次收弯里 8 次落在选定的雪上，整趟明显省力。

drills.name: 抖刃还是甩尾
drills.purpose: 把丢抓地的两种方式分开，因为解法正好相反。
drills.setup: 一段你熟悉的硬实坡，同伴在下方看。
steps: 滑 10 个弯，每次丢抓地当场报出来：刃嗡嗡响但线还在，还是板尾放开。
抖刃就降刃角放软腿；甩尾就往前移、更早压外板。
一次只用一种解法，各滑 10 个弯，记下哪种管用。
drills.success_indicator: 能当场叫出「抖刃」或「甩尾」，并选对解法。

drills.name: 坡向与钟点路线计划
drills.purpose: 把读雪况变成写下来、能被核对的预判。
drills.setup: 雪道图、昨夜最低温、预报最高温、压雪报告。
steps: 头一晚按坡向写下 9 点、正午、下午 3 点硬雪在哪里。
路线排成跟着雪变软走，点出两条要避开的道。
收工时逐条标记预判对了还是错了。
drills.success_indicator: 到第五天，抽查的 5 趟里有 4 趟预判成立。

faults.diagnosis_test: 三段刃都做指甲测试。任何一处是滑过去而不是刮下屑，就去磨刃。

cues: 先查板，再改滑行。
先指甲，后口令。
fix.equipment_check: 侧刃角与底刃角、撞石毛刺、去刃有没有蔓延到脚下段。

faults.looks_like: 两侧对称地丢抓地，动作没毛病，口令全不起作用。
faults.name: 钝刃被误诊成技术问题
root_causes: 从来不查刃，或只在行程第一天查过一次。
去刃与刃角按软雪设的，之后没改回来。
faults.symptom: 硬雪上抓不住，越滑越用力，问题其实在刃上。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做硬雪花环（dr-08-02）：只有板头指向山下才抓得住，就是晚了。

cues: 落线以上就咬住。
还在横切山坡时就把刃接上。

faults.looks_like: 上三分之一干净但没有刃，落线以下一口咬住、随即抹开。
faults.name: 立刃太晚
root_causes: 把咬刃当减速手段，不当转向手段。
在硬雪上不敢把身体交给落线。
faults.symptom: 到落线甚至更下面才要抓地，抓地伴着搓响来，始终没咬实。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做半刃角转弯（dr-08-03）。刃角减半反而抓得更牢，多出来的刃角就是问题。

cues: 刃少一点，平衡多一点。
髋进弯内，胸口压在外板上。

faults.looks_like: 内倾越走越大，肩往弯内掉，两条刃一起放开。
faults.name: 用更大刃角回答冰面
root_causes: 以为抓地来自刃角，不是来自平衡好的板上的压力。
第一次打滑之后慌了，第二次更糟。
faults.symptom: 一丢抓地就往里再倒，结果彻底丢掉外板，滑出去。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做三分之二转弯（dr-08-04）。弧线在落线以上做不完，收弯就不是问题。

cues: 下面那段搓雪，是上面造出来的。
弯要早早赢下来。

faults.looks_like: 每次收弯一声响亮压刃，雪痕是 Z 形，第三趟腿就废。
faults.name: 在弯的下半段修弯
root_causes: 在哪里感觉到搓雪，就以为是在哪里产生的。
起弯晚，到落线时方向改变还没做完。
faults.symptom: 搓雪在收弯处被感觉到，于是每弯都在那里加刃加力。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做找雪（dr-08-05）：数收弯落在指名雪上的次数。10 次里不到 5 次即被动读雪。

cues: 滑白的，不滑灰的。
把接下来三个收弯点报出来。

faults.looks_like: 线无视两侧的软雪，最难的几个弯偏落在刮得最净的雪上。
faults.name: 不看雪面、只走落线
root_causes: 线按习惯和人流选，不按雪面选。
从来没练过往前看超过一个弯。
faults.symptom: 习惯性走雪道正中间，跟脚下的任何雪面较劲。

faults.diagnosis_test: 硬雪上拍 10 个弯、压实粉雪上拍 10 个。站姿肉眼看得出差别就是它。

cues: 小腿贴住靴舌，越结冰越要贴。
换雪不换站姿。
fix.equipment_check: 低温下靴子的实际硬度；先在软雪热开后毛病是否整个消失。

faults.looks_like: 宽而僵死的站姿，髋落在后跟之后，板尾抖，手往下掉。
faults.name: 硬雪上的防御性站姿
root_causes: 对不给回馈的雪面的恐惧反应。
一紧张就交出全部活动范围，是 ft-07-04 的复发。
faults.symptom: 一上冰面就撑宽站姿、绷硬身体、退到脚后面。

zh.goal: 在硬雪和短段冰面上做出圆润连贯的可控转弯，不靠刹车，不把站姿撑宽。
zh.one_line: 同一个平行式转弯，拿到不给回馈的雪面上验一遍：低温硬雪、刮净的压雪道、冰面。
safety_notes: 在冰面上摔了会一路滑。挑出口干净、下方无硬物的坡；定后果的是出口，不是坡度。
头盔在这里比任何地方都重要：机制就是头撞冰面。
一旦滑出去，四肢摊开、脚转到身体下方，还在动就不要站起来。

cues: 指甲横着刮过刃：该刮下屑，不该滑过去。
第一个弯就搓，先查板，再查滑行。
skills.description: 上雪前查刃并保养，第一个弯就能判断这套磨刃顶不顶。
skills.name: 刃口锋利是前置条件
skills.why: 板一钝，本级其余技能全测不出来，装备毛病就伪装成技术毛病。

cues: 早咬、高咬，落线之前就咬住。
整条弧线一路把刃拧紧。
skills.description: 刃在落线以上就咬住，刃角随弧线一路增大，不是某一刻压下去。
skills.name: 落线以上渐进立刃
skills.why: 硬雪上崩掉的就是「一记压刃」；st-10 的刻滑只是把它做到全程渐进。

cues: 刃少一点，平衡多一点。
整只外脚踩实，安静地站上去。
skills.description: 上了冰面就收小刃角，把身体更准地放在外板上方，不是往里立。
misconceptions: 以为冰面要靠「凶一点」滑。力气在冰上抓不到东西，抓得住的是受力板上的精准平衡。
skills.name: 降刃角，提平衡
skills.why: 用「再立一点」回答冰面的人会整体内倾、丢掉外板，反射还会留着。

cues: 弯是在落线以上赢下来的。
上半段慢慢做，下半段自己会好。
skills.description: 弧线前三分之一要有耐心、要完整；收弯处的搓雪是在开头造的。
skills.name: 把弯的上半段做圆
skills.why: 硬雪对起弯晚的惩罚是一段救不回来的搓雪；st-09 的陡坡罚得更重。

cues: 滑白的，不滑灰的。
每弯都收在你看得见的雪上。
skills.description: 线选在雪还活着的地方：雪道边缘、背阴带、压雪机接缝旁的雪垄。
skills.name: 走雪道两侧
skills.why: 冰面上战术胜过技术；「下去之前先读雪面」正是 st-14 安全的前提。

cues: 先东坡，正午南坡，最后西坡。
选第一趟前先看昨夜最低温。
skills.description: 从坡向、日照、夜间低温和压雪作业推断硬雪在哪里，据此排路线。
skills.name: 读坡向与时间
skills.why: 这一手把糟糕的早上换成好下午。没有它，后面的野雪级别靠运气。

tactics: 冷早晨第一趟放在简单地形上，当雪面测试，不是热身。
跟着太阳走：清早东坡，正午南坡，下午西坡。
被刮净的道，走两侧和压雪机接缝旁的雪垄。

avoid: 出口不佳的长冰坡：滑倒的地方不是停住的地方。
起车辙、起包的硬雪：那是 st-13，还附赠后果。
拥挤的雪道：一次滑倒会带上别人。
terrain.ideal_description: 18-25 度的蓝道，早上 9 点趁它还没软就滑；再加一条落线处有刮净斑块的压雪黑道。最好两侧还留有软雪可以退。

zh.why_it_matters: 只滑软压雪的人技术从未被证伪。冰面拦住中级滑雪者的原因常与平行式无关：刃钝、立刃晚、不读雪面。

adjustments: Light skiers pivot easily and hold a corridor badly. Test ac-09-02 on a blue: same mechanics, very different consequence if the slip runs away.
Short radius arrives naturally at this age; counteracting does not. Use the corridor and the tracks as evidence, not verbal correction.

criteria_modifications.change: Count aloud instead of a metronome, and 12 turns rather than 20. Speed-hold unchanged.

do_not: Do not run pivot slips with a child on crowded terrain; a slipping ski leaves no steering to avoid anyone.

adjustments: Hip rotation range, not effort, is usually the limiter on counteracting. Ten minutes of mobility before the first run moves ac-09-04 more than any cue.
Short-swing sets are anaerobic. Spread tempo work across sessions rather than drilling to fatigue.

criteria_modifications.change: The 20 turns may be split into two sets of 10 with a 60-second rest, same tempo and speed-hold.

adjustments: Volume down, quality up: six clean pivot slips beat twenty degraded ones.
A shorter, lighter ski pivots at a lower edge angle and brings the corridor into reach. An optimization, not a concession.

criteria_modifications.change: 50-60 plants per minute is acceptable; corridor width and speed-hold do not change.

adjustments: A narrower heel with higher calf volume commonly leaves heel lift, which makes a pivot feel vague and a plant feel late. Solve heel hold first.
Where the knee tracks inward as the counter is applied, treat it as cuff alignment and canting rather than adding cues.

criteria_modifications.change: No change to the standard. Where lower mass makes groomed black hard, change ski length, not corridor width.

en.core_question: Can I choose my turn size, and hold it through rolls, pitch changes and traffic?

dose.notes: 32 turns minimum per run.

drills.name: Corridor ladder, four widths
drills.purpose: Shrinks the corridor until shape, not tempo, has to change.
drills.setup: A fall line and four widths: 12 m, 8 m, 5 m, 3 m.
steps: Ski 8 turns at each width, widest to narrowest, without stopping.
Hold one tempo; only the corridor changes.
Repeat narrowest to widest; note which width degrades first.
drills.success_indicator: All four widths round, at one speed.

drills.name: Sideslip to quarter pivot
drills.purpose: Builds the pivot inside the sideslip, before any 180.
steps: Sideslip across the hill, chest downhill, hands level.
Pivot the tips 45 degrees toward the fall line and back, without gripping.
Then pivot 90 degrees and hold the slip.
Stop the slip on command before continuing.
drills.success_indicator: Direction changes with no change in descent speed.

dose.notes: Two runs blue, one groomed black once blue is clean.

drills.name: Pivot slip corridor
drills.purpose: The centrepiece: 180-degree pivots in a corridor barely wider than the skis.
drills.setup: A 2 m corridor down a groomed fall line, marked by a groomer seam.
steps: Sideslip in the corridor, chest facing straight downhill.
Pivot 180 degrees, then keep slipping.
Plant the downhill pole at each pivot to block the torso.
Six pivots before stopping; corridor width is the test.
drills.success_indicator: Six pivots, no net sideways drift, chest in the fall line.

dose.notes: One garland set each direction first.

drills.name: Hands-on-hips counteracting garlands
drills.purpose: Isolates pelvis counteracting from shoulder twist by removing the arms.
drills.setup: Hands on the hip bones, poles left at the side.
steps: Ski short garlands, feeling the hip bones turn toward the outside ski tip.
Notice how much rotational range is left at each finish.
Ski a full run keeping that hip feel, then take the poles back.
drills.success_indicator: Range still available at the finish; no hip check.

dose.notes: 20 turns minimum at each tempo.

drills.name: Short swing on a count
drills.purpose: Fixes tempo externally, so braking cannot hide in the rhythm.
drills.setup: Count aloud, or a metronome at 60-70 beats per minute.
steps: Ski short turns in a 3 m corridor, one plant per beat.
Hold the tempo 20 turns; speed must neither build nor fall.
Drop to 50 beats and lengthen the arc, same corridor.
drills.success_indicator: A metronomic plant and no speed change across 20 turns.

dose.notes: Count out loud.

drills.name: Hold the size over the roll
drills.purpose: Exposes the radius growth that happens unnoticed at every pitch change.
steps: Set a 5 m corridor; count the ten turns before the lip and ten after.
Match the counts. A lower count means the radius grew.
Move the hips forward before the lip so the tips stay engaged.
drills.success_indicator: Equal counts above and below the lip, same speed.

drills.name: Called sizes in traffic
drills.purpose: Puts size selection under the pressure of other people.
drills.setup: A busy blue at midday, partner behind, calling sizes.
steps: The partner calls short, medium or long every 6-8 turns.
The change happens on the next turn, with no preparatory turn.
The skier names each hazard being planned around.
drills.success_indicator: Size changes within one turn of the call, no speed spike.

faults.diagnosis_test: 20 short turns on a count (dr-09-05). If speed keeps falling, every turn is a brake.

cues: Round, even at three metres.
Release, do not throw.

faults.looks_like: Sharp corners and a spray at every finish; a Z-shaped track.
faults.name: Edge-check chain instead of short turns
root_causes: Pressure dumped sideways at the finish rather than released.
Short radius attempted above the speed the skier can shape.
faults.symptom: Short turns sound like scraping; speed drops every turn.

faults.diagnosis_test: Hands-on-hips garlands (dr-09-04). If rhythm improves without arms, the shoulders were steering.

cues: Face the next turn.
Plant ahead of the boot.

faults.looks_like: Shoulders leading, outside arm thrown across, alternating hip checks.
faults.name: Shoulder rotation returning under tempo
root_causes: Counteracting treated as stillness rather than movement.
Tempo above the leg rotation the skier owns.
faults.symptom: The torso twists into every turn and rhythm dies after six.

faults.diagnosis_test: Quarter pivots (dr-09-02). If the skis grip at 45 degrees, they never go flat.

cues: Flat to turn, edge to stop.
Both feet spin together.

faults.looks_like: A widening arc at each pivot, and a diagonal rather than vertical track.
faults.name: Pivot that hooks
root_causes: The skis never go flat, so an edge catches mid-pivot.
Pivot led with the outside ski, building a platform to turn on.
faults.symptom: The pivot becomes a small turn; the skier leaves the corridor.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film 20 turns from the side. A basket at or behind the boot toe is late.

cues: Hands in front, plant ahead.
Block, do not lean.
fix.equipment_check: Pole length: 5 cm shorter fixes more late planters than any cue.

faults.looks_like: A basket landing at or behind the boot, torso rolling toward it.
faults.name: Pole plant carrying weight
root_causes: The plant used as support rather than as a rotational block.
Hands drifted back, so the plant can only land late.
faults.symptom: The plant is late and heavy; the inside shoulder dips.

faults.diagnosis_test: Count turns ten above and ten below a lip (dr-09-06). A drop over two is this fault.

cues: Hips forward before the lip.
Same corridor over the roll.

faults.looks_like: Turn count dropping below the lip; hips behind the boots after it.
faults.name: Radius growing at the pitch change
root_causes: Fore/aft not moved until after the terrain arrives.
Defensive response to the sight line vanishing over a convex roll.
faults.symptom: The chosen size survives uniform pitch and opens at every roll.

faults.diagnosis_test: Pivot slips (dr-09-03). A chest that leaves the fall line by the second pivot is locked, not separated.

cues: Turn the pelvis, breathe out.
Reset the counter every finish.

faults.looks_like: A rigid square torso facing across the hill by the third turn.
faults.name: Locked torso mistaken for separation
root_causes: Separation taught as a position to hold, not a movement to repeat.
No counter at the finish, so the range is spent and never reset.
faults.symptom: The skier believes the torso is quiet; on video it turns a beat late.

en.goal: Produce short, medium and long radius on command in a marked corridor, hold a chosen size through terrain change and traffic, and pivot the skis 180 degrees inside a sideslip.
en.one_line: Turn size becomes a decision, and it survives rolls, pitch changes, cat tracks and other people.
safety_notes: A slipping ski accelerates and cannot be steered around anyone. Check below before every pivot-slip set.
Short-radius skiing holds you in the fall line on a predictable rhythm: easy to overtake, easy to hit. Stay to one side.
Cat tracks combine low speed, high traffic and a narrow corridor. Stopping on one is how collisions happen — see mod-safety.

cues: Name the size out loud before you push off.
Stay in the corridor, not in your comfort.
skills.description: Radius is named before the run and held for a stated count. Corridor width sets it, not terrain.
misconceptions: Short radius is a narrower corridor, not faster feet. Tempo is a separate variable.
skills.name: Turn size on command
skills.why: Steeps, glades and bumps each impose a radius. One radius means one line.

cues: Chest downhill, feet spin underneath.
Flat to turn, edge to stop.
skills.description: From a controlled sideslip the skis pivot 180 degrees beneath a chest that stays facing downhill.
misconceptions: A hop is not a pivot. A hop means the skis were still gripping.
skills.name: Pivot slip
skills.why: The gate to st-12. A 35-degree face has no room to shape an arc, only to pivot.

cues: Face the next turn, not the skis.
Belly button toward the outside ski tip.
skills.description: The pelvis actively turns to face outside the arc, so the legs keep rotational range at the finish.
misconceptions: Separation is not stillness. Held still, the torso is dragged around by the third turn.
skills.name: Counteracting as active separation
skills.why: A merely quiet torso runs out of leg rotation by the fall line. Short turns become hip checks.

cues: Plant ahead of the boot, then release.
The plant starts a turn, not finishes one.
skills.description: The st-07 blocking plant held on the beat at 60-70 turns a minute, one plant per turn, without the arm swinging.
skills.name: Plant timing at short-radius tempo
skills.why: Without the block the torso follows the skis and rhythm collapses above sixty turns a minute.

cues: Same corridor over the lip.
Move with the hill before it arrives.
skills.description: Rolls, cat tracks and traffic change pressure and sight lines, not the corridor. Fore/aft moves early.
skills.name: Holding a size through terrain change
skills.why: Every stage above is terrain variation. A radius that grows at each roll cannot hold a line in trees.

cues: Round, even at three metres wide.
Release the pressure, do not throw it.
skills.description: A shaped short turn keeps steering and releases pressure; an edge check sets and dumps.
misconceptions: Short swing is a rhythm, not a braking trick. Speed still comes from shape.
skills.name: Shaped short turn versus edge check
skills.why: Braking at forty turns a minute fails on the steeps, which give no room to brake.

tactics: Read the corridor from the chairlift, then ski the size you read, not the size you feel like.
Traffic dictates radius more often than pitch. On a busy run, short and predictable beats long and fast.
Cat tracks are where intermediates fall: enter slow, hands forward, look uphill before rejoining.

avoid: Crowded runs for pivot-slip work; a slipping ski cannot avoid anyone.
Ungroomed or bumped terrain, which hides turn size.
Boilerplate, where the pivot becomes survival, not skill.
terrain.ideal_description: A groomed 22-28 degree pitch with a visible fall line, one distinct roll and a cat-track exit. Long enough for 40 turns, quiet enough for pivot slips.

en.why_it_matters: The last rung of tier 2, and the one that decides whether the steeps are reachable. The pivot slip is the only descent on a face too narrow to shape an arc on. It looks remedial and gates everything above.

adjustments: 体重轻的人枢转容易，守走廊难。ac-09-02 放蓝道测：机制一样，后果差得远。
这个年龄小回转自己会来，反向不会。用走廊和雪痕当证据，不靠嘴。

criteria_modifications.change: 出声数拍代替节拍器，弯数由 20 改为 12。守速那条不变。

do_not: 不要带孩子在人多地形上做枢转侧滑；侧滑中的板没有余地避让。

adjustments: 限制反向的通常是髋旋转范围，不是用力。第一趟前十分钟活动度练习，对 ac-09-04 胜过口令。
短摆组是无氧的。节奏训练摊到多次上雪，别练到力竭。

criteria_modifications.change: 20 个弯可拆成两组 10 个、中间歇 60 秒，节奏与守速不变。

adjustments: 降量保质：六次干净的枢转侧滑胜过二十次退化的。
更短更轻的板在更小刃角上就能枢转，把走廊拉进可及范围。是优化，不是让步。

criteria_modifications.change: 每分钟 50-60 次插杖可以接受；走廊宽度与守速不变。

adjustments: 后跟窄而小腿围大，常留后跟提空，枢转发虚、插杖显晚。先解决后跟锁定。
做反向时膝盖往内走，按靴筒对线与楔片处理，不叠口令。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。若因体重较轻压雪黑道吃力，改板长，不改走廊。

zh.core_question: 我能选定转弯尺寸，并在坡沿、坡度变化和人流里守住吗？

dose.notes: 每趟至少 32 个转弯。

drills.name: 四档走廊阶梯
drills.purpose: 把走廊逼窄，直到必须改形状而不是改节奏。
drills.setup: 一条落线加四种宽度：12 米、8 米、5 米、3 米。
steps: 每档滑 8 个弯，由宽到窄，中间不停。
节奏保持一个，只有走廊在变。
再由窄到宽一遍，记下哪档最先崩。
drills.success_indicator: 四档都圆润，速度只有一个。

drills.name: 侧滑中的四分之一枢转
drills.purpose: 先把枢转建在侧滑里，再谈 180 度。
steps: 横向侧滑过山坡，胸口朝山下，两手齐平。
把板头朝落线枢转 45 度再转回来，全程不咬刃。
再枢转 90 度，把侧滑保持住。
继续之前先按口令把侧滑停掉。
drills.success_indicator: 方向变了，下滑速度没变。

dose.notes: 蓝道两趟；干净了再上压雪黑道一趟。

drills.name: 枢转侧滑走廊
drills.purpose: 本级核心：在只比板宽一点的走廊里做 180 度枢转。
drills.setup: 顺压雪落线划一条 2 米走廊，用接缝当边。
steps: 在走廊里侧滑，胸口正对山下。
枢转 180 度，然后继续侧滑。
每次枢转都用山下侧雪杖插一下，挡住上身。
连做六次再停；考的是走廊宽度。
drills.success_indicator: 六次枢转，无横向净漂移，胸口留在落线上。

dose.notes: 先每个方向各做一组花环。

drills.name: 手扶髋骨的反向花环
drills.purpose: 把手臂拿掉，才能把骨盆反向从扭肩里分出来。
drills.setup: 两手扶住髋骨，雪杖放在道边。
steps: 滑短花环，感觉髋骨朝外板板头转。
注意每次收弯还剩多少余量。
带着这个髋部感觉滑完一趟，再把雪杖拿回。
drills.success_indicator: 收弯时还有余量，不出现坐胯。

dose.notes: 每种节奏至少 20 个弯。

drills.name: 数拍短摆
drills.purpose: 把节奏钉在外部，刹车就藏不进去。
drills.setup: 出声数拍，或用节拍器设 60-70 拍每分钟。
steps: 在 3 米走廊里滑小回转，一拍一杖。
节奏守住 20 个弯；速度不许涨也不许掉。
降到 50 拍，把弧线放长，走廊不变。
drills.success_indicator: 插杖像节拍器，20 个弯里速度没变。

dose.notes: 出声数。

drills.name: 过坡沿守尺寸
drills.purpose: 把每次坡度变化处没察觉的半径变大揪出来。
steps: 定一条 5 米走廊；数坡沿前十个弯和后十个弯。
两边个数要对上。个数少了就是半径变大。
坡沿之前先送髋，让板头保持咬雪。
drills.success_indicator: 坡沿上下个数相同，速度也相同。

drills.name: 人流中听令换尺寸
drills.purpose: 把尺寸选择放到别人造成的压力下做。
drills.setup: 正午人多的蓝道，同伴在后面喊尺寸。
steps: 同伴每 6-8 个弯喊一次小、中或大。
下一个弯就换过来，不许先滑过渡弯。
滑雪者把正在避让的每一个隐患报出来。
drills.success_indicator: 听到口令一个弯之内换完，速度不冒尖。

faults.diagnosis_test: 数拍做 20 个小回转（dr-09-05）。速度一直往下掉，每弯都是刹车。

cues: 三米宽也要画圆。
放掉，不要甩掉。

faults.looks_like: 每次收弯一个尖角、一片雪雾；雪痕是 Z 形。
faults.name: 一串压刃冒充小回转
root_causes: 收弯时压力被横向甩掉，不是被放掉。
在自己造不出形状的速度上硬做小回转。
faults.symptom: 小回转听着是搓雪声，速度每弯都掉一点。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做手扶髋骨花环（dr-09-04）。没手臂节奏反而变好，就是肩在转向。

cues: 朝着下一个弯。
插在靴子前面。

faults.looks_like: 肩先于板走，外侧手臂横甩，左右交替坐胯。
faults.name: 加速节奏下上身旋转回潮
root_causes: 把反向当成不动，而不是一个动作。
节奏高过了自己真正拥有的腿部转动。
faults.symptom: 每个弯都用躯干扭进去，节奏到第六个弯就死。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做四分之一枢转（dr-09-02）。板在 45 度上就咬住，说明它没放平。

cues: 放平才转得动，立刃才停得住。
两只脚一起转。

faults.looks_like: 每次枢转弧线越张越开，雪痕是斜线不是竖线。
faults.name: 枢转挂住变成转弯
root_causes: 板始终没有真正放平，枢转中途被刃咬住。
用外板领着枢转，等于造了一个转弯的平台。
faults.symptom: 枢转变成一个小弯，人滑出走廊。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从侧面拍 20 个弯。杖篮落在靴尖处或更后就是晚。

cues: 手在前面，杖插前面。
是挡，不是靠。
fix.equipment_check: 杖长：短 5 厘米治好的晚插杖比任何口令都多。

faults.looks_like: 杖篮落在靴子处或更后，上身朝它倒过去。
faults.name: 插杖承重
root_causes: 把插杖当支撑用，不当旋转阻挡用。
手漂到后面去了，杖只可能插晚。
faults.symptom: 插杖又晚又重，内侧肩往下掉。

faults.diagnosis_test: 数坡沿上下各十个弯（dr-09-06）。掉超过两个就是它。

cues: 坡沿之前先送髋。
过坡沿，同一条走廊。

faults.looks_like: 坡沿以下弯数变少；过坡沿髋落在靴子后面。
faults.name: 坡度变化处半径变大
root_causes: 前后调整等地形到了才做。
凸起坡沿上视线消失，身体反应是防御。
faults.symptom: 均匀坡度上尺寸守得住，到坡沿就张开。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做枢转侧滑（dr-09-03）。胸口到第二次枢转就离开落线，是锁死不是分离。

cues: 转骨盆，同时呼气。
每次收弯都把反向重置一次。

faults.looks_like: 上身板正僵硬，到第三个弯已朝着横切方向。
faults.name: 把锁死的上身当成分离
root_causes: 分离被当成要保持的姿势，不是要重复的动作。
收弯不做反向，余量用光就再没有重置。
faults.symptom: 自己以为上身很安静；录像里它总慢半拍转过去。

zh.goal: 划定走廊里按口令给出小、中、大回转，地形变化与人流中守住尺寸，并能在侧滑中把双板枢转 180 度。
zh.one_line: 转弯尺寸变成一个决定，而且在坡沿、坡度变化、猫道和人流里守得住。
safety_notes: 侧滑中的板会加速，绕不开任何人。每组枢转侧滑前先看下方。
小回转把人按在落线上、节奏又规整：好被追上，也好被撞上。靠一侧。
猫道把低速、高人流和窄走廊凑在一起。停在猫道上就是碰撞来源——见 mod-safety。

cues: 出发前把尺寸喊出来。
待在走廊里，不是待在舒服里。
skills.description: 出发前先报半径，按个数守住。定尺寸的是走廊宽度，不是地形。
misconceptions: 小回转是走廊更窄，不是脚更快。节奏是另一个变量。
skills.name: 按口令给出转弯尺寸
skills.why: 陡坡、树林、雪包各自逼出一种半径。只有一种半径就只有一条线。

cues: 胸口朝山下，脚在身下转。
放平才转得动，立刃才停得住。
skills.description: 在可控侧滑中把双板原地转过 180 度，胸口始终朝山下。
misconceptions: 跳起来不算枢转。要跳，说明板还咬着雪。
skills.name: 枢转侧滑
skills.why: 通往 st-12 的门。35 度的坡面没有空间画弧线，只有空间枢转。

cues: 朝着下一个弯，不是朝着板。
肚脐对准外板板头。
skills.description: 骨盆主动转向弯外，让腿到收弯还剩着可用的转动余量。
misconceptions: 分离不是不动。摆着不动，第三个弯上身就被板拖走。
skills.name: 反向：主动做出来的分离
skills.why: 上身只是「安静」，到落线腿的转动就用光，小回转变成一串坐胯。

cues: 插在靴子前面，然后就放开。
插杖是起一个弯，不是收一个弯。
skills.description: 把 st-07 的阻挡式插杖放到每分钟 60-70 个弯上：一弯一杖，踩着拍子，不甩臂。
skills.name: 小回转节奏下的插杖时机
skills.why: 没有阻挡，上身就跟着板走，节奏一过六十就崩。

cues: 过坡沿，同一条走廊。
地形还没到，人先跟上去。
skills.description: 坡沿、猫道、人流改变的是压力和视线，不是走廊。前后调整早于地形。
skills.name: 地形变化中守住尺寸
skills.why: 上面每一级都是地形变化。半径到坡沿就变大，树林里就守不住线。

cues: 三米宽也要画圆。
把压力放掉，不要甩出去。
skills.description: 造型小回转一直在转向、把压力放掉；压刃止速是压住再横向泄。
misconceptions: 短摆是一种节奏，不是刹车花招。速度仍来自形状。
skills.name: 造型小回转与压刃止速的区别
skills.why: 每分钟四十个弯的刹车在陡坡上不成立：陡坡不给刹车空间。

tactics: 从缆车上把走廊读出来，滑你读到的尺寸。
决定半径的常是人流，不是坡度。人多的道上，小而可预测胜过大而快。
猫道是中级滑雪者摔得最多的地方：慢进、手在前、汇入前上看。

avoid: 拥挤的雪道不做枢转侧滑：正在侧滑的板躲不开任何人。
非压雪或起包地形：它会把转弯尺寸藏起来。
冰面：枢转在那里变成求生，不是技术。
terrain.ideal_description: 22-28 度的压雪坡，落线看得清，带一处明显坡沿，出口接一段猫道。够滑 40 个弯，且安静到可以做枢转侧滑。

zh.why_it_matters: 第二层级的最后一格，也决定陡坡能不能到手。枢转侧滑是窄到画不出弧线的坡面上唯一的下法：像补课，却是上面级别的门。

adjustments: Carving needs mass to bend a ski, and a 30 kg skier cannot bend one at any edge angle. Clean-looking tracks from a light child are tipping practice, not this stage.
Run the railroad-track work and the track inspection, which are age-appropriate and transfer directly, then postpone the gates.
do_not: Do not put a light child on a long, stiff adult ski to make carving possible.

adjustments: Adult mass arrives here and carving becomes available, which makes this the band most likely to self-award ac-10-01 and ac-10-02.
Enforce track inspection and video. A teenager carving a blue at speed with a banked body is the classic serious-fall profile.
Shorter, softer, lighter skis bend at lower speed, bringing carving into reach where a fall is survivable.
Volume down, standard unchanged: four inspected arcs beat sixteen unexamined ones.

criteria_modifications.change: The 8 arcs may be split into two sets of 4 with a climb back between. The 2 cm standard does not change.

adjustments: For a lighter skier a shorter, softer ski is an upgrade: a ski that cannot be bent cannot carve. Choose by mass.
Where the knee tracks inward at high edge angle, treat it as cuff alignment and canting before adding cues.

criteria_modifications.change: No change. If lower mass makes 12 arcs hard to sustain, change the ski, not the standard.

adjustments: A ski too soft for the skier's mass folds mid-arc and washes out, with symptoms identical to ft-10-01. Check the ski before coaching the fault.
Release values scale with mass and must be set by a technician; carving loads a binding harder than earlier stages.

en.core_question: Can I leave two clean lines instead of two smears?

dose.notes: Track inspection after every run, all arcs.

drills.name: Railroad tracks ladder
drills.purpose: Builds edge angle in steps while the tracks report every degree of steering added.
drills.setup: First corduroy, a gentle pitch, nobody above you.
steps: From a straight run with flat skis, tip both feet one way and let the skis cross the hill.
Do not steer and do not complete the turn; tip back the other way.
Ski four passes at rising edge angle: shin, knee, hip, then as far as the arc holds.
Stop and inspect the tracks after every pass. Inspection is the drill.
drills.success_indicator: Two pencil-width lines with no widening at the tail, at every angle.

dose.notes: One filmed run per session.

drills.name: Early edge change on a count
drills.purpose: Moves the edge change above the fall line by tying it to a place, not a feeling.
steps: Ski medium arcs and say 'now' at the moment both skis are flat.
The word must land while the tips still point across the hill.
Film one run from below and check where the new edges appear.
drills.success_indicator: The fall line arrives with the arc already shaping.

drills.name: Inside-foot tipping, outside ski light
drills.purpose: Trains the inside foot as the lead tipping foot by removing the outside ski's compensation.
steps: Ski arcs tipping only the inside foot, with the outside ski deliberately light.
Keep tipping that foot to the finish rather than stopping at the fall line.
Return to normal turns and keep the inside foot working.
drills.success_indicator: The arc tightens through the second half with no added steering.

dose.notes: Both versions watched before the next run.

drills.name: Banking versus angulation, filmed
drills.purpose: Makes the one fault the skier cannot feel visible, by comparing two runs.
drills.setup: A phone filming from below, and a marked 8-turn section.
steps: Ski the section deliberately banking: whole body tipped, shoulders low inside.
Ski it again with the hip in and the chest over the outside ski.
Compare the clips for torso-to-leg angle and for the inside ski's track.
drills.success_indicator: The angulated clip shows a bend at the hip and a light inside-ski track.

dose.notes: Ten arcs per run, counted out loud.

drills.name: Silent finishes
drills.purpose: Separates building pressure from dumping it, using the ski's own noise as feedback.
steps: Ski long arcs and listen: a carve hisses evenly, a dumped finish scrapes.
Release each arc by flexing both legs so the skis pass under the body.
Count how many of ten arcs finish without a scrape.
drills.success_indicator: Eight of ten arcs finish with a flex and no scrape.

drills.name: Carve, skid, carve
drills.purpose: Makes the skid a tool by inserting and removing it inside one arc.
steps: Start an arc carving, add steering until the ski skids, then take the steering away.
Hold the same corridor; the skid must not become a traverse.
Alternate one carved arc and one carve-skid-carve arc, ten pairs.
drills.success_indicator: The track reads clean line, widened section, clean line.

dose.notes: Inspect all eight arcs, not the best two.

drills.name: Track inspection walk
drills.purpose: Trains the skier to read their own tracks, the only honest judge.
steps: Ski eight arcs, stop, and climb back up beside your own tracks.
Measure each line: under 2 cm is carved, over 5 cm is a skid.
Note where the widening starts. That is where the fault lives.
drills.success_indicator: Six of eight arcs under 2 cm, widening only at the finish.

faults.diagnosis_test: Track inspection (dr-10-07). Measure eight arcs; over 5 cm is a skid whatever it felt like.

cues: Tip, do not turn.
Let the ski run its own radius.
fix.equipment_check: Edge sharpness underfoot and current bevels; see mod-equipment.

faults.looks_like: Two broad smears with a spray at the finish; the tail runs outside the tip's line.
faults.name: Smear instead of carve
root_causes: Rotary added out of habit whenever the arc feels slow.
Edge angle too low for the speed and radius chosen.
faults.symptom: The turn feels carved and the tracks are 5-10 cm wide from the fall line on.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film 8 turns from below (dr-10-04) and look for a bend at the hip. Banking is invisible from inside.

cues: Hip in, chest over the outside ski.
Long outside leg.

faults.looks_like: A straight shoulder-hip-boot line tipped inside, with the inside ski tracking deeper.
faults.name: Banking
root_causes: Inclination with no lateral bend at hip or knee.
Edge angle pursued before outside-ski balance is genuine.
faults.symptom: The whole body leans into the arc; grip is fine until it is suddenly gone.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film from below (dr-10-02) and mark where the new edges engage. Below the fall line is late.

cues: New edges before the tips point down.
Change early, then wait.

faults.looks_like: A clean top half that goes nowhere, then a widening, braked bottom half.
faults.name: Late edge change
root_causes: Waiting for the fall line to feel safe before committing.
No pole or count reference to fix the timing to.
faults.symptom: The turn starts with tips already downhill and finishes with a skid.

faults.diagnosis_test: Count silent finishes out of ten (dr-10-05). Fewer than five means pressure is being thrown away.

cues: Flex to release.
Build, then let go.

faults.looks_like: A scrape and spray at the finish, then a moment with no ski bend.
faults.name: Pressure dumped at the finish
root_causes: Releasing by pushing the skis away rather than by flexing.
Weight aft at the finish, so the tails do the work.
faults.symptom: The last third of each arc is a push; the next edge change is rushed and flat.

faults.diagnosis_test: Carve, skid, carve (dr-10-06). If the skid becomes a check or a traverse, this is the fault.

cues: Skid to make room, carve to make speed.
Add steering, then remove it.

faults.looks_like: Long clean arcs, interrupted by hockey stops whenever anyone appears.
faults.name: Carving as the only setting
root_causes: Skidding treated as a fault rather than as a tool.
Carving practised only on empty runs.
faults.symptom: The skier can carve or brake and has nothing between; traffic forces the brake.

faults.diagnosis_test: Draw a fingernail across the edge underfoot: it should shave. Then check tip and tail are dull.

cues: Fix the ski before the skier.
Sharp underfoot, dull at the ends.
fix.equipment_check: 0.5-1 degree base, 1-2 degrees side, tip and tail detuned; see mod-equipment.

faults.looks_like: Chatter and a sudden mid-arc loss of grip, often worse on one ski.
faults.name: Tune blamed on technique
root_causes: Base bevel over 1 degree, or side bevel under 1 degree, for recreational carving.
Blunt underfoot, or tip and tail not detuned, so the ski hooks.
faults.symptom: The ski lets go on hardpack at an edge angle that holds on corduroy.

en.goal: Carve linked medium-radius turns on a blue groomer with the edge change above the fall line, angulation rather than banking, and tracks under 2 cm wide on inspection.
en.one_line: Two clean lines in the corduroy instead of two smears, from an edge change made above the fall line.
safety_notes: A carved turn crosses the hill fast and makes you the least predictable skier there. Uphill skiers cannot read your line, so the uphill check is a mechanism, not manners.
Speeds here are high enough that a fall slides. Never carve above a lift line, a merge or stopped skiers.
Banking (ft-10-02) at carving speed washes the inside ski out with no warning.

cues: Tip, do not turn.
Let the ski choose the radius.
skills.description: Edge angle is built by tipping both feet with no rotary input. The ski bends and runs its own arc.
skills.name: Pure tipping without steering
skills.why: Steering added to an arc is the smear. Every st-11 skill assumes edge angle without twisting.

cues: New edges before the tips point down.
Change early, then wait for the fall line.
skills.description: Old edges release and new ones engage while the tips still point across the hill.
skills.name: Early edge change above the fall line
skills.why: An edge change below the fall line leaves no arc to control speed with, forcing a skidded finish.

cues: Little toe down first, and keep tipping.
Both feet roll at one rate.
skills.description: The new inside foot leads the tipping onto its little-toe edge; the outside ski rolls onto its big-toe edge at the same rate.
misconceptions: The inside ski is not passive. A flat inside ski forces the outside ski to skid.
skills.name: Tipping led by the inside foot
skills.why: Inside-foot lead is what makes an early edge change possible. Leading with the outside ski is a stem.

cues: Hip in, chest over the outside ski.
Long outside leg, short inside leg.
skills.description: The body inclines to balance the forces while hip and knee angulate, keeping mass over the outside ski.
misconceptions: More lean is not more edge. Past a modest angle, leaning moves mass inside the outside ski.
skills.name: Inclination and angulation together
skills.why: Inclination alone is banking: it loads the inside ski and lets go without warning, at speed.

cues: Build it, then let it go.
Flex to release, do not push.
skills.description: Pressure rises from the edge change to just past the fall line, then releases by flexing, not by pushing.
skills.name: Pressure built and released, not dumped
skills.why: A dumped finish unloads the ski exactly when the next edge change needs a platform.

cues: Add steering, then take it away.
Skid to make room, carve to make speed.
skills.description: A carved arc is converted into a controlled skid and back within one turn, corridor unchanged.
skills.name: Carve to skid to carve on command
skills.why: A carve commits to a line. Bleeding it into a skid on demand keeps carving safe in traffic.

tactics: First corduroy is the laboratory. Ski the first two runs as inspection runs; by 10 a.m. the evidence is gone.
Pick runs you can climb back up alongside, so inspection costs seconds, not a run.
Carve the flatter pitches and shape the steeper ones. A steep run here is a speed problem, not a test.

avoid: Narrow runs and cat tracks; a carved arc needs the whole width.
Busy runs, where a crossing arc makes you the least predictable skier there.
Soft spring snow, which hides a smear.
terrain.ideal_description: A wide, uniform 18-22 degree groomer on first corduroy, empty enough to cross the full width and to climb back up alongside your own tracks.

en.why_it_matters: The first stage where the ski does more work than the skier, and where a hidden skid stops being cosmetic. The forces roughly double, and a merely adequate platform lets go at the highest edge angle.

adjustments: 刻滑要有体重才压得弯板，30 公斤的人在任何刃角上都压不弯。轻孩子的干净雪痕是立刃练习，不是这一级。
铁轨练习和看雪痕照做，它们适龄且直接迁移；关卡往后放。
do_not: 不要为了让孩子能刻滑，把他放到又长又硬的成人板上。

adjustments: 成人体重在这里到来，刻滑变得可用，因此这一档最容易自封通过 ac-10-01 与 ac-10-02。
看雪痕和录像必须执行。一个用整体内倾在蓝道上高速「刻滑」的少年，是重摔的典型画像。
更短更软更轻的板在更低速度就弯，把刻滑拉进摔得起的范围。
降量不降标准：四条看过雪痕的弧线胜过十六条没看的。

criteria_modifications.change: 8 条弧线可拆成两组 4 条，中间走回上方一次。2 厘米这条标准不变。

adjustments: 体重较轻的人换更短更软的板是升级：压不弯的板刻不了。按体重选板。
大刃角下膝盖往内走，先按靴筒对线与楔片处理，再谈口令。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。若因体重较轻难以撑住 12 条弧线，换板，不换标准。

adjustments: 对这个体重过软的板会在弧线中段折掉并甩出去，症状与 ft-10-01 一样。先查板，再教毛病。
脱离值随体重变化，须由技师设定；刻滑对固定器的负荷高于前面各级。

zh.core_question: 我能留下两条细线，而不是两道抹痕吗？

dose.notes: 每趟结束都看雪痕，所有弧线都看。

drills.name: 铁轨阶梯
drills.purpose: 分档加大刃角，雪痕会把每一度多加的转向都报出来。
drills.setup: 第一批压雪纹，缓坡，上方无人。
steps: 从平板直行开始，两脚同时倒向一侧，让板横穿山坡。
不转向、也不把弯做完；再倒向另一侧。
按刃角递增滑四趟：到小腿、到膝、到髋，再到弧线持得住的极限。
每趟结束停下来看雪痕。看雪痕就是这个练习本身。
drills.success_indicator: 每个刃角下都是两条铅笔宽的细线，尾部不变宽。

dose.notes: 每次上雪录一趟。

drills.name: 数口令提前换刃
drills.purpose: 把换刃钉在一个地点上，而不是钉在一种感觉上。
steps: 滑中回转，两板放平的那一刻喊一声「到」。
这一声必须落在板头还横指山坡的时候。
拍一趟从下方的录像，核对新刃是在哪里出现的。
drills.success_indicator: 落线到来时，弧线已经在造型了。

drills.name: 内脚立刃、外板放轻
drills.purpose: 拿掉外板的代偿，把内脚练成引导立刃的那只脚。
steps: 只倒内脚滑弧线，外板刻意放轻。
这只脚一直倒到收弯，不在落线处停手。
回到正常转弯，内脚继续保持在工作。
drills.success_indicator: 弧线后半段自己收紧，没有额外加转向。

dose.notes: 两个版本都要在下一趟之前看完。

drills.name: 整体内倾对折角：拍下来比
drills.purpose: 用两趟对比，把这个自己感觉不到的毛病变成看得见的。
drills.setup: 手机在下方拍摄，选定一段 8 个弯的路段。
steps: 刻意用整体内倾滑这一段：整个身体倒进去，肩往弯内低下去。
再滑一遍，髋进弯内、胸口压在外板上。
比两段片子的躯干与腿夹角，以及内板的雪痕。
drills.success_indicator: 折角那段片子里髋处有明显折弯，内板雪痕很轻。

dose.notes: 每趟十条弧线，出声数。

drills.name: 安静收弯
drills.purpose: 用雪板自己的声音，把「建压力」和「泄压力」分开。
steps: 滑长弧线并且听：刻滑是均匀的嘶声，泄压力是搓响。
每条弧线靠两腿同时屈曲解开，让板从身下穿过去。
数十条弧线里有几条收弯没有搓响。
drills.success_indicator: 十条里有八条以屈腿收弯、没有搓响。

drills.name: 刻滑—搓雪—刻滑
drills.purpose: 在一条弧线里把搓雪插进去再拿出来，让它成为工具。
steps: 以刻滑起弧，加转向直到板开始搓，再把转向撤掉。
走廊不许变；搓雪不能变成横切。
一条纯刻滑、一条刻—搓—刻交替，做十对。
drills.success_indicator: 雪痕读出来是：细线、一段变宽、细线。

dose.notes: 八条全看，不是只看最好的两条。

drills.name: 走回去看雪痕
drills.purpose: 把「读自己的雪痕」练成习惯——那是唯一诚实的裁判。
steps: 滑八条弧线，停下，沿着自己的雪痕走回上方。
逐条量：细于 2 厘米是刻滑，宽于 5 厘米是搓雪。
记下变宽是从哪里开始的。毛病就住在那里。
drills.success_indicator: 八条里有六条细于 2 厘米，只在收弯处变宽。

faults.diagnosis_test: 走回去看雪痕（dr-10-07）。量八条，宽于 5 厘米的就是搓雪，手感不算。

cues: 倒板，不要转板。
让板走它自己的半径。
fix.equipment_check: 脚下段的刃是否锋利、刃角是否是新的；见 mod-equipment。

faults.looks_like: 两道宽抹痕，收弯带雪雾；板尾走在板头线之外。
faults.name: 抹痕冒充刻滑
root_causes: 弧线一慢下来就习惯性地加旋转。
刃角配不上选定的速度与半径。
faults.symptom: 弯感觉是刻上了，雪痕从落线起就有 5-10 厘米宽。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从下方拍 8 个弯（dr-10-04），看髋处有没有折弯。整体内倾在里面是看不见的。

cues: 髋进弯内，胸口压在外板上。
外腿长。

faults.looks_like: 肩—髋—靴成一条直线整体往里倒，内板雪痕反而更深。
faults.name: 整体内倾
root_causes: 有内倾而髋膝没有横向折弯。
外板平衡还不真实就去追刃角。
faults.symptom: 整个身体倒进弯内；抓地一直很好，然后突然就没了。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从下方拍（dr-10-02），标出新刃咬上的位置。落线以下就是晚。

cues: 板头还没指下去，新刃就得上。
早换，然后等。

faults.looks_like: 上半段很干净但去不了哪里，下半段变宽、带刹车。
faults.name: 换刃太晚
root_causes: 要等到落线才觉得安全，才肯交出身体。
没有杖或口令这样的参照，把时机钉住。
faults.symptom: 弯起来时板头已经朝下，收弯是搓开的。

faults.diagnosis_test: 数十条里有几次安静收弯（dr-10-05）。不到五次，说明压力在被扔掉。

cues: 屈腿解弯。
先建起来，再放开。

faults.looks_like: 收弯一声搓响带雪雾，随后有一瞬间板完全不弯。
faults.name: 收弯把压力泄掉
root_causes: 解弯靠把板推出去，不是靠屈腿。
收弯重心偏后，活让板尾去干了。
faults.symptom: 每条弧线最后三分之一是一次外推；下一次换刃又急又平。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做刻滑—搓雪—刻滑（dr-10-06）。搓雪变成压刃或横切，就是这个毛病。

cues: 搓雪腾地方，刻滑要速度。
加转向，再撤掉。

faults.looks_like: 一串干净的长弧线，每次有人出现就插进一个横向急停。
faults.name: 只有刻滑一个挡
root_causes: 把搓雪当毛病，不当工具。
刻滑只在空道上练过。
faults.symptom: 只会刻滑或刹车，中间什么都没有；一有人就只能刹。

faults.diagnosis_test: 指甲横刮脚下段的刃：应该刮下屑。再查板头板尾是不是钝的。

cues: 先修板，再修人。
脚下要锋，两端要钝。
fix.equipment_check: 底 0.5-1 度、侧 1-2 度，板头板尾去刃；见 mod-equipment。

faults.looks_like: 抖刃，弧线中段突然丢抓地，常常一只板更明显。
faults.name: 磨刃的问题算在技术头上
root_causes: 对大众刻滑而言底刃角超过 1 度，或侧刃角不到 1 度。
脚下段钝了，或者板头板尾没去刃，板会自己挂住。
faults.symptom: 同一个刃角在压雪纹上持得住，在硬雪上板就放开。

zh.goal: 在蓝道压雪面上连续刻中回转：换刃在落线以上，用折角而不是整体内倾，雪痕实测细于 2 厘米。
zh.one_line: 压雪纹上留下两条细线，而不是两道抹痕；换刃在落线以上完成。
safety_notes: 刻滑弧线横穿山坡且速度高，让你成为道上最难预判的人。上方的人读不出你的线，所以向上观察是机制，不是客气。
这里的速度足以让一次摔倒滑很远。绝不在缆车线、汇流口或停着的人上方刻滑。
整体内倾（ft-10-02）在刻滑速度上会让内板毫无预警地甩出去。

cues: 倒板，不要转板。
半径让板自己挑。
skills.description: 刃角只由两脚倒板建立，不加旋转。板自己弯，自己走出弧线。
skills.name: 纯立刃，不转向
skills.why: 加在弧线上的转向就是抹痕。st-11 的每项技能都假定只立刃、不扭板。

cues: 板头还没指下去，新刃就得上。
早换，然后等落线来。
skills.description: 板头还横指着山坡时，旧刃就已解开、新刃已经接上。
skills.name: 落线以上提前换刃
skills.why: 落线以下换刃，就没剩下弧线可以控速，只能靠搓着收弯。

cues: 小脚趾先落，而且一直倒下去。
两只脚一个速率。
skills.description: 新内脚先倒向小脚趾侧刃引导，外板以同样速率滚上大脚趾侧刃。
misconceptions: 内板不是闲着的。内板一放平，外板就只能搓。
skills.name: 由内脚引导立刃
skills.why: 内脚引导才使提前换刃成为可能。外板先动就是外八字。

cues: 髋进弯内，胸口压在外板上。
外腿长，内腿短。
skills.description: 身体内倾去平衡受力，同时髋膝折出角度，把质量留在外板上方。
misconceptions: 倒得多不等于刃角大。过了一个不大的角度，再倒只是把质量挪到外板内侧。
skills.name: 内倾与折角同时用
skills.why: 只有内倾就是整体内倾：它把内板压上，然后在速度上毫无预警放开。

cues: 先建起来，再放开。
屈腿解弯，不要推。
skills.description: 压力从换刃一路涨到落线稍后，然后靠屈腿放掉，不是靠往外推。
skills.name: 压力是建起来再放掉，不是泄掉
skills.why: 收弯把压力泄掉，恰好在下一次换刃需要平台的时候把板卸载了。

cues: 加一点转向，再把它撤掉。
搓雪腾地方，刻滑要速度。
skills.description: 在一条弧线之内把刻滑放成可控搓雪，再收回来，走廊不变。
skills.name: 听令刻滑转搓雪再转回刻滑
skills.why: 刻滑把线定死了。能随时把它放成搓雪，才使刻滑在人流里成立。

tactics: 第一批压雪纹就是实验室。头两趟当看雪痕的趟；到上午十点，证据就没了。
选能沿雪痕走回上方的雪道，看一次只花几十秒，不花一趟。
缓坡用来刻，陡坡用来造型。这一级的陡坡是速度问题，不是考题。

avoid: 窄道和猫道：一条刻滑弧线要用掉整个道宽。
人多的雪道：横穿的弧线让你成为最难被预判的人。
春季软雪：它会把抹痕藏起来。
terrain.ideal_description: 宽阔、坡度均匀的 18-22 度压雪道，第一批压雪纹，空到能横穿整个道宽、并能沿自己的雪痕走回去看。

zh.why_it_matters: 第一次由雪板干的活多于人干的活，也是搓雪不再只是难看的一级。这里的力大约翻倍，「勉强够用」的平台在最大刃角上会放开。

adjustments: A 30 kg skier cannot bend a carving ski, so these angles are unavailable.
Train shape on short, soft, sharp skis at blue speeds and defer every gate.
do_not: Do not test ac-11-01 or ac-11-04; a light skier fails them for reasons of mass.

adjustments: Eccentric strength is the gate before technique; without the dryland block, six arcs is the ceiling.
Three focused runs with a lift ride between beat one long exhausting descent.

criteria_modifications.change: The 3 runs may spread across a morning; the per-run standard stands.

adjustments: A 14-16 m ski at lower edge angle trains the same skill at far lower load.
Volume down, quality up. Fall consequence means empty runs, not lower gates.

criteria_modifications.change: 300 vertical metres may drop to 200, still timed twice; the 8 percent tolerance stands.

adjustments: A ski that cannot be bent cannot carve. For a lighter skier, shorter and softer is a performance choice.
An A-frame appearing only at these angles is an alignment question before it is a cue.

criteria_modifications.change: No change. Where mass makes the lift hard, change the ski, not the gate.

adjustments: A ski too soft for the skier's mass folds at high angle, producing ft-11-05.
Release values must be set by a technician; a pre-release at 60 km/h is a crash.
Manage arc count and rest rather than the standard.

en.core_question: Can I hold a high-edge-angle arc at speed without banking, and release it on demand?

dose.notes: Inspect every run.

drills.name: High-angle railroad tracks
drills.purpose: Separates edge angle from steering. The tracks are the only honest witness.
drills.setup: Empty fresh corduroy, one grade below your steepest terrain.
steps: From a straight run, tip both feet together and let the skis go. No steering.
Ride each arc back across the hill, then flex, release, tip the other way.
After 6 arcs, inspect the whole track: two lines, no widening at the tails.
drills.success_indicator: Two lines under 3 cm wide, and the arc tightens by itself.

drills.name: Carve to a stop uphill
drills.purpose: Proves the arc survives the finish, the half most carvers abandon.
drills.setup: Wide run, nothing above you, room to the side.
steps: Roll onto the new edges from a moderate straight run and carve one arc without releasing.
Carry it past across-the-hill and up the hill until the ski stops you.
Inspect the track: one continuous curve, no smear in the uphill hook.
drills.success_indicator: The ski stops you by turning, not skidding, and the hook is clean.

drills.name: Outside hand to outside boot
drills.purpose: Forces counterbalance by making the body reach across the outside ski.
drills.setup: Medium carved arcs at moderate speed on groomed blue.
steps: Through the shaping phase, reach the outside hand toward the top of the outside boot.
Keep the chest outside the arc; do not twist toward the hand.
Alternate two reaching arcs with two normal ones, keeping mass on the outside ski.
drills.success_indicator: The outside ski feels heavier at once and the arc tightens.

drills.name: Inside-ski-off carving
drills.purpose: Removes the inside ski as a place to hide load.
drills.setup: Established medium carved arcs; easier side first.
steps: Begin the arc, then lift the inside ski 2-5 cm through the shaping phase.
Set it down at the release and lift the new inside ski.
The line must not change when the ski comes up.
drills.success_indicator: Line and speed unchanged with the inside ski in the air, both directions.

drills.name: Flex to release, counted
drills.purpose: Builds a cross-under release by removing standing up as an option.
drills.setup: Medium arcs, hands forward, one filmed run planned.
steps: At each release flex both legs and say 'down'; the skis travel under you.
The body must not rise at any transition and the skis must never go quiet.
Alternate two flexed releases with two stand-up releases to feel the timing cost.
drills.success_indicator: Skis stay on the snow and the new edges engage above the fall line.

drills.name: Two-radius constant-speed set
drills.purpose: Makes turn shape the speed control at velocity, at two radii.
drills.setup: A groomed black with one pitch change, 300+ vertical metres, low traffic.
steps: Ski 6 long arcs, 6 medium, then 6 long again, all carved, one speed.
The steeper pitch shows a rounder, longer finish, not a lower speed.
Time the run twice; the times should fall within 8 percent.
drills.success_indicator: Speed feels identical across both radii and both pitches, with no check.

drills.name: Stivot on command
drills.purpose: Turns a late redirect into a chosen tool rather than a failure.
drills.setup: Pick a fixed mark on the run where the arc must redirect.
steps: Carve toward the mark; at the mark pivot both feet 20-40 degrees, brushing the tails.
Re-engage the outside edge immediately and carve the remainder clean.
The brush must end inside the first quarter of the arc, or it is a skid.
drills.success_indicator: A short scrub at the top and a clean carved track after it.

faults.diagnosis_test: Lift the inside ski mid-arc (dr-11-04). If the line changes, you are banking.

cues: Ribs over the outside boot.
Head outside the arc.
fix.equipment_check: Cuff alignment and canting, especially if only one side banks.

faults.looks_like: Head, hips and feet in one line tipped into the hill.
faults.name: Banking
root_causes: Inclination without counterbalance, at angles that demand both.
Chasing angle before outside-ski balance was proven at st-10.
faults.symptom: The body leans inside the arc; the ski holds, then lets go at the steepest part.

faults.diagnosis_test: At the fall line, glance at the boot toes: over a boot length of lead fails.

cues: Belly button toward the outside ski tip.
Pull the inside foot back.

faults.looks_like: Inside hip trailing, inside ski shooting ahead, hands square to the skis.
faults.name: Hips rotating into the arc
root_causes: Counteracting treated as a shoulder position, not a pelvic one.
Inside foot not pulled back as that leg shortens.
faults.symptom: The pelvis turns with the skis and the arc runs out of steering at the finish.

faults.diagnosis_test: Inspect tracks after dr-11-01: clean lines beginning at or below the fall line fails.

cues: Highest angle before the fall line.
Tip early, then hold.
fix.equipment_check: Edge sharpness and bevel: 0.5-0.7 base, 2-3 side. See mod-equipment.

faults.looks_like: A track smeared at the top and clean at the bottom.
faults.name: Edge angle arriving late
root_causes: Release delayed until the skis already point downhill.
Dull or wrongly bevelled edges that need a big angle to bite.
faults.symptom: The top of the arc feels flat and fast; the ski grips only below the fall line.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film from the side and step through a transition: rising hips or a track gap confirms it.

cues: Release by flexing, never standing up.
Let the skis run under you.

faults.looks_like: An up-and-down bob from the side, and a break in the tracks.
faults.name: Standing up to release
root_causes: A cross-over release carried up from st-07 into speeds it does not fit.
Up-unweighting used to break the grip of a high edge angle.
faults.symptom: The body rises at every transition and the next arc starts late.

faults.diagnosis_test: Carve to a stop uphill (dr-11-02). A tail releasing before the stop is a spike.

cues: Squeeze the ski, do not hit it.
Keep tipping to the end.
fix.equipment_check: Ski stiffness and radius against mass; a folded ski looks like a fault.

faults.looks_like: A clean line ending in a fan-shaped smear.
faults.name: Pressure spike and tail washout
root_causes: Load hit in a spike instead of built along the arc.
A ski too soft or short for the skier's mass at this load.
faults.symptom: The arc feels good until the finish, when the tails let go.

faults.diagnosis_test: A partner calls for a stop within two arcs, unannounced: three arcs or a skid fails.

cues: Finish across the hill before you release.
Too fast means turn further.

faults.looks_like: Long flat sections between arcs, the run-out doing the braking.
faults.name: Speed accumulating between arcs
root_causes: The finish abandoned because a completed arc at speed feels like too much load.
Terrain or traffic beyond the skier's shape control.
faults.symptom: Arcs open toward the fall line and speed builds beyond what the skier can cancel.

en.goal: Carve long- and medium-radius arcs at speed on groomed black, at edge angles that bend the ski, with a flexion release available anywhere.
en.one_line: High edge angle held at speed, mass over the outside ski rather than leaning inside it, released on demand.
safety_notes: At 60 km/h a carved arc crosses a 30 m trail in two seconds, from a direction uphill traffic is not watching.
Run choice is the safety decision: an empty groomed black at 60 km/h beats a busy blue at 40.
Falls here slide further and catch edges. Sharp edges and technician-set release values stop being optional. See mod-injury.

cues: Tip early, then hold.
Highest angle before the fall line.
skills.description: Angle rises from the transition, peaks at or just before the fall line, then holds — roughly 45-60 degrees at the ski.
misconceptions: More angle is not more lean. Past 45 degrees it comes from hip and knee.
skills.name: Edge angle built early and sustained
skills.why: Angle arriving after the fall line cannot bend the ski while it matters, so the finish skids.

cues: Ribs over the outside boot.
Belly button toward the outside ski tip.
skills.description: Counterbalance keeps mass over the outside ski while the body inclines. Counteracting faces the pelvis outside the arc, so legs steer under a stable torso.
misconceptions: Counter is a pelvis position, not a shoulder one.
skills.name: Counterbalance and counteracting
skills.why: Without both, inclination becomes banking: load slides to the inside ski and the outside ski lets go.

cues: Shorten both legs; let the skis run under you.
Release by flexing, never by standing up.
skills.description: The arc is released by flexing both legs and letting the skis travel underneath the body, without rising and without losing snow contact.
skills.name: Cross-under release at speed
skills.why: At speed a cross-over release becomes standing up, going light and starting late. Steeps then have no transition at all.

cues: Squeeze the ski, do not hit it.
Longest outside leg at the fall line.
skills.description: Load builds from the initiation, peaks at and just past the fall line, then releases progressively. The ski bends and unbends smoothly.
misconceptions: A carve does not hold itself; park and ride at 50 km/h is a pending washout.
skills.name: Pressure along the arc, not at a point
skills.why: A spike over-bends the ski, the tail washes out, and the arc ends in a skid read as too much speed.

cues: Finish across the hill before you release.
Too fast means turn further uphill.
skills.description: A GS-shaped arc carried 15-25 m across the hill, controlling speed by how far it completes. A finished arc and an abandoned one differ by 15-20 km/h.
skills.name: Long-radius shape as the speed governor
skills.why: Shape is the only speed control a carving ski offers. A skier who cannot close an arc can only straighten and hope.

cues: Brush the top, carve the bottom.
Pivot with the feet, then stand on it.
skills.description: A controlled pivot and brush at the top of the arc that redirects the skis 20-40 degrees, sheds speed, then re-engages the edges.
misconceptions: Not a fancier skid. The pivot ends inside the first quarter of the arc.
skills.name: The stivot: deliberate pivot, then carve
skills.why: Without it a late line leaves two options at speed: hold a line that no longer fits, or abandon the turn.

tactics: Arcs this size use the whole trail. Ski them early on empty runs; stop when it fills up.
Read the pitch from the lift: where ice forms, where traffic merges.
You can have the better line and still owe the yield. Right of way belongs below.
Corduroy holds a high edge angle about two hours. Plan the carving block first.

avoid: Narrow trails. A long-radius arc needs 20-30 m of width; on a narrow trail you are borrowing someone else's.
Crowded or late-afternoon runs, where closing speeds make a carved line indefensible.
Boilerplate for acquisition. Test edge angle on ice; do not learn it there.
terrain.ideal_description: A wide groomed black of 25-32 degrees, freshly groomed and empty, early on a weekday. Long enough for 12-15 full-radius arcs, with a clear run-out and no merging traffic, because arcs this size need the whole trail width.

en.why_it_matters: Here a carve stops being a demonstration on a gentle blue and becomes a way to ski steep groomed terrain fast. It is the last stage trained in clean conditions.

adjustments: 30 kg 的滑雪者压不弯刻滑板，所以这些刃角对他们根本不存在。
在短、软、刃锋利的板上以蓝道速度练弧线形状，关卡一律延后。
do_not: 不要测 ac-11-01 或 ac-11-04；体重轻的滑雪者不合格是因为体重，不是技术。

adjustments: 离心力量是技术之前的关；没有陆地训练那一块，六个弧线就是上限。
三趟专注、中间坐缆车恢复，胜过一趟又长又累的下滑。

criteria_modifications.change: 那几趟可以摊在一上午完成；每趟标准不变。

adjustments: 14-16 m 半径的板配较小刃角，练的是同一能力，负荷低得多。
降量保质。摔倒后果意味着选没有人的雪道，不是降低关卡。

criteria_modifications.change: 300 米落差可以降到 200 米，仍然计时两趟；容差不变。

adjustments: 压不弯的板刻不出弧。体重较轻的人，更短更软是性能选择，不是妥协。
只在这种刃角下出现的 A 形腿，先是对线问题，才是口令问题。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。体重让抬板变难，要换的是板，不是关卡。

adjustments: 对这个体重太软的板会在大刃角下被压塌，直接产生 ft-11-05。
脱离值必须由技师设定；60 km/h 下一次误脱离就是一次事故。
要管的是弧线数量和休息，不是标准。

zh.core_question: 高速下我能守住大刃角而不整体内倾，并随时解开吗？

dose.notes: 每趟都检查雪痕。

drills.name: 大刃角铁轨
drills.purpose: 把刃角从转向里剥离出来。雪痕是唯一的证人。
drills.setup: 没有人的新压雪纹，比你最陡的地形低一档。
steps: 从直行开始两脚同时倒向一侧，让板自己走，不做转向。
把每个弧线带到横切山坡，然后屈腿解刃，倒向另一侧。
6 个弧线之后检查整条雪痕：两条线，板尾不变宽。
drills.success_indicator: 两条不到 3 cm 宽的细线，弧线自己会收紧。

drills.name: 刻滑到上坡停住
drills.purpose: 证明弧线活过收弯期——多数人放掉的正是这一半。
drills.setup: 宽雪道，上方无人，侧边有余量。
steps: 从中速直行滚到新刃上，刻一个弧线，中途不解刃。
一路带过横切方向，继续往山上带，直到板把你停住。
检查雪痕：一条连续曲线，上坡的钩里没有抹痕。
drills.success_indicator: 板是靠转弯停住你的，不是靠打滑；钩子干净。

drills.name: 外手摸外板靴
drills.purpose: 让身体越过外板去摸，把侧向反平衡逼出来。
drills.setup: 蓝道压雪面上中等速度的中回转刻滑弧线。
steps: 造型期用外侧手去摸外板靴子上口。
胸口留在弯外，不要跟着手扭过去。
两个「去摸」的弧线换两个正常的，质量始终留在外板上。
drills.success_indicator: 外板立刻变重，弧线自己收紧。

drills.name: 抬内板刻滑
drills.purpose: 把内板这个藏负荷的地方取消掉。
drills.setup: 成型的中回转刻滑弧线；先做顺的那侧。
steps: 弯建立后，造型期全程把内板抬离雪面 2-5 cm。
解刃时放下，随即抬起新的内板。
板抬起来时，线不许变。
drills.success_indicator: 内板在空中时，线和速度不变，两个方向都成立。

drills.name: 数着屈腿解刃
drills.purpose: 把「站起来」这个选项拿走，建立收腿换刃。
