drills.setup: 中回转弧线，双手前置，计划拍一趟。
steps: 每次解刃都屈两腿，同时喊「下」；板从身下跑过去。
任何一次换刃都不许起身，板也不许安静。
两个屈腿解刃换两个站起来解刃，体会时机的代价。
drills.success_indicator: 板不离雪，新刃在落线以上就咬住。

drills.name: 两种半径的恒速组
drills.purpose: 在高速下用两种半径，把弧线形状变成控速手段。
drills.setup: 一条带坡度变化、落差 300 米以上、人少的压雪黑道。
steps: 滑 6 个大回转、6 个中回转、再 6 个大回转，全刻滑，一个速度。
更陡那段应表现为更圆更长的收弯，不是更低的速度。
同一趟计时两次；两次应落在 8% 以内。
drills.success_indicator: 两种半径、两段坡度速度感一致，全程零压刃止速。

drills.name: 口令先搓后刻
drills.purpose: 把「线走晚了」从失败变成主动选用的工具。
drills.setup: 在雪道上选一个固定标记，弧线必须在那改向。
steps: 刻向标记；到标记处两脚枢转 20-40 度，刷一下板尾。
立刻重新咬住外刃，把剩下的弧线刻干净。
刷的那一下必须在弧线前四分之一内结束，否则就是搓雪。
drills.success_indicator: 顶上一小段刷痕，之后是干净的刻滑雪痕。

faults.diagnosis_test: 弧线中段抬起内板（dr-11-04）。线一变，就是整体内倾。

cues: 肋骨压在外板靴子上方。
头留在弯的外侧。
fix.equipment_check: 靴筒对线与内外倾垫片，尤其只有一侧内倾时。

faults.looks_like: 头、髋、脚成一条线，一起倒向山内。
faults.name: 整体内倾
root_causes: 在要两者并用的刃角上只有内倾，没有侧向反平衡。
在 st-10 把外板平衡做实之前就去追刃角。
faults.symptom: 身体倒进弯内；刃先咬住，到最陡处松开。

faults.diagnosis_test: 在落线处扫一眼两只靴尖：领先超过一个靴长即不合格。

cues: 肚脐对着外板板头。
内脚往后收。

faults.looks_like: 内侧髋落后，内板往前冲，双手与板平齐。
faults.name: 髋跟着弯转进去
root_causes: 把反向当成肩的位置，不是骨盆的。
内侧腿变短时没有把内脚往后收。
faults.symptom: 骨盆跟着板转，收弯时转向已用完。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做完 dr-11-01 检查雪痕：细线从落线或落线以下才开始即不合格。

cues: 最大刃角出现在落线之前。
早立刃，然后守住。
fix.equipment_check: 刃的锋利度与打磨角：底刃 0.5-0.7 度、侧刃 2-3 度。见 mod-equipment。

faults.looks_like: 雪痕上半段抹开、下半段干净。
faults.name: 刃角来晚
root_causes: 解刃拖到板头已指向山下。
刃钝或打磨角度不对，要很大角度才咬得住。
faults.symptom: 弧线上半段又平又快；板只在落线以下才咬住。

faults.diagnosis_test: 侧面拍摄，逐帧过一次换刃：髋升起或雪痕断开即确认。

cues: 用屈腿解刃，绝不站起来。
让板从身下跑过去。

faults.looks_like: 从侧面看是一上一下的点头，雪痕上有断口。
faults.name: 靠站起来解刃
root_causes: 把 st-07 的越板换刃带到了它不适用的速度。
用上提减压去掰开大刃角的咬合。
faults.symptom: 每次换刃身体都升起来，下个弧线都起晚。

faults.diagnosis_test: 刻滑到上坡停住（dr-11-02）。板尾在停住前就松开，就是峰值。

cues: 把板挤弯，不是砸弯。
一直立到最后。
fix.equipment_check: 按体重核对板的硬度与半径；被压塌的板看起来就像技术毛病。

faults.looks_like: 一条干净的线，末端摊成一把扇形抹痕。
faults.name: 压力峰值与板尾外滑
root_causes: 负荷是一记砸下去的，不是沿弧线累积的。
板对这个体重和负荷来说太软或太短。
faults.symptom: 弧线一直不错，直到收弯时板尾松开。

faults.diagnosis_test: 让同伴不预告地喊「两个弧线内停住」：用了三个弧线或搓出去即不合格。

cues: 先把弯横切完，再解刃。
太快就多转一点。

faults.looks_like: 弧线之间夹着长直段，最后由出口平缓段替你刹车。
faults.name: 弧线之间速度累积
root_causes: 收弯被放掉：高速下把一个弯做完的负荷感觉太大。
地形或人流超出这位滑雪者的形状控制能力。
faults.symptom: 弧线朝落线敞开，速度涨到人已经消不掉。

zh.goal: 在压雪黑道上高速刻出大回转与中回转弧线，刃角大到能压弯板，任何位置都能屈腿解刃。
zh.one_line: 高速下守住大刃角，质量压在外板上方、不是倒进弯里，且随时能解开。
safety_notes: 60 km/h 下，一个刻滑弧线两秒就横穿 30 m 宽的雪道，且来自上方人流不会看的方向。
选道就是安全决策：没人的 60 km/h 压雪黑道胜过拥挤的 40 km/h 蓝道。
这一级的摔倒滑得更远、更容易挂刃。锋利的刃和技师设定的脱离值不再可选。见 mod-injury。

cues: 早立刃，然后守住。
最大刃角出现在落线之前。
skills.description: 刃角从换刃期开始长，在落线处或稍前达到峰值，然后守住——板下约 45-60 度。
misconceptions: 刃角大不等于人倒得多。过了 45 度，刃角来自髋和膝。
skills.name: 刃角早立，并守住
skills.why: 刃角在落线之后才到，就没能在最要紧的那段把板压弯，收弯只好搓。

cues: 肋骨压在外板靴子上方。
肚脐对着外板板头。
skills.description: 侧向反平衡在内倾的同时把质量留在外板上方；反向让骨盆朝向弯外，腿才能在稳定躯干下转动。
misconceptions: 反向是骨盆的朝向，不是肩的朝向。
skills.name: 侧向反平衡与反向
skills.why: 两者缺一，内倾就变成整体内倾：负荷滑到内板，外板松开。

cues: 两条腿一起变短，让板从身下跑过去。
用屈腿解刃，绝不用站起来解刃。
skills.description: 两条腿同时屈曲解开弧线，让板从身体下方穿过去；人不起身，板不离雪。
skills.name: 高速下的收腿换刃解刃
skills.why: 高速下的越板换刃会变成「站起来」：一站就轻，一轻就晚；到陡坡上换刃期干脆消失。

cues: 把板挤弯，不是砸弯。
落线处外侧腿最长。
skills.description: 负荷从起弯开始累积，在落线及稍后达到峰值，再渐进释放；板平顺地压弯与回弹。
misconceptions: 刻滑不会自己维持；50 km/h 的站死，是一次待发生的外滑。
skills.name: 压力沿整条弧线走，不集中在一点
skills.why: 一记峰值把板压过头，板尾外滑，弧线以搓雪收尾，人却读成「速度太快」。

cues: 先把弯横切完，再解刃。
太快就往山上多转一点。
skills.description: 一个 GS 尺寸的弧线横切山坡 15-25 m，靠完成到什么程度控速。做完和放掉的弧线差 15-20 km/h。
skills.name: 以大回转弧线形状作为速度阀门
skills.why: 形状是刻滑板唯一的控速手段。收不住弯的人只能把线拉直，然后祈祷。

cues: 顶上刷一下，下半段刻出去。
用脚枢转，然后站上去。
skills.description: 在弧线顶部有控制地枢转刷一下，把板改向 20-40 度，卸掉速度，再重新咬刃。
misconceptions: 它不是花式搓雪。枢转必须在弧线前四分之一内结束。
skills.name: 先搓后刻：刻意枢转，再刻出去
skills.why: 没有它，高速下线走晚了只剩两条路：硬守一条不合用的线，或放掉这个弯。

tactics: 这个尺寸的弧线要用掉整条道。趁早趁空滑；人一多就收。
从缆车上读坡：哪里结冰，哪里汇入人流。
线更好不等于路权更优先。路权永远属于下方。
压雪纹撑得住大刃角约两小时。把刻滑那一块排在最前面。

avoid: 窄道。一个大回转弧线要 20-30 m 宽；在窄道上你用的是别人的地方。
拥挤或下午晚段的雪道：相对速度一上来，刻滑的线就无法辩护。
拿冰面学动作。刃角可在冰上检验，不要在冰上学。
terrain.ideal_description: 宽阔的 25-32 度压雪黑道，刚压过、没有人，工作日清早。长度够 12-15 个满半径弧线，出口开阔、无人流汇入——这个尺寸的弧线要用掉整条道。

zh.why_it_matters: 刻滑到这里不再是缓坡上的展示，而是快速滑陡压雪道的方式，也是最后一个在干净雪况下训练的级别。

adjustments: Children in this band ski steep terrain by instinct and speed while lacking the pivot slip and the escape route.
Teach the sideslip escape and pivot slips on blue as games; black is not the classroom.
do_not: Do not follow a child down a steep pitch. Ski below them, one pitch at a time.

adjustments: Eccentric strength and ankle mobility decide whether the edge set is available at all.
Short pitches with a rest between beat one long descent; degraded steep skiing trains the fault.
Fall consequence, not capability, is the limit. Soft steep is a different sport from firm steep.
Volume down, gates unchanged. Four clean pitches beat eight managed ones.

criteria_modifications.change: The 10 short swings on the steep may be taken as two sets of 5 with one regroup between; the count and tempo requirements are unchanged.

adjustments: Pole length and cuff fit dominate the plant: a pole that forces the hand back produces ft-12-06 directly.
The late-release, loaded-tail fault is the phantom-foot mechanism magnified. Treat ft-12-01 as a safety gate.
Momentum makes a late release more expensive; the pivot slip and escape route matter more, not less.
Hop turns are the wrong tool: landing load scales with mass. Cap at the blue stage of dr-12-06.

en.core_question: On steep terrain, am I skiing — or surviving?

drills.name: Pivot slip corridor, narrowing
drills.purpose: Builds the pivot slip against a width limit, which is what a chute is.
drills.setup: Pick a corridor between two features, starting 4 m wide.
steps: Sideslip down the fall line, then pivot 180 degrees without leaving the corridor.
Resume the slip, pivot back, and continue: 8 pivots per run.
Narrow the corridor to 3 m, then 2 m.
drills.success_indicator: The corridor holds, the chest never turns, the slip never stops.

dose.notes: Both directions every run.

drills.name: Sideslip the pitch, stop on call
drills.purpose: Proves the escape route on the actual terrain, before it is needed.
drills.setup: A 100 vertical metre pitch with a clean run-out.
steps: Descend the whole pitch sideways, facing across the hill, without turning.
On five unannounced calls, stop the slide within one metre.
Repeat facing the other way; the weak side matters most.
drills.success_indicator: The pitch is descended and every stop lands inside a metre.

drills.name: Short swing ladder
drills.purpose: Builds the rhythm where it is not punished, then moves it uphill.
drills.setup: A 3 m corridor down the fall line, counted out loud.
steps: On blue, ski 15 short swings in the corridor, one per second, chest downhill.
Move to a groomed black and repeat without changing tempo.
Only then move to a 32-38 degree pitch, 10 turns at a time.
drills.success_indicator: The tempo is unchanged across all three pitches.

drills.name: Blocking plant from a standstill
drills.purpose: Isolates the pole plant, so the block is learned before the tempo.
drills.setup: Standing across a steep pitch on a firm edge set.
steps: Plant the downhill pole ahead of the boot and lean on it; feel the torso stop.
Release the edges against the plant and let the skis come around underneath.
Set the new edges, step across, repeat the other way.
drills.success_indicator: The plant holds the chest still while the skis change direction under it.

drills.name: Release before you want to
drills.purpose: Attacks the fear delay by making the release early on purpose.
drills.setup: A consistent pitch, moderate turn size, nothing below you.
steps: Count 'one' at the release and 'two' at the finish, out loud.
The release must happen while the skis still point across the hill.
Film one run and check where the new edges engage.
drills.success_indicator: The skis point downhill briefly and the turn takes hold without a check.

drills.name: Hop turn, staged
drills.purpose: Builds the hop turn where the landing is cheap, and stops there.
drills.setup: Four stages, one per session, in order.
steps: Flat ground: plant both poles, hop both skis 90 degrees, land on both feet.
Green: from a traverse, hop 180 degrees to the other traverse, landing on set edges.
Blue of 18-25 degrees: traverse to traverse, 6 per direction, landing quiet.
Stop here. Black terrain is not a hop-turn training ground and no gate requires it.
drills.success_indicator: The landing is quiet and on both edges, with no scramble.

drills.name: Read the line, then ski it
drills.purpose: Separates line choice from turning, and makes the escape part of the plan.
drills.setup: Study the pitch from below or the lift before dropping in.
steps: Name six turn locations and two places you could stop, out loud, before starting.
Ski the line you named. Deviating is a fail, not an adaptation.
At the bottom, say what the pitch was actually like.
drills.success_indicator: The line skied matches the line named, stopping places included.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film from below and mark where the new edges engage; below the fall line is this fault.

cues: Release before you want to.
Down the hill to slow down.

faults.looks_like: A long traverse, a rushed pivot, a loaded tail, and a scrub at every finish.
faults.name: Late release: the fear delay
root_causes: The fear reflex delaying the release, which is normal and trainable.
No proven escape route, so committing feels irreversible.
faults.symptom: The skier waits until the skis point downhill to release, then arrives too fast.

faults.diagnosis_test: Count turns per 100 vertical metres. Under 10 on a 35-degree pitch is a traverse.

cues: Turn where you are, not where it flattens.
One breath per turn.

faults.name: Survival skiing: traverse and check
root_causes: Speed managed by braking rather than by turn shape and pivot.
Terrain chosen ahead of the skills, usually by a group.
faults.symptom: The descent is long traverses joined by edge sets; there are no turns in it.

faults.diagnosis_test: Standing on the pitch, try to touch the snow below the downhill boot.

cues: Reach down the hill with the downhill hand.
Stand on the downhill ski.

faults.looks_like: Shoulders and hips uphill of the feet, uphill hand high, tails washing first.
faults.name: Leaning into the hill
root_causes: A defensive reaction to the drop below.
No counterbalance, so leaning into the slope is the only way to feel safe.
faults.symptom: The body leans uphill, the skis lose their edge, and the slide starts from the top of the turn.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ski a pitch with both poles held across the chest. If they swing, the torso is steering.

cues: Chest to the bottom of the run.
Legs turn, chest stays.

faults.name: Upper body rotating into the turn
root_causes: Separation treated as a movement rather than a permanent posture.
Pole plant missing or late, so the torso has nothing to block against.
faults.symptom: The turn is started by swinging the shoulders, and the skis get stuck across the hill.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ask for 8 pivot slips in a 2 m corridor. A hopper usually cannot.

cues: Slip it, do not jump it.
Feet stay on the snow.

faults.name: Hopping instead of pivoting
root_causes: The pivot slip was never made reliable, so the only release is a jump.
A jump feels safer than a slip, which is backwards here.
faults.symptom: Every turn on the steep is a jump; the skier is exhausted in 20 turns.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ski a pitch trying to see both hands. A hand you must look for is behind you.

cues: Plant ahead of the boot, hand forward.
The pole times the turn.
fix.equipment_check: Pole length: 5 cm shorter helps on steep terrain.

faults.name: Pole plant that carries weight
root_causes: Plant used for support instead of as a block.
Poles too long, which forces the hand back and down.
faults.symptom: The skier leans on the pole, the hand ends behind the hip, and the body follows.

en.goal: Ski 30-38 degree pitches in controlled short-radius turns, with a proven sideslip escape, on terrain where a fall would still stop.
en.one_line: Steep terrain skied by choice: a pivot you can stop, a rhythm you can hold, and a bail-out you have already proved.
safety_notes: A fall on a 35-degree pitch does not stop where it starts. Choose terrain where a slide runs into snow, not rocks.
Never ski a steep pitch out of sight of a partner, and never above a group. One at a time, with a regroup point named first.
Refrozen and boilerplate surfaces turn every fault into an uncontrolled slide. Wait for the sun. See mod-safety and mod-injury.

cues: Feet turn, chest stays.
Slip, pivot, slip — never stop moving.
skills.description: The st-09 pivot slip held on a 30-38 degree pitch, where a lost corridor accelerates rather than drifts.
misconceptions: Not a slow hockey stop. The slip continues through and after the pivot.
skills.name: Pivot slip at steep-pitch consequence
skills.why: The steeps skill: how to change direction where there is no room to turn, and how to stop when it goes wrong.

cues: Plant, then release.
Hand forward and down the hill, not back.
skills.description: Rhythmic short-radius turns down the fall line, each finished with a decisive edge check and released against a pole plant that blocks the torso.
skills.name: Short swing with a blocking pole plant
skills.why: The plant makes a fast tempo possible on a steep pitch: it holds the torso still so the legs turn under it.

cues: Chest to the bottom of the run, legs underneath.
Both hands where you can see them.
skills.description: Chest, hands and pelvis face down the fall line continuously, not only at the finish. Here it is a posture, not a movement.
skills.name: Permanent upper-lower body separation
skills.why: A torso that turns with the skis runs out of rotation halfway down, and here the recovery is a slide.

cues: Release before you want to.
Down the hill to slow down.
skills.description: The edges are released above the fall line and the skis point downhill briefly before the new turn takes hold. The first instant accelerates; the arc does not.
skills.name: Committing to the new turn early
skills.why: The fear reflex delays the release. A late release loads the tail, straightens the ski and accelerates the skier: the fault that feels like speed is too little commitment.

cues: Flatten to go, tip to stop.
Look where you are going, not at your skis.
skills.description: Descending an entire steep pitch on the edges, sliding sideways under control, stopping and restarting the slide at will.
skills.name: Sideslipping a whole pitch
skills.why: The bail-out, and what makes commitment rational. A skier who has proved they can always get down will release early.

cues: Plant, unweight, land on both edges.
Land quiet, not hard.
skills.description: Both skis jumped clear and landed pointing the new way, on the spot. Learned flat, then green, then blue traverse-to-traverse — and only then, if at all, steeper.
skills.name: Hop turn, built in stages
skills.why: Genuinely useful in a couloir or a ski-width gap. For most recreational skiers a pivot slip with an edge check does the same job at far lower knee load.

tactics: Read the pitch from below or the lift, and name two places you could stop.
Ski steeps one pitch at a time, regrouping above a rise and out of the fall line.
Fear is trainable: drop a grade, prove the escape, then add pitch back.
Risk assessment is not fear. If a slide would not stop, turn around; that decision is the skill.

avoid: Exposure while the skills are being built. Consequence and difficulty are separate axes.
Spring refreeze and boilerplate, where a slide that will not stop turns a technique problem into an accident.
Narrow couloirs and blind entrances until pivot slips are automatic.
terrain.ideal_description: A consistent 32-38 degree pitch of 100-200 vertical metres, soft or packed rather than refrozen, with a clean run-out visible from the bottom and no rocks, cliffs or trees below. Learn on terrain where a slide stops on its own.

en.why_it_matters: Steeps are where every earlier fault becomes a consequence. A skier with a late release does not get a bad turn here; they get an accelerating one.

adjustments: 这一档的孩子靠本能和速度就能滑陡坡，却没有枢转侧滑和退路。
把侧滑退路和枢转侧滑当游戏放在蓝道上教；黑道不是教室。
do_not: 不要跟在孩子后面滑陡坡。滑在他们下方，一段一段来。

adjustments: 离心力量和踝的活动度决定这个压刃到底有没有。
短坡加休息，胜过一次长下滑；退化状态下的陡坡滑行是在练毛病。
限制来自摔倒后果，不是能力。软陡坡和硬陡坡是两项运动。
降量，关卡不动。四段干净的坡胜过八段勉强管住的。

criteria_modifications.change: 陡坡上那组短摆可拆成两半、中间集合一次；个数和节奏要求不变。

adjustments: 杖长和靴筒适配主导插杖：把手推到后面去的杖直接产生 ft-12-06。
晚解刃加被压住的板尾就是幻足机制的放大版。把 ft-12-01 当安全关卡。
动量让晚解刃的代价更高；枢转侧滑和退路因此更重要。
跳转是错的工具：落地负荷随体重放大。到 dr-12-06 的蓝道阶段就封顶。

zh.core_question: 在陡坡上，我是在滑雪，还是在求生？

drills.name: 逐步收窄的枢转侧滑走廊
drills.purpose: 在宽度限制下建立枢转侧滑——窄槽就是一个宽度限制。
drills.setup: 在两个地形参照物之间选一条走廊，先取 4 m。
steps: 沿落线侧滑，然后原地枢转 180 度，不许滑出走廊。
接着恢复侧滑、转回来、再继续：每趟 8 次枢转。
把走廊收到 3 m，再收到 2 m。
drills.success_indicator: 走廊守住，胸口一次没转，侧滑一次没断。

dose.notes: 每趟都做两个朝向。

drills.name: 整段坡侧滑，随叫随停
drills.purpose: 在真正要用它的地形上提前验证退路。
drills.setup: 一段落差 100 米、出口干净的坡。
steps: 整段坡横着滑下来，身体朝横坡方向，全程不转弯。
五次不预告的叫停，每次都在一米内把滑动止住。
换另一侧朝向再做一遍；弱的那侧最重要。
drills.success_indicator: 整段坡滑完，每次叫停都在一米内停住。

drills.name: 短摆阶梯
drills.purpose: 先在不被惩罚的地方把节奏建起来，再往陡处搬。
drills.setup: 沿落线一条 3 m 走廊，出声数拍。
steps: 在蓝道上，走廊里滑 15 个短摆，一秒一个，胸口朝山下。
换到压雪黑道上重复，节奏不许变。
之后才上 32-38 度的坡，一次 10 个弯。
drills.success_indicator: 三种坡度上节奏完全一样。

drills.name: 站定练阻挡插杖
drills.purpose: 把插杖单独拿出来，让「阻挡」先于节奏学会。
drills.setup: 在陡坡上横向站定，刃踩实。
steps: 把山下侧雪杖插在靴子前方靠上去，感受躯干被按住。
顶着这根杖解开刃，让板从身下绕过来。
踩住新刃，横向上跨一步，换另一侧重复。
drills.success_indicator: 插杖把胸口按住，板在它下面完成改向。

drills.name: 在你想解刃之前就解刃
drills.purpose: 刻意提前解刃，直接对付恐惧的延迟。
drills.setup: 坡度均匀，中等弯幅，下方无人。
steps: 解刃时出声数「一」，收弯时数「二」。
解刃必须发生在板还指着横坡方向时。
拍一趟，检查新刃是在哪里咬住的。
drills.success_indicator: 板短暂指向山下，弯随即咬住，不需要压刃止速。

drills.name: 分阶段的跳转
drills.purpose: 在落地代价最低的地方建起跳转，然后停在那里。
drills.setup: 四个阶段，一次上雪一个，按顺序来。
steps: 平地：双杖插好，双板跳转 90 度，双脚同时落地。
绿道：从横切跳 180 度到另一侧横切，落地刃已踩住。
18-25 度蓝道：横切到横切，每个方向 6 次，落地要轻。
到这里就停。黑道不是跳转的训练场，也没有关卡要求它。
drills.success_indicator: 落地轻、双刃同时踩住，没有手忙脚乱的补救。

drills.name: 先读线，再滑线
drills.purpose: 把线路选择从转弯里分出来，把退路写进计划。
drills.setup: 出发前从坡底或缆车上把这段坡看清楚。
steps: 出发前出声说出六个转弯位置和两个能停住的地方。
照你说的线滑。偏离就是不合格，不叫临场应变。
到坡底，说一遍这段坡实际是什么样。
drills.success_indicator: 滑的线和说的线一致，包括停靠点。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从下方拍摄，标出新刃咬住的位置；落线以下就是这个毛病。

cues: 在你想解刃之前就解刃。
想慢下来，先指向山下。

faults.looks_like: 一段长横切、一次赶出来的枢转、一个被压住的板尾，每次收弯都要搓。
faults.name: 晚解刃：恐惧造成的延迟
root_causes: 恐惧反射把解刃拖晚，这很正常，也能训练。
没有验证过的退路，所以「交出去」感觉像不可逆。
faults.symptom: 等到板已指向山下才解刃，然后到得太快。

faults.diagnosis_test: 数每 100 米落差的转弯次数。35 度坡上少于 10 个，那是横切。

cues: 就在这里转，不要等它变平。
一个弯一口气。

faults.name: 求生式滑行：横切加压刃
root_causes: 用刹车控速，不是用弧线形状和枢转。
地形选在能力之前，通常是被同伴带上去的。
faults.symptom: 整段下滑是一串长横切用压刃连起来；里面没有弯。

faults.diagnosis_test: 在坡上站定，试着摸山下侧靴子下方的雪面。

cues: 山下侧手往山下伸。
站到山下那只板上。

faults.looks_like: 肩和髋都在脚的山上侧，山上侧手举高，板尾先外滑。
faults.name: 往山里倒
root_causes: 面对下方落差做出的防御反应。
没有侧向反平衡，倒向坡面就是唯一觉得安全的做法。
faults.symptom: 身体倒向山上，板失去刃，滑坠从弯顶就开始。

faults.diagnosis_test: 双手横持雪杖滑一段坡。杖一跟着甩，就是躯干在转向。

cues: 胸口对着坡底。
腿转，胸口不动。

faults.name: 上身跟着弯转
root_causes: 把分离当成一个动作，不是一个常驻姿态。
插杖没有或来晚，躯干没有东西可顶。
faults.symptom: 靠甩肩启动转弯，板卡在横坡方向。

faults.diagnosis_test: 要求在 2 m 走廊里做 8 次枢转侧滑。爱跳的人通常做不出来。

cues: 滑过去，不要跳过去。
脚不要离开雪面。

faults.name: 该枢转时在跳
root_causes: 枢转侧滑从没做可靠，所以唯一的解刃方式是跳。
跳起来感觉比侧滑安全，而在这里这感觉是反的。
faults.symptom: 陡坡上每个弯都是一次跳；20 个弯人就干了。

faults.diagnosis_test: 滑一段坡，全程试着同时看见两只手。要「找」的那只就在你身后。

cues: 插在靴子前方，手保持在前。
杖是给弯计时的。
fix.equipment_check: 杖长：陡坡上短 5 cm 有帮助。

faults.name: 承重的插杖
root_causes: 把插杖当支撑用，不是当阻挡用。
杖太长，逼得手往后往下走。
faults.symptom: 人靠在杖上，手落到髋后面，身体跟着过去。

zh.goal: 在 30-38 度坡上用可控的小回转滑行，带一条验证过的侧滑退路，地形是摔了还会自己停的那种。
zh.one_line: 主动选择去滑的陡坡：一个叫得停的枢转、一个守得住的节奏、一条验证过的退路。
safety_notes: 35 度坡上摔一跤，不会停在摔倒的地方。要选滑下去撞进雪里、不是岩石的地形。
绝不在同伴看不见的地方滑陡坡，也绝不在一群人上方滑。一个一个来，集合点先说好。
再冻雪和冰面会把每个毛病变成失控滑坠。等太阳。见 mod-safety 与 mod-injury。

cues: 脚转，胸口不动。
滑、转、再滑——一刻都不要停。
skills.description: 把 st-09 的枢转侧滑搬到 30-38 度坡上：走廊一丢，人不是漂出去，是加速出去。
misconceptions: 这不是慢动作横向急停。侧滑在枢转当中和之后都要继续。
skills.name: 陡坡后果之下的枢转侧滑
skills.why: 这就是陡坡的核心能力：在没地方转弯的地方改变方向，以及出问题怎么停。

cues: 先插杖，再解刃。
手往前、往山下，不许往后。
skills.description: 沿落线做有节奏的小回转，每个弯以果断的压刃止速收尾，顶着阻挡上身的插杖解刃。
skills.name: 带阻挡插杖的短摆
skills.why: 插杖是陡坡上快节奏的前提：它把躯干按住，腿才能在下面转。

cues: 胸口对着坡底，腿在身体下面。
两只手都在你看得见的地方。
skills.description: 胸口、双手和骨盆持续朝向落线，不只在收弯那刻。在这级它是姿态，不是动作。
skills.name: 常驻的上下身分离
skills.why: 跟着板转的躯干，滑到半坡就没有旋转可用，而这里的补救办法是滑坠。

cues: 在你想解刃之前就解刃。
想慢下来，先指向山下。
skills.description: 在落线以上就解刃，让板短暂指向山下，新的弯随后咬住。加速的只是第一瞬间，弧线不加速。
skills.name: 早一点交出去，进入新的弯
skills.why: 恐惧反射把解刃拖晚。晚解刃压住板尾、把板拉直、把人加速：那个像「太快」的毛病，其实是交出去太少。

cues: 放平就走，立刃就停。
看你要去的地方，不要看板。
skills.description: 整段陡坡都站在刃上，横向可控地滑下来，随时能停、停了能重新起滑。
skills.name: 把整段坡侧滑下来
skills.why: 这是退路，也是「敢交出去」的理由。证明过自己总能下来，才会早解刃。

cues: 插杖、卸载、双刃落地。
落地要轻，不要砸。
skills.description: 两板同时跳离雪面，原地落在新方向上。先平地、再绿道、再蓝道横切到横切——之后才是更陡的坡，且未必要。
skills.name: 分阶段建立的跳转
skills.why: 在窄槽或一个板宽的缝里确实有用。但对多数休闲滑雪者，一次枢转侧滑加一次果断的压刃止速就能办到，膝关节负荷只有一小部分。

tactics: 从坡底或缆车上读一遍这段坡，说出两个能停住的地方。
陡坡一段一段滑，在凸起之上、落线之外集合。
恐惧可以训练：降一档、验证退路，再把坡度加回来。
风险判断不是恐惧。滑下去停不住就转身回去；那个决定就是能力。

avoid: 技术还在建立时不要碰暴露感强的地形。后果和难度是两根轴。
春季再冻雪和冰面：在停不下来的雪面上，技术问题会变成事故。
窄槽和看不见底的入口，等枢转侧滑成了本能再说。
terrain.ideal_description: 一段坡度均匀的 32-38 度坡，落差 100-200 米，软雪或压实雪而非再冻雪，从坡底能看见干净出口，下方没有岩石、断崖或树。要在「滑下去会自己停住」的地形上学。

zh.why_it_matters: 陡坡是所有旧毛病变成后果的地方。解刃晚的人得到的不是一个坏弯，而是一个越来越快的弯。

adjustments: Children in this band often ski bumps by instinct while being years away from carving, which needs mass. Expect st-13 terrain skills alongside st-06 edging skills.
Absorption is usually already there; line discipline and eyes-ahead are the teaching content.
Bump size relative to body height is the gate, not the run's rating: a blue bump is a black bump to a 30 kg skier.

criteria_modifications.change: Substitute a blue bump run of the same length: a black bump field is dimensionally wrong for a small skier.

do_not: Do not read instinctive bump skiing as a passed stage; hands and line are usually missing.

adjustments: Eccentric strength declines faster than concentric, and absorption is purely eccentric. The dryland block decides whether this stage is reachable.
Ankle and hip range of motion cap the absorption stroke. Test mobility off snow first.

criteria_modifications.change: The three descents may carry a longer rest, and the block may repeat later the same day rather than back to back.

adjustments: Volume down, softness up. Four rounded-line runs in soft afternoon bumps beat eight in anything harder.
Shorter, lighter skis enlarge the absorption range and cut the cost of a late landing.
Reaction time and balance recovery decline, so the rounded line is the whole stage here.

criteria_modifications.change: The zipper section may drop to 2 bumps. Changing line on command is the point, not trough speed.

adjustments: The published higher incidence of ACL injury makes ft-13-03 a hard stop here rather than a later refinement.
Hamstring strength and single-leg eccentric control belong in the block before bumps, not after.
A knee tracking inward under absorption load is alignment work for a bootfitter, not more cues.
Absorption load scales with mass, so run three degrades sooner. Shorten the block, not the standard.
A ski too soft for the skier's mass folds in the trough and mimics ft-13-03.

en.core_question: Do my legs absorb the terrain while my upper body stays quiet?

dose.notes: Both directions; the weaker side gets twice the volume.

drills.name: One bump at a time, across the hill
drills.purpose: Isolates absorption from speed by taking the fall line out.
drills.setup: A shallow section of a blue bump run, traversed.
steps: Traverse across the bumps, absorbing each one, head at constant height.
Stop every third bump and check the track for hops.
Traverse the same line faster, head height unchanged.
drills.success_indicator: The skis stay in contact with the snow over every crest.

drills.name: Rounded line, one turn per face
drills.purpose: Builds the friendly line and proves speed control lives on the faces.
drills.setup: Pick three bumps in a line; plan a turn on each uphill face.
steps: From a stop, turn on the first bump's uphill face, finishing across the hill.
Stop, choose the next bump, repeat: every turn planned first.
Link three, then six, then ten bumps without stopping.
drills.success_indicator: Speed after ten bumps is the same as at the start.

drills.name: Trough sideslip and crest pivot
drills.purpose: Trains the crest pivot and rebuilds the escape route this stage needs.
drills.setup: A single trough with a clean run-out below it.
steps: Sideslip a trough, chest downhill, stopping the slide on command.
On a crest, pivot 180 degrees inside the sideslip without moving forward.
Alternate slip and pivot six times down the trough.
drills.success_indicator: The pivot happens on the crest and the chest never turns with the skis.

drills.name: Hands on the crests
drills.purpose: Attaches pole discipline to the terrain, so the bump drives the hands.
drills.setup: Normal stance, hands forward and slightly wider than on a groomer.
steps: Ski the rounded line, touching a pole basket on every crest.
Say 'touch' aloud for a run; a missed word is a missed transition.
Finish with a run where both hands stay in view.
drills.success_indicator: A touch on every crest, no arm swing, no shoulder dip.

dose.notes: Six chunks per run minimum.

drills.name: Three-bump chunks
drills.purpose: Builds the habit of choosing a line in blocks instead of bump by bump.
drills.setup: Any blue bump run with visible spacing and a safe stop.
steps: Name out loud the three bumps you will use, ski them, stop.
Name the next three from where you stopped, ski those.
Extend to six, then nine, still naming out loud.
drills.success_indicator: The bumps you ski are the ones you named.

drills.name: Zipper-line samples
drills.purpose: Doses the fast line short enough to survive, and exposes missing absorption.
drills.setup: Small evenly spaced bumps in soft snow, rounded-line exit planned.
steps: Enter the troughs down the fall line for four bumps, absorbing each.
On the fourth crest, pivot onto the rounded line and let the face brake you.
Four samples per run; extend only when the exit is automatic.
drills.success_indicator: Four bumps with skis on the snow and a controlled exit.

drills.name: Three-run block
drills.purpose: Bumps are an endurance skill; this exposes what fails on run three.
drills.setup: Three descents of one bump run, only the lift ride between.
steps: Ski the same line three times, filming descents one and three.
Compare hands, head height and turn location between the clips.
Stop when absorption becomes hopping; a fourth degraded run teaches nothing.
drills.success_indicator: The third descent is recognisably the same skiing as the first.

faults.diagnosis_test: Traverse ten bumps (dr-13-01) filmed from the side. A head that rises is a leg that did not shorten.

cues: Suck the bump up.
Head stays level.

faults.looks_like: Air off every crest, a bobbing head, a landing in the trough.
faults.name: Getting bounced
root_causes: Legs held at constant length, so the bump goes into the body.
More speed than the current absorption range can swallow.
faults.symptom: The bumps throw the skier upward; the skis land where they land.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film from below and mark the first bump at which a hand leaves your field of view.

cues: Hands out over the tips.
Touch every crest.
fix.equipment_check: Pole length: about 5 cm shorter than a groomer pole.

faults.looks_like: A trailing inside arm, rotating shoulders, hands out of view.
faults.name: Hands and arms left behind
root_causes: Reaching for balance with the arms instead of absorbing with the legs.
Poles too long, driving the hand back to keep the basket clear.
faults.symptom: One or both hands drift back; the pole touch disappears.

faults.diagnosis_test: After three bumps, ask where boot tongue pressure was. No contact in the trough is this fault.

cues: Reach downhill with your feet.
Shins on the tongues at the crest.

faults.looks_like: Straight legs at the crest, hips back in the hole, tips out of the snow.
faults.name: Back seat in the trough
root_causes: Extension into the trough happening late, so the body arrives after the terrain.
Skis too long, making the tips impossible to keep down.
faults.symptom: The skier lands hips behind heels; tips rise, tails hook.

faults.diagnosis_test: Count bumps from entry to your first unplanned stop. Under eight means the line is beyond you.

cues: Turn on the faces to slow down.
Plan the exit before the entry.

faults.looks_like: Three good bumps, a straight line, then a hockey stop or a fall.
faults.name: Zipper-line chasing
root_causes: The zipper line taken as the objective rather than the hardest of three options.
No planned exit onto the rounded line.
faults.symptom: The skier drops into the troughs, accelerates, and finishes out of control.

faults.diagnosis_test: Trough pivot slips (dr-13-03). A chest that turns with the skis has no separation.

cues: Chest down the hill.
Turn the feet, not the shoulders.

faults.looks_like: Shoulders swinging bump to bump, and a turn out of steering on the crest.
faults.name: Upper body turning with the skis
root_causes: Leg rotation not independent enough to pivot under a still torso.
Short-radius work from st-09 done on groomers only.
faults.symptom: The chest rotates every turn; rhythm collapses after five bumps.

faults.diagnosis_test: Name three bumps from the top, ski them, and check you skied those three.

cues: Look three bumps ahead.
Choose the line from the top.

faults.looks_like: Eyes at the tips, a stuttering rhythm, a wandering track.
faults.name: Bump-to-bump skiing with no line
root_causes: Vision working at the tips rather than two to three bumps ahead.
No line chosen before dropping in.
faults.symptom: Each bump is a separate problem; the skier resets every three or four bumps.

en.goal: Descend blue bump runs in continuous rhythm on a chosen line, absorbing with the legs while torso and hands stay quiet.
en.one_line: The legs swallow the terrain and the head travels a level path; line choice, not strength, makes a bump field skiable.
safety_notes: Frozen bumps are the highest-consequence common terrain in a resort: absorption is impossible, and a caught tip in a hard trough is a knee injury.
Bumped runs are blind. Stop at the side above a crest, visible from above - never in a trough.
Fatigue turns absorption into hopping unnoticed. Leave a run in reserve; see mod-injury.

cues: Suck the bump up, stretch into the hole.
Legs are the suspension; the head rides level.
skills.description: Legs shorten to swallow the crest and lengthen into the trough, so the head and torso travel a nearly level path.
misconceptions: Absorption is not a downward push. The bump does the flexing; the skier allows it, then extends behind it.
skills.name: Absorption and extension
skills.why: Without absorption the bump throws the skier airborne, and airborne skis cannot turn, brake or recover.

cues: Turn on top, not in the hole.
Pivot where the ski is light.
skills.description: Pivoting where the crest lifts tips and tails clear of the snow, so a short turn costs almost nothing.
skills.name: Turning on the crest
skills.why: Turning in the trough means turning against the deepest snow and highest resistance, where legs and rhythm go.

cues: Pick the line from the top, then commit.
The face of the bump is your brake.
skills.description: Reading the field as three lines - zipper down the troughs, rounded line on the faces, high line across the tops - and choosing one up top.
misconceptions: The zipper line is not the goal: it is the fastest and least forgiving line, and speed control lives on the rounded line.
skills.name: Line choice as an explicit skill
skills.why: A skier without a line reacts to whatever bump arrives. That is bump survival, not bump skiing.

cues: Hands out over the tips.
Touch on every crest.
skills.description: Both hands forward and slightly wide, out over the tips, with a light pole touch on every crest.
skills.name: Quiet forward hands and a crest pole touch
skills.why: Bumps punish a trailing hand hardest: the hand goes back, the hips follow, the next bump throws you.

cues: Look where you will be in three bumps.
Never look at your tips.
skills.description: Vision working ahead of the skis, so the line is chosen before the current bump arrives.
skills.name: Eyes two to three bumps ahead
skills.why: Looking at the tips makes every bump a surprise, and a surprise is absorbed by the spine, not the legs.

cues: Steer up the face to slow down.
Brake with the hill, not the edges.
skills.description: Using the uphill face of the next bump as the braking surface rather than checking in the trough.
skills.name: Speed control on the uphill face
skills.why: Braking in the trough dumps pressure and kills the rhythm; without face-braking you accelerate until the run wins.

tactics: Ski bumps in the afternoon on a sunny aspect. Softness is the biggest variable in this stage.
Read the field from the chairlift: spacing, trough depth, and where the exits are.
Bumps grow through the season: December's blue bump run is a different run in March.

avoid: Frozen bumps on a cold morning: the terrain teaches nothing and the falls end seasons.
Black bump runs with deep troughs and no exit, before absorption is automatic.
Late-season bumps grown to chest height, which hide their own troughs.
terrain.ideal_description: A blue bump run of 18-25 degrees with small, evenly spaced moguls, skied in the afternoon once sun has softened the faces. Troughs shallow enough to see the next three bumps from the top.

en.why_it_matters: Bumps are the honesty test for every fundamental below them. A residual stem, a rotating torso, a trailing hand and a back-seat finish all survive on groomers and none survive here. Bumps also build the leg-as-suspension movement off-piste snow demands.

adjustments: 这一档的孩子常常靠本能就能滑雪包，却离刻滑还有好几年——刻滑要体重。要预期地形能力到了 st-13、立刃还在 st-06。
吸收通常已有；要教的是线路纪律和眼睛往前。
关卡是雪包相对身高的大小，不是道的难度标：对 30 kg 的人，蓝道的包就是黑道包。

criteria_modifications.change: 换成同长度的蓝道雪包：黑道雪包场对小个子尺寸就不对。

do_not: 不要把本能式的雪包滑行读成通过这级；缺的通常是手和线。

adjustments: 离心力量比向心力量掉得快，而吸收纯粹离心。陆地训练那块决定这级能不能到。
踝和髋的活动范围给吸收行程封顶。先在雪下测灵活。

criteria_modifications.change: 三趟之间可以多休息，这组也可放同一天稍后做，不必背靠背。

adjustments: 降量，提高软度。下午软雪包四趟绕包圆线，胜过更硬的雪里八趟。
更短更轻的板放大吸收范围，也降低落地迟到的代价。
反应时间和平衡恢复下降，所以这一档里绕包圆线就是全部。

criteria_modifications.change: 直线过槽那段可降到 2 个包。重点是按口令换线，不是沟里速度。

adjustments: 文献中更高的 ACL 发生率，使 ft-13-03 是一道硬停，不是以后再修的细节。
腘绳肌力量和单腿离心控制属于雪包之前那块训练，不是之后。
吸收负荷下膝盖内扣，是交给靴技师的对线工作，不是加口令。
吸收负荷随体重放大，第三趟退化更早。缩短这组，不要降低标准。
对这个体重太软的板在沟里会压塌，症状和 ft-13-03 一样。

zh.core_question: 我的腿在吸收地形，而上身保持安静吗？

dose.notes: 两个方向都做；弱的那侧练两倍的量。

drills.name: 一个包一个包，横着过
drills.purpose: 把落线拿掉，从速度里分出吸收。
drills.setup: 蓝道雪包里较缓的一段，横切着走。
steps: 横着穿过雪包，每个都吸收掉，头保持同高。
每三个包停一次，看雪痕里有没有跳的痕迹。
同一条线走快一点，头的高度不变。
drills.success_indicator: 每个包顶雪板都没有离开雪面。

drills.name: 绕包圆线，一个包面一个弯
drills.purpose: 把友好那条线建起来，并证明控速住在包面上。
drills.setup: 选成一条线的三个包；每个上坡面计划一个弯。
steps: 从静止出发，在第一个包的上坡面转弯，收弯横切。
停下，选下个包，重复：每个弯都先计划再滑。
先连三个，再六个，再十个包，中间不停。
drills.success_indicator: 过十个包之后的速度和出发时一样。

drills.name: 沟里侧滑加包顶枢转
drills.purpose: 练包顶枢转，同时重建这一级要的退路。
drills.setup: 一条下方出口干净的沟槽。
steps: 沿沟侧滑，胸口朝山下，随叫随停。
在一个包顶上、在侧滑当中枢转 180 度，人不往前走。
沿这条沟侧滑与枢转交替六次。
drills.success_indicator: 枢转发生在包顶，胸口从不跟着板转。

drills.name: 包顶上的手
drills.purpose: 把杖的纪律挂到地形上，让雪包驱动手。
drills.setup: 正常站姿，双手前置，比压雪道上略宽。
steps: 滑绕包圆线，每个包顶轻点一次杖篮。
有一趟出声喊「点」；漏一个字就是漏一次换刃。
最后滑一趟，全程保持两手都在视野里。
drills.success_indicator: 每个包顶一次点杖，不甩臂，不掉肩。

dose.notes: 每趟至少六段。

drills.name: 三个包一组
drills.purpose: 养成按段选线的习惯，不是一个包一个包选。
drills.setup: 间距看得清、有安全停靠点的蓝道雪包。
steps: 出声说出要用的三个包，滑掉它们，停。
从停住处说出下三个包，再滑那三个。
扩到六个、九个，仍然出声说。
drills.success_indicator: 你滑掉的包，就是你说出口的那些包。

drills.name: 直线过槽取样
drills.purpose: 把这条快线切成活得下来的小剂量，并暴露缺失的吸收。
drills.setup: 软雪里间距均匀的小包，绕包圆线出口先想好。
steps: 沿落线进入沟槽，走四个包，每个都吸收掉。
在第四个包顶枢转上绕包圆线，让包面替你刹。
每趟四次取样；出口成了本能才加长。
drills.success_indicator: 四个包板都不离雪，出口在控制中。

drills.name: 三趟一组
drills.purpose: 雪包是耐力项目；这练习暴露第三趟才崩的东西。
drills.setup: 同一条雪包道连滑三趟，中间只坐缆车。
steps: 同一条线滑三趟，拍第一趟和第三趟。
对比两段录像的双手、头高和转弯位置。
吸收一变成跳就停；退化的第四趟教不了什么。
drills.success_indicator: 第三趟看得出和第一趟是同一套。

faults.diagnosis_test: 横着过十个包（dr-13-01）侧面拍。头升起来就是腿没变短。

cues: 把包吸上来。
头保持水平。

faults.looks_like: 每个包顶都腾空，头一上一下，落地在沟里。
faults.name: 被弹起来
root_causes: 腿始终一个长度，雪包直接顶进身体里。
速度超出当前吸收行程能吞的范围。
faults.symptom: 雪包把人往上弹；板落哪里算哪里。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从下方拍摄，标出手第一次离开视野是第几个包。

cues: 双手放到板头外面去。
每个包顶都点一次。
fix.equipment_check: 杖长：比压雪道用的杖短大约 5 cm。

faults.looks_like: 内侧手臂拖在后面，肩在转，手离开视野。
faults.name: 手和手臂被落在后面
root_causes: 用手臂找平衡，不是用腿吸收。
杖太长，为了杖篮不挂雪，手被推到后面。
faults.symptom: 一只或两手往后漂；点杖消失。

faults.diagnosis_test: 过三个包之后问靴舌压力在哪里。沟里没接触就是这个毛病。

cues: 用脚往山下伸出去。
包顶上小腿贴住靴舌。

faults.looks_like: 包顶上腿是直的，髋落在坑里，板头离雪。
faults.name: 沟里后座
root_causes: 伸进沟里来晚，身体比地形迟到。
板太长，板头根本压不下去。
faults.symptom: 落地时髋在脚跟后；板头翘起，板尾勾住。

faults.diagnosis_test: 数从进入到第一次非计划停住过了几个包。少于八个，这条线超出你了。

cues: 在包面上转弯就慢下来了。
先定出口，再定入口。

faults.looks_like: 三个好包、一段直线，然后一次横向急停或一跤。
faults.name: 追直线过槽
root_causes: 把直线过槽当成目标，不是三个选项里最难的。
没有计划切上绕包圆线的出口。
faults.symptom: 人掉进沟里，加速，最后失控收场。

faults.diagnosis_test: 在沟里做枢转侧滑（dr-13-03）。胸口跟着板转就是没有分离。

cues: 胸口对着山下。
转脚，不转肩。

faults.looks_like: 肩一个包一个包地甩，包顶的弯转向已用完。
faults.name: 上身跟着板转
root_causes: 腿的独立性不足，无法在安静躯干下枢转。
st-09 的小回转只在压雪道上练过。
faults.symptom: 每个弯胸口都在转；五个包之后节奏就崩。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从坡顶说出三个包，滑掉它们，核对是不是那三个。

cues: 看三个包之后。
在坡顶就把线选好。

faults.looks_like: 眼睛在板头上，节奏一顿一顿，雪痕游走。
faults.name: 没有线，一个包一个包地滑
root_causes: 视线停在板头，不是两三个包之外。
进场之前没有选线。
faults.symptom: 每个包都是独立问题；每三四个包就重置一次。

zh.goal: 在蓝道雪包上沿选定的线连续有节奏地下降，用腿吸收，躯干和双手安静。
zh.one_line: 腿把地形吞掉，脑袋走一条平的轨迹；让雪包可滑的是线路，不是力气。
safety_notes: 冻硬的雪包是雪场里后果最重的常见地形：吸收做不到，板头在硬沟里挂住就是膝伤。
雪包道看不见下方。停在雪道侧边、凸起之上、上方看得见处——绝不停在沟里。
疲劳会不知不觉把吸收变成跳。留一趟在口袋里。见 mod-injury。

cues: 把包吸上来，往坑里伸出去。
腿是悬挂，脑袋走平的。
skills.description: 腿变短吞掉包顶、变长伸进沟里，让脑袋和躯干走一条几乎平的线。
misconceptions: 吸收不是往下压。屈曲是雪包做的，人只是允许它发生，再在包后伸展。
skills.name: 吸收与伸展
skills.why: 没有吸收，雪包会把人弹到空中；空中的板不能转弯、不能刹车，也救不回。

cues: 在顶上转，不要在坑里转。
板轻时枢转。
skills.description: 在包顶板头板尾被托离雪面处枢转，小弯几乎不要成本。
skills.name: 在包顶转弯
skills.why: 在沟里转弯就是在最深的雪、最大的阻力里转弯，腿和节奏都栽在那。

cues: 在坡顶选好线，然后照它走。
包面就是你的刹车。
skills.description: 把这片雪包读成三条线——沿沟槽的直线过槽、走包面的绕包圆线、横过包顶的走包顶高线——坡顶选定一条。
misconceptions: 直线过槽不是目标：它最快也最不宽容，而控速住在绕包圆线上。
skills.name: 把线路选择当成一项明确的技术
skills.why: 没有线的人只能对眼前那个包做反应。那是雪包求生，不是滑雪。

cues: 双手放到板头外面去。
每个包顶点一次。
skills.description: 双手前置、略微打开，越过板头，每个包顶轻点一次杖。
skills.name: 安静前置的双手与包顶点杖
skills.why: 雪包对落在身后的手惩罚最重：手一往后髋跟着走，下个包把你弹出去。

cues: 看三个包之后你会在哪里。
永远不要看自己的板头。
skills.description: 视线走在板前面，线在这个包到来之前就选好。
skills.name: 眼睛看到两三个包之外
skills.why: 盯着板头看，每个包都是意外，而意外是用脊椎吸收的，不是腿。

cues: 往包面上转，就慢下来了。
用坡刹车，不用刃刹车。
skills.description: 把下个雪包的上坡面当刹车面，不是在沟里压刃止速。
skills.name: 在包的上坡面上控速
skills.why: 在沟里刹车会一次性泄压、打断节奏；没有包面刹车，你会加速到这条道赢。

tactics: 下午到向阳坡滑雪包。软硬是这级最大的变量。
从缆车上读这片雪包：间距、沟深、出口在哪。
雪包整季在长：12 月那条蓝道雪包，3 月已是另一条道。

avoid: 冷天早上的冻硬雪包：地形什么都教不了，摔一次可以结束一个雪季。
沟深、没有出口的黑道雪包，吸收成了本能再碰。
季末长到胸口高的雪包，会把自己的沟槽藏起来。
terrain.ideal_description: 18-25 度的蓝道雪包，包小、间距均匀，下午等太阳晒软包面再滑。沟槽浅到从坡顶能看见接下来三个包。

zh.why_it_matters: 雪包是对所有基本功的诚实检验：残留外八字、旋转躯干、落在身后的手、后座收弯，压雪道上都能活，这里全活不下来。它也练出野雪要的「腿当悬挂」。

adjustments: Light skiers cannot ski deep snow without adequate ski width and speed. A 30 kg child on narrow rentals sinks regardless of technique.
Depth relative to height is the real variable: 25 cm is knee-deep to an adult and thigh-deep to a child.
Keep pitches steeper than instinct suggests; a light skier cannot generate planing speed on flat soft snow.

criteria_modifications.change: Reduce the depth to 10-15 cm and keep the 25-turn count: rhythm is what is being tested, not depth.

do_not: Do not send a child into deep snow out of sight; a fallen light skier can be genuinely stuck.

adjustments: Lighter, wider skis are the largest lever here: float bought with equipment is float not paid for with effort.
Choose settled snow a day after the storm over bottomless fresh; density is more predictable and falls are softer.

criteria_modifications.change: 4 descents rather than 6, still across 3 runs. Durability is the point; volume is not the gate.

adjustments: Lower average mass makes a ski that will not plane a common and misdiagnosed cause of failure. A lighter skier needs relatively more width, not less.
Width and length, not flex, are the variables to change: a soft ski still sinks.
The back-seat habit of ft-14-04 carries an elevated ACL cost; fix it with speed and equipment.
Greater mass sinks a given ski further, so width and length requirements rise: a 95 mm ski may behave like an 85 mm one.
Planing speed arrives sooner, but the eccentric cost of each flex is higher and fatigue arrives earlier.

en.core_question: Can I find rhythm in snow that pushes back?

drills.name: Straight run, both feet even
drills.purpose: Establishes the platform and the planing sensation before any turning.
drills.setup: A gentle untracked slope of 15-20 degrees with a clear run-out.
steps: Run straight down the fall line, both feet equally loaded, hip-width apart.
Feel the tips rise as speed builds; note where they stop ploughing.
Stop, look back, check the two tracks are the same depth.
drills.success_indicator: Two even tracks, tips riding at or near the surface.

dose.notes: At least 15 uninterrupted turns per run.

drills.name: Porpoise turns
drills.purpose: Builds the flex-extend rhythm by exaggerating it until the skis surface between turns.
drills.setup: A consistent soft pitch with room for 15 fall-line turns.
steps: Ski the fall line in rhythmic symmetric turns, flexing deeply to release each.
Extend until the snow loads both feet, then flex again.
Count aloud: down, long, down, long, for a full run.
drills.success_indicator: The skis surface at every transition and the rhythm needs no thought.

drills.name: Count to three
drills.purpose: Forces patience by putting a measured delay between initiation and the demand for direction.
drills.setup: Moderate soft pitch, medium-radius turns, no obstacles.
steps: Start each turn, then count three beats before asking for more direction.
Let the arc finish itself; add no steering at the end.
Alternate three counted turns with three normal ones.
drills.success_indicator: The turn completes with no late steering, speed still chosen.

drills.name: Soft shoulder laps
drills.purpose: Gives deep-snow practice on an ordinary day, on the untracked edges of groomers.
drills.setup: The ungroomed strip beside a familiar blue, 10-20 cm deep.
steps: Ski the strip for 10 turns, then the groomer for 10.
Name what you changed: platform, speed, where pressure peaked.
Repeat until crossing between surfaces costs no thought.
drills.success_indicator: You cross between surfaces mid-run with no break in rhythm.

drills.name: 80/20 versus 60/40
drills.purpose: Makes the platform difference explicit by skiing the wrong distribution on purpose.
drills.setup: A soft, gentle, obstacle-free pitch where a tip dive is harmless.
steps: Ski four turns loading the outside ski as on a groomer.
Ski four with both feet near equal; compare tip depth and effort.
Inspect both tracks: the groomer distribution leaves one deep trench.
drills.success_indicator: The even-platform turns feel easier and leave two matched tracks.

drills.name: Speed calibration
drills.purpose: Finds today's planing threshold for this snow and ski, as a reusable pace.
drills.setup: One pitch with a long clear run-out, skied four times.
steps: Ski it slowly, then at normal pace, then faster than feels comfortable.
Note which run stopped the tips ploughing and started the skis surfacing.
Ski a fourth at that threshold and hold it the whole pitch.
drills.success_indicator: You can name the pace at which the skis plane and reproduce it.

drills.name: Probe and predict
drills.purpose: Turns snow reading into a testable habit by forcing a prediction before dropping in.
drills.setup: Any ungroomed run with sun on some aspects and shade on others.
steps: Before dropping in, push a pole to the basket and rate resistance one to five.
Predict aloud what speed and edge angle the snow will need.
Ski 10 turns, correct the prediction, repeat on the next aspect.
drills.success_indicator: Predictions match the skiing more often than not, across two aspects.

faults.diagnosis_test: Look back at ten turns. Two matched tracks pass; one trench and one smear is this fault.

cues: Two skis, one platform.
Feel both feet.
fix.equipment_check: Under about 90 mm underfoot in 25 cm guarantees this symptom.

faults.looks_like: One deep trench and one shallow track; a tip surfacing mid-turn.
faults.name: Skiing powder like a groomer
root_causes: Outside-ski dominance carried straight over from groomed skiing.
Edge angle high enough to sink the platform instead of floating it.
faults.symptom: The outside ski sinks, the inside tip dives, and the skier is thrown forward.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ski the same pitch faster once. If the problem disappears, it was never technique.

cues: Point it down the hill.
Slow is the dangerous speed.

faults.looks_like: A bow wave over the tips, then a slow forward fall.
faults.name: Too slow, tip buried
root_causes: Speed reduced in response to fear of the depth.
Turns finished too far across the hill, bleeding all the speed.
faults.symptom: The tips plough, planing stops, and the skier pitches forward.

faults.diagnosis_test: Count to three (dr-14-03). If the counted turns feel better, the normal ones are forced.

cues: Start it, then wait.
Let the snow turn you.

faults.looks_like: An abrupt twist at the top of each turn, jerky rhythm, sideways finish.
faults.name: Forcing the turn
root_causes: Groomed-snow timing applied to snow that answers more slowly.
Impatience with the pressure build under both skis.
faults.symptom: The skier steers hard and early; the skis stall and the arc never develops.

faults.diagnosis_test: In a straight run, feel for the boot tongues. No contact means the stance was abandoned.

cues: Stay centred and add speed.
Ankles closed, hips over the feet.
fix.equipment_check: Ski length and width against mass: a light skier on narrow skis cannot float at any stance.

faults.looks_like: Hips behind the heels, arms trailing, no fore/aft movement available.
faults.name: Sitting back
root_causes: The persistent myth that powder is skied from the back seat.
Speed below the planing threshold, treated as a balance problem.
faults.symptom: The skier leans back to keep the tips up; the quads burn out in a run.

faults.diagnosis_test: Demo a 100 mm ski for one run. If the problem disappears, it was equipment.

cues: Match the ski to the snow.
Demo before you coach.
fix.equipment_check: 95-110 mm underfoot, length at or above head height. See mod-equipment.

faults.looks_like: Sinking tips and a platform that will not build.
faults.name: The wrong ski, coached as a fault
root_causes: A narrow, short or stiff-tipped ski used in snow it was never designed for.
Binding mounted well forward for piste skiing, which loads the tip.
faults.symptom: Coaching produces no soft-snow improvement, while the skier skis groomers well.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ask for a resistance prediction before a run and a rating after. A mismatch is this fault.

cues: Probe before you commit.
Ask how hard it will push.

faults.looks_like: A clean pitch, then a stall where the aspect changed.
faults.name: One tactic for all densities
root_causes: No probe or observation before dropping in.
Depth treated as the only variable that matters.
faults.symptom: Light and heavy snow are treated identically, and density changes catch the skier out.

en.goal: Ski linked, rhythmic turns in in-bounds ungroomed snow of varying density, on a two-footed platform, fast enough to plane.
en.one_line: Both skis work as one platform, the snow supplies the resistance, and the turn is built by waiting rather than forcing.
safety_notes: IN-BOUNDS ONLY. This stage covers patrolled, avalanche-mitigated terrain. Sidecountry and backcountry are a different activity with a different risk model.
Avalanche education, a transceiver, shovel, probe and a trained partner are the entry requirements for out-of-bounds snow, and all of it is out of scope.
In-bounds deep snow still hides stumps, rocks and tree wells. Keep a partner in visual contact.

cues: Two skis, one platform.
Feel both feet the whole arc.
skills.description: Both skis carrying near-equal load - roughly 60/40 rather than 80/20 - working as one wide platform.
misconceptions: Two-footed does not mean feet locked together: hip-width with equal load is the modern platform.
skills.name: The two-footed platform
skills.why: An 80/20 platform sinks the outside ski and leaves the light inside tip to dive, the mechanism behind most powder crashes.

cues: Start it, then wait.
Let the snow do the turning.
skills.description: Starting the turn and then waiting: the snow builds pressure under both skis and the arc completes itself.
skills.name: Patience through the initiation
skills.why: Forcing a soft-snow turn moves the skis faster than the snow can answer, which stalls the platform.

cues: Down to release, long to load.
Breathe the turns, do not fight them.
skills.description: A continuous down-up cycle: flex to release and let the skis rise, extend to load them into the new arc.
skills.name: The flex-extend rhythm
skills.why: This rhythm makes powder skiing feel like breathing. Without it every turn is an isolated effort.

cues: Point it down the hill and let it run.
Slow is the dangerous speed here.
skills.description: Carrying enough speed that the shovels ride up and the tips stay near the surface.
misconceptions: Slowing down is not the safe response to depth: below planing speed the tips dive.
skills.name: Enough speed to plane
skills.why: Too slow is what buries a tip. Most powder problems that look like technique faults are speed problems.

cues: Probe with the pole before you commit.
Ask how hard it will push back.
skills.description: Judging how hard the snow will push back before dropping in: temperature, aspect, time of day, pole probe.
skills.name: Reading snow density
skills.why: Light and heavy snow need different speeds and edge angles. A skier who reads only depth is caught by the first change.

cues: Match the ski to the snow.
Float is equipment before it is technique.
skills.description: Choosing a wider, longer ski for soft snow because float changes what technique can achieve.
skills.name: Ski width and length as a technique variable
skills.why: A 75 mm ski at nose height cannot plane in 30 cm, so the skier learns to fight instead of float.

tactics: First tracks are worth planning for: first lift, know which run opens first, and take the fall line.
Follow the storm around the mountain. Shaded aspects hold light snow longest; sun-facing slopes turn heavy by midday.
In flat light, ski treeline edges where contrast exists rather than open bowls.

avoid: Trees on a powder day: tree wells and the partner rules belong to st-15.
Anything with a flat exit, where a bogged tip means a long walk.
Steep, narrow lines where a lost ski leaves you stranded above a hazard.
terrain.ideal_description: A patrolled, avalanche-mitigated ungroomed run of 20-28 degrees, wide, with a clear run-out and no trees or buried obstacles. Consistent pitch matters more than depth on a first day.

en.why_it_matters: Soft snow is where groomer technique stops transferring. Outside-ski dominance, high edge angles and quick edge sets all work on corduroy and all bury a tip here. It also opens crud, crust and spring snow.

adjustments: 板不够宽、速度不够，体重轻的人就滑不了深雪。30 kg 的孩子踩窄租板，技术再好也往下沉。
真正的变量是雪深相对身高：25 cm 对成年人没到膝，对孩子到大腿。
坡度要比直觉更陡；体重轻的人在平的软雪上生不出浮起速度。

criteria_modifications.change: 把雪深降到 10-15 cm，25 个弯的数量不变：这里测的是节奏，不是雪深。

do_not: 不要让孩子进到看不见的深雪里；体重轻的人摔倒后可能真的动不了。

adjustments: 更轻更宽的板是这里最大的杠杆：装备买的浮力，不用体力去付。
宁可选降雪后第二天沉降过的雪，不要见不到底的新雪；密度更可预期，摔起来更软。

criteria_modifications.change: 4 趟而不是 6 趟，仍然要跨 3 条雪道。要的是耐久，量不是关卡。

adjustments: 平均体重较低，使「板浮不起来」成为常见又常被误诊的失败原因。体重轻的人要相对更宽的板，不是更窄。
该改的是宽度和长度，不是硬度：软板照样往下沉。
ft-14-04 的后座习惯带着更高的 ACL 代价；用速度和装备去修它。
体重更大，同一双板沉得更深，宽度和长度的要求跟着上去：95 mm 的板可能像 85 mm 在用。
浮起速度来得更早，但每次屈腿的离心代价更高，疲劳也更早。

zh.core_question: 在会往回顶的雪里，我能不能找到节奏？

drills.name: 直行，双脚均匀
drills.purpose: 转弯之前，先建立平台和浮起来的感觉。
drills.setup: 15-20 度、没被滑过的缓坡，出口干净。
steps: 沿落线直行，两脚负荷相等，与髋同宽。
速度上来时感觉板头抬起，记住它在哪停止犁雪。
停下回头看，确认两条雪痕深度一样。
drills.success_indicator: 两条深度相同的雪痕，板头贴近雪面。

dose.notes: 每趟至少 15 个不间断的弯。

drills.name: 海豚弯
drills.purpose: 把屈伸节奏放大到板在弯之间浮出雪面。
drills.setup: 坡度均匀的软雪坡，够做 15 个落线弯。
steps: 沿落线做左右对称的节奏弯，每个弯深屈腿解开。
伸到雪把两只脚压实，再屈下去。
整趟出声数：下、长、下、长。
drills.success_indicator: 每次换刃板都浮出雪面，节奏不用想。

drills.name: 数三拍
drills.purpose: 在起弯和要方向之间放一个量好的延迟。
drills.setup: 中等坡度的软雪，中等半径，没有障碍物。
steps: 每个弯起出来之后，数三拍再要更多方向。
让弧线自己走完，收尾不许再加转向。
三个数拍的弯和三个正常的弯交替。
drills.success_indicator: 弯自己走完，收尾没有补转向，速度仍是选出来的。

drills.name: 雪道边软肩练习
drills.purpose: 普通日子里，用压雪道旁没被滑过的那条带练深雪。
drills.setup: 熟悉的蓝道旁那条非压雪带，10-20 cm 深。
steps: 在软带里滑 10 个弯，再到压雪面上滑 10 个。
说出你改了什么：平台、速度、压力峰值在哪。
重复到两种雪面之间来回不用想。
drills.success_indicator: 滑行中途跨过雪面分界，节奏不断。

drills.name: 80/20 对 60/40
drills.purpose: 故意用错的压力分配滑一遍，把差别摆到明面上。
drills.setup: 软、缓、没有障碍的坡，埋一次板头也不会有事。
steps: 先滑四个弯，像在压雪面上那样压外板。
再滑四个双脚接近对等的弯，比较板头深度和费力。
回头看雪痕：压雪那套分配会留下一条深沟。
drills.success_indicator: 均匀平台那几个弯更省力，留下两条一致的雪痕。

drills.name: 速度标定
drills.purpose: 找出今天这片雪、这双板的浮起门槛，变成可复用的节奏。
drills.setup: 一段出口长而干净的坡，滑四遍。
steps: 先慢滑一遍，再正常速度一遍，再比舒服快一点一遍。
记下哪一遍板头停止犁雪、开始浮上来。
第四遍就用那个速度，整段坡都保持住。
drills.success_indicator: 你能说出板浮起来的速度，并能再滑出来。

drills.name: 探一下再预测
drills.purpose: 投入之前先逼出一个预测，把读雪变成可检验的习惯。
drills.setup: 任何非压雪雪道，有的坡向晒太阳、有的在阴影里。
steps: 下去之前把雪杖插到杖篮，给阻力打一到五分。
出声预测这片雪要什么速度和刃角。
滑 10 个弯，修正预测，换下一个坡向再来。
drills.success_indicator: 跨两个坡向，预测对上的多于对不上的。

faults.diagnosis_test: 回头看十个弯：两条一致的雪痕算过，一条沟加一条抹痕就是它。

cues: 两只板，一个平台。
两只脚都要有感觉。
fix.equipment_check: 25 cm 雪里用腰宽不到约 90 mm 的板，必出这个症状。

faults.looks_like: 一条深沟加一条浅痕；弧线中途有一只板头冒出。
faults.name: 把粉雪当压雪滑
root_causes: 压雪滑行的外板主导原样搬了过来。
刃角大到把平台压沉，而不是让它浮。
faults.symptom: 外板往下沉，内板板头扎进去，人被甩向前。

faults.diagnosis_test: 同一段坡快滑一遍。问题消失，就从来不是技术问题。

cues: 板头指向山下。
慢才是危险的速度。

faults.looks_like: 板头前推出一道雪浪，然后慢慢向前摔。
faults.name: 太慢，板头被埋
root_causes: 因为怕雪深，把速度收掉了。
弯横切得太远，把速度全放掉了。
faults.symptom: 板头犁雪，浮力消失，人往前扑。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做数三拍（dr-14-03）。数拍的弯更舒服，正常的弯就是拗出来的。

cues: 起了弯，就等。
让雪替你转。

faults.looks_like: 每个弯开头一记突兀的扭转，节奏发涩，收尾横着走。
faults.name: 硬拗弯
root_causes: 把压雪的时机套到回答更慢的雪上。
对两板下面压力慢慢堆起来没耐心。
faults.symptom: 转向又早又猛；板停住，弧线根本没长出来。

faults.diagnosis_test: 直行时感受靴舌。没有接触，站姿就已经放弃了。

cues: 站回中立位，再加速度。
收踝，髋在脚上方。
fix.equipment_check: 板长板宽要对上体重：体重轻的人踩窄板，什么站姿都浮不起来。

faults.looks_like: 髋在脚跟后面，手臂拖在身后，前后一点余量都没有。
faults.name: 坐后座
root_causes: 「粉雪靠后座滑」这个流传很久的说法。
速度低于浮起门槛，却被当成平衡问题处理。
faults.symptom: 为了让板头抬起来而往后靠；一趟就把大腿烧干。

faults.diagnosis_test: 借一双 100 mm 的板滑一趟。问题消失，就是装备。

cues: 板要配得上雪。
先试板，再教人。
fix.equipment_check: 腰宽 95-110 mm，板长在头顶高度或以上。见 mod-equipment。

faults.looks_like: 板头一直往下沉，平台建不起来。
faults.name: 板不对，却被当成技术毛病来教
root_causes: 拿又窄又短或板头偏硬的板，滑它不是为之设计的雪。
固定器为雪道滑行前移安装，把压力压在板头上。
faults.symptom: 软雪怎么教都不见好，而这个人压雪滑得很好。

faults.diagnosis_test: 出发前要一个阻力预测，滑完再要一个评分。对不上就是它。

cues: 投入之前先探。
先问它会顶多硬。

faults.looks_like: 一段滑得很干净，坡向一换就卡住。
faults.name: 一套战术打所有密度
root_causes: 下去之前既不探也不看。
把雪深当成唯一重要的变量。
faults.symptom: 轻雪重雪一个样地滑，密度一变人就被抓住。

zh.goal: 在场内非压雪、密度不一的软雪里，用双脚平台滑出连贯节奏弯，速度足以浮起板头。
zh.one_line: 两只板当一个平台，阻力由雪提供；弯是等出来的，不是拗出来的。
safety_notes: 只在场内。这一级讲的是有巡逻、做过雪崩控制的地形。侧野雪和野雪（backcountry）是另一项活动，风险模型完全不同。
雪崩教育、信标、雪铲、探杆和受过训练的同伴，是进场界之外的门槛，全部不在本课程范围内。
场内深雪照样藏着树桩、石头和树坑。同伴要保持目视联系。

cues: 两只板，一个平台。
整个弧线都感觉到两只脚。
skills.description: 两只板负荷接近相等——大约 60/40 而不是 80/20——当成一个宽平台用。
misconceptions: 双脚平台不是双腿夹紧：与髋同宽、负荷对等才是现代平台。
skills.name: 双脚平台
skills.why: 80/20 会把外板压沉，轻的内板板头随即扎下去；粉雪里大多数摔倒就是这么来的。

cues: 起了弯，就等。
让雪替你转。
skills.description: 把弯起出来，然后等：雪在两板下面堆起压力，弧线自己走完。
skills.name: 起弯之后要等
skills.why: 在软雪里硬拗，板走得比雪回答得快，平台就塌了。

cues: 屈下去解刃，伸长了受力。
把弯呼吸出来，不要和它打架。
skills.description: 连续的下-上循环：屈腿解开旧弯让板浮上来，伸腿把它们压进新弧线。
skills.name: 屈伸节奏
skills.why: 有这个节奏，粉雪滑起来像呼吸；没有它，每个弯都是一次单独用力。

cues: 板头指向山下，让它走。
这里，慢才是危险的速度。
skills.description: 带足够的速度，让板头抬起来、贴近雪面。
misconceptions: 雪一深就减速不是安全反应：低于浮起速度，板头就往下扎。
skills.name: 足以浮起来的速度
skills.why: 埋板头的原因是太慢。粉雪里看着像技术毛病的，多数是速度问题。

cues: 投入之前先用杖探一下。
先问它会顶多硬。
skills.description: 下去之前先判断雪会顶多硬：气温、坡向、时间，再用杖探一下。
skills.name: 读雪的密度
skills.why: 轻雪重雪要的速度和刃角不同。只读雪深的人，第一次密度变化就被抓住。

cues: 板要配得上雪。
浮力先是装备，才是技术。
skills.description: 软雪要更宽更长的板：浮力决定技术能做到什么。
skills.name: 板宽与板长是技术变量
skills.why: 鼻尖高度的 75 mm 板在 30 cm 雪里浮不起来，人只能学会硬扛。

tactics: 第一道雪痕值得提前计划：赶头缆、知道哪条道先开，走落线。
跟着这场雪绕山走。阴坡轻雪留得最久，朝阳的坡到中午就变重。
平光天滑树线边缘有反差的地方，不要进开阔大碗。

avoid: 下雪天的树林：树坑和同伴规则属于 st-15。
出口是平地的线路：板头一被埋就得走很远。
又陡又窄的线：掉一只板就被困在危险地形上方。
terrain.ideal_description: 有巡逻、做过雪崩控制的非压雪雪道，20-28 度，宽、出口开阔、没有树和埋着的障碍物。第一天坡度均匀比雪深要紧。

zh.why_it_matters: 软雪是压雪技术不再迁移的地方：外板主导、大刃角、快速压刃在压雪纹上都对，在这里全都埋板头。过了它，乱雪、壳雪、春雪一起打开。

adjustments: Children ski trees well by instinct and are most at risk in them: low mass, small airway, and a habit of vanishing from view.
Assess the glade and crud gates; skip breakable crust, which a light skier cannot make behave.

criteria_modifications.change: Not assessed: a 30 kg skier cannot support breakable crust. Substitute a naming call and a decision to leave.

do_not: Do not let a child lead in trees, or ski deep snow out of arm's reach.
Do not use trees as an end-of-day reward.

adjustments: Recovery rather than technique limits this stage: crud is eccentric work, and two consecutive days degrade the third.
Grip and shoulder strength matter here: digging a partner out is the fitness test nobody schedules.

criteria_modifications.change: The 300 vertical metres may be split into two 150 m pitches with one regroup, if rhythm holds inside each.

adjustments: Fall consequence sets the terrain, not capability. Choose soft crud over refrozen, and decline crust as standing policy.
Lighter, wider skis reduce the resistance the legs must absorb - a technique intervention here, not a comfort choice.

criteria_modifications.change: The documented declination route is a full pass; the 10-turn version is optional.

adjustments: Lower mass changes what the surface does: a crust that supports one skier breaks under another. Width and length are the lever.
A ski too long or stiff for heavy crud mimics poor absorption exactly. Check the ski first.

criteria_modifications.change: Standard unchanged. Where mass makes the crust unskiable rather than the skier unskilled, the declination route is the pass.

en.core_question: Can I ski what the mountain gives me, with a partner protocol I never skip?

dose.notes: Both directions.

drills.name: Level-head crud traverse
drills.purpose: Isolates absorption by removing the turn.
drills.setup: Tracked-out pitch, 20-25 degrees, clear run-out.
steps: Traverse the chopped snow at steady speed, hands quiet.
Let the feet rise and fall while the helmet tracks a straight line.
Repeat once standing tall, to feel what a used-up range costs.
drills.success_indicator: Feet move, head does not, speed holds.

dose.notes: 6 probes a season, on different aspects.

drills.name: Crust probe
drills.purpose: Makes ski-or-leave a three-turn test, not a guess at speed.
drills.setup: Edge of an ungroomed run, one traverse from the groomer.
steps: Three round, equally weighted turns: did it support, break evenly, or grab one ski?
Name the surface out loud, with aspect and time of day.
Decide - rounder and slower, or leave - and say it aloud.
drills.success_indicator: Decided in three turns, above the pitch, on evidence.

drills.name: Equal-weight garlands in crust
drills.purpose: Trains a symmetric edge change where asymmetry is punished.
drills.setup: Short crusted pitch, soft flat run-out.
steps: From a traverse, release both edges together, turn to the fall line, return.
Keep the load equal; if one ski breaks through, reduce the pitch.
Add a light retraction so both skis leave the crust at once.
drills.success_indicator: Both skis break or both stay up.

dose.notes: One run aloud, two silent.

drills.name: Gap call
drills.purpose: Forces vision to lead: the next-but-one gap becomes a spoken commitment.
drills.setup: Trunks 8-10 m apart, partner in visual contact, straps off.
steps: Name the exit and the regroup point before dropping in.
Ski 10-12 turns calling 'left' or 'right' for the gap two ahead.
Then repeat with the calls silent, eyes doing the same job.
drills.success_indicator: Turns arrive early and the trees feel wide.

dose.notes: 20+ turns per run, no traverse breaks.

drills.name: Six-metre corridor off-piste
drills.purpose: Builds a small off-piste radius before the trees demand it.
drills.setup: Open ungroomed pitch, 20-28 degrees, corridor about 6 m wide.
steps: Ski 20 turns inside the corridor, releasing by flexing rather than standing up.
Chest faces down the corridor, pole plants light.
Repeat at 4 m, return to 6 m, name which broke first.
drills.success_indicator: Rhythm survives the narrow corridor at constant speed.

drills.name: Condition lap
drills.purpose: Trains a running read of the snow instead of one guess at the top.
drills.setup: One long descent crossing at least two aspects.
steps: Every 10 turns, name the surface aloud and the tactic you are changing.
Change nothing about the fundamentals; only the named tactic moves.
At the bottom, list the conditions crossed in order.
drills.success_indicator: Names are specific, and the tactic changes before the surface bites.

dose.notes: Twice a season, plus the first deep day of any trip.

drills.name: Drop-in briefing and immersion rehearsal
drills.purpose: Makes the protocol a spoken sequence and puts one extraction in your own hands.
drills.setup: A partner, a whistle each, and a soft deep bank beside a run.
steps: Brief aloud before every drop-in: order, exit, regroup, and what if someone is missing.
Fall head first in the bank, hands to the face for an air space, then stop moving.
The partner digs from the airway down. Time it, then swap.
drills.success_indicator: Briefing unprompted; either partner clears an airway inside 2 minutes.

faults.diagnosis_test: Probe three turns (dr-15-02) and read the tracks: one deep and one shallow means unequal load.

cues: Same weight both feet.
Rounder, slower, or leave.

faults.looks_like: A high-edge turn stalling mid-arc, then a twisting stumble.
faults.name: Fighting crust with edge angle
root_causes: Groomed-snow reflex: more grip, which is the wrong answer here.
Unequal weighting carried over from the carving stages.
faults.symptom: In breakable crust the skier edges harder; one ski dives, the other stays up.

faults.diagnosis_test: Call the gap two ahead aloud (dr-15-04); a call that arrives late is a vision fault.

cues: Look at the gap.
Two gaps ahead.

faults.looks_like: Late cramped turns near trunks, shoulders rotating toward the obstacle.
faults.name: Trunk fixation
root_causes: Eyes on the hazard rather than two gaps ahead.
Radius too large for the spacing, so each gap surprises.
faults.symptom: The skier stares at the tree they are trying to miss, and steers toward it.

faults.diagnosis_test: Hold a 4 m corridor for 20 turns on open ungroomed snow (dr-15-05) and count the checks.

cues: Flex to release.
Turn the feet, not the body.

faults.name: One turn size off-piste
root_causes: Short radius trained only on groomed snow, where the release is easier.
Standing up to release, which costs time a small turn lacks.
faults.symptom: Every off-piste turn is the same medium radius; tight terrain gets traversed.

faults.diagnosis_test: Film a crud traverse from the side (dr-15-01): a helmet line matching the snow means no absorption.

cues: Ride it with the legs.
More speed, less edge.

faults.name: Rigid legs in crud
root_causes: Stance already extended, with no travel left.
Speed too low to stay on top, so every pile is hit.
faults.symptom: The skier is bounced by the surface, finishes in the back seat, and blames the snow.

faults.diagnosis_test: A partner asks unannounced before a drop-in: exit, regroup, order. An answer invented on the spot is a fail.

cues: Brief before every drop-in.
One at a time in blind terrain.

faults.looks_like: A group entering trees together and leaving separately.
faults.name: Partner protocol drift
root_causes: Excitement on a deep day, when the protocol is kept least.
Reading in-bounds as patrolled therefore supervised.
faults.symptom: The partner is 'somewhere on this run'; nobody agreed exit, regroup or order.

faults.diagnosis_test: Ask what today's avalanche problem, aspect and elevation band are. No answer means it was not a decision.

cues: A rope is not a grade.
In-bounds only, this whole stage.

faults.looks_like: Sidecountry entries with no transceiver, shovel or probe.
faults.name: Technique confidence mistaken for hazard judgement
root_causes: Skill in variable snow feeling like competence in avalanche terrain.
Following tracks, which record that somebody went, not that it was safe.
faults.symptom: A rope or gate gets read as a difficulty rating and crossed because the skiing feels easy.

en.goal: Ski tracked crud, crust and wind-affected snow in rhythm, hold a short radius through glades, and never skip the partner protocol.
en.one_line: The snow stops cooperating and the terrain stops repeating: tactics change every pitch, the fundamentals do not.
safety_notes: Tree wells and deep snow kill in-bounds. Head first: make an air space with your hands immediately, stop struggling, make noise, and do not count on getting out.
A partner is someone in visual contact who would notice within seconds, not someone on the same run. Never trees or deep snow alone.
Sidecountry and backcountry are out of scope. A rope is not a difficulty rating, and tracks record that somebody went, not that it was safe.

cues: Long legs into the soft, short legs into the hard.
Let the snow move your feet, not your head.
skills.description: Legs as suspension with travel in reserve: shortening where the snow resists, lengthening into soft pockets, so the body tracks a level line.
skills.name: Absorbing variable resistance turn to turn
skills.why: Without reserve travel, one hard patch puts you behind the feet for the rest of the run.

cues: Same weight on both feet, all the way round.
Rounder, slower, or leave.
skills.description: Both skis carry near-equal load and change edge on one beat, so neither breaks through alone. Breakable crust is the hardest common condition in skiing.
skills.name: Both feet as one platform in breakable crust
skills.why: An independently edged ski submarines while the other rides on top, twisting the leg attached to it.

cues: Feet turn; chest stays with the gap.
Flex to release, don't stand up.
skills.description: Turns inside a 4-6 m corridor, made by leg rotation and a flexed release rather than by edge angle.
skills.name: Short radius on demand in ungroomed snow
skills.why: Glades give no room to negotiate turn size; a 10 m minimum radius makes you a passenger.

cues: Look at the gap you want, not the tree you don't.
Two gaps ahead, always.
skills.description: The eyes travel two or three gaps ahead and rest on the spaces, never the trunks.
skills.name: Reading a line through trees: looking at the gaps
skills.why: Vision leads the skis. A skier who looks at what they fear steers into it.

cues: Say what it is before you drop in.
Change the plan, not the fundamentals.
skills.description: Say the surface out loud - crud, breakable crust, sun crust, wind slab, refreeze - and name the one tactic it changes.
skills.name: Naming the snow before you ski it
skills.why: Fundamentals never change with the snow; tactics always do. A skier who cannot name the surface rebuilds technique instead.

cues: Name the exit and the regroup before you drop.
If you cannot see your partner, stop and shout.
skills.description: One at a time in blind terrain, visual contact rather than 'somewhere on this run', exit and regroup agreed before dropping in.
misconceptions: That in-bounds means safe. Patrol mitigates avalanche hazard; it does not stand under a tree.
skills.name: Partner protocol and deep-snow self-rescue
skills.why: The only skill here whose absence kills rather than limits: tree wells are survivable with a partner in sight, and usually not without one.

tactics: Ski the untracked seams: run edges, under lift lines, behind a rollover.
Follow the freeze-thaw clock - east aspects early, south mid-morning, west last.
In blind terrain go one at a time, and stop where you can be seen from above.

avoid: Anything past a rope or gate: that is sidecountry, and out of scope.
Refrozen spring surfaces before they soften.
Tight trees within 48 hours of a storm.
terrain.ideal_description: Patrolled ungroomed terrain of 20-30 degrees with a clear run-out, plus glades with 8-10 m trunk spacing, long enough for 30 turns.

en.why_it_matters: Crud is what powder becomes by eleven o'clock, and the most common off-piste surface there is. It is also where in-bounds skiing starts killing people, through tree wells.

adjustments: 孩子靠本能就把树林滑得很好，而树林里恰恰最危险：体重轻、气道细，一转眼就不见。
林间和乱雪两条关卡照测；易碎壳雪跳过：体重轻的人没法让它听话。

criteria_modifications.change: 不测：30 kg 撑不住易碎壳雪。改成一次雪况报名加一个走人决定。

do_not: 不要让孩子在树林里领滑，也不要在伸手抓不到的地方滑深雪。
不要把树林当成一天结束时的奖励。

adjustments: 限制这一级的是恢复，不是技术：乱雪是离心工作，连两天会让第三天退化。
握力和肩部力量在这里有用：把同伴挖出来，是没人排进计划的体能测试。

criteria_modifications.change: 300 米落差可以拆成两段 150 米、中间一次集合，只要每段里节奏不断。

adjustments: 定地形的是摔倒后果，不是能力。软乱雪优于再冻雪，壳雪当成常设的放弃政策。
更轻更宽的板降低腿要吸收的阻力——这里是技术干预，不是舒适选择。

criteria_modifications.change: 有记录的放弃算完整通过；10 个弯那条路径是可选的。

adjustments: 体重较低会改变雪面的行为：托得住一个人的壳，可能在另一个人脚下就破。宽度和长度才是杠杆。
对重乱雪太长或太硬的板，看起来和吸收不好一模一样。先查板。

criteria_modifications.change: 标准不变。如果是体重让这片壳雪不可滑，而不是人不会滑，放弃这条路径就是通过。

zh.core_question: 山给什么雪我就能滑什么雪，同伴规程一次不跳过？

dose.notes: 两个方向都做。

drills.name: 头不动的乱雪横切
drills.purpose: 把转弯去掉，单独练吸收。
drills.setup: 滑乱的坡，20-25 度，出口干净。
steps: 稳定速度横切碎雪，双手安静。
让脚上下起落，头盔走一条直线。
再站直了做一遍，体会行程用光的代价。
drills.success_indicator: 脚在动，头不动，速度不掉。

dose.notes: 一季 6 次试探，分布在不同坡向。

drills.name: 壳雪试探
drills.purpose: 把「滑还是走」变成三个弯的测试。
drills.setup: 非压雪雪道边缘，从压雪面横切进去。
steps: 三个圆润、双脚等重的弯：托住了、均匀破了，还是抓住一只板。
出声说出雪面名字，连坡向和时间。
做决定——更圆更慢，还是走人——并说出来。
drills.success_indicator: 在坡上方、三个弯之内按证据做出决定。

drills.name: 壳雪里的等重花环
drills.purpose: 在不对称会被惩罚的地方练对称换刃。
drills.setup: 一小段结壳的坡，出口是软平地。
steps: 从横切开始，两侧旧刃一起解开，转到落线再回来。
负荷保持相等；有一只板破壳就降坡度。
加一点收腿，让两只板同时离开壳面。
drills.success_indicator: 要么两只板一起破，要么两只板一起在上面。

dose.notes: 一趟出声，两趟不出声。

drills.name: 报空隙
drills.purpose: 逼视线走在前面：把第二个空隙变成说出口的承诺。
drills.setup: 树距 8-10 米，同伴视线内可见，杖带解开。
steps: 下去之前先说出口和集合点。
滑 10-12 个弯，为第二个空隙喊「左」或「右」。
再滑一遍不出声，让眼睛做同一件事。
drills.success_indicator: 弯来得早，树林感觉是宽的。

dose.notes: 每趟 20 个弯以上，不许横切歇气。

drills.name: 野雪六米走廊
drills.purpose: 树林开始要求之前，先练出野雪里的小半径。
drills.setup: 开阔非压雪坡，20-28 度，走廊宽约 6 米。
steps: 在走廊里滑 20 个弯，屈腿解刃，不靠站起来。
胸口对着走廊往下，插杖轻。
再收到 4 米做一遍，回到 6 米，说出哪段先崩。
drills.success_indicator: 走廊收窄之后节奏还在，速度不变。

drills.name: 雪况巡趟
drills.purpose: 练成一路读雪，而不是在坡顶猜一次。
drills.setup: 一趟长下降，至少穿两个坡向。
steps: 每 10 个弯出声说一次雪面名字，以及你在改的那个战术。
基本要素一条不动，只动被说出来的那个战术。
到底之后按顺序列出穿过的雪况。
drills.success_indicator: 名字叫得具体，战术在雪面咬人之前就改。

dose.notes: 一季两次，加上每次行程的第一个深雪日。

drills.name: 下坡前简报与雪埋演练
drills.purpose: 把规程变成说出口的流程，把一次挖掘放进自己手里。
drills.setup: 一个同伴、各带一个哨子，雪道旁一处软深雪堆。
steps: 每次下去之前出声简报：顺序、出口、集合点，和有人不见了怎么办。
在雪堆里头朝下摔进去，立刻用手臂在面前护出呼吸空间，然后停止挣扎。
同伴从呼吸道往下挖。计时，再交换。
drills.success_indicator: 不用提醒就做简报；两边都能在 2 分钟内挖通呼吸道。

faults.diagnosis_test: 做三个弯的试探（dr-15-02）再读雪痕：一深一浅就是负荷不等。

cues: 两只脚一样重。
更圆、更慢，或者走人。

faults.looks_like: 大刃角的弯中段卡住，接着一次带扭转的踉跄。
faults.name: 用刃角去和壳雪硬碰
root_causes: 压雪反射：要更多抓地，这里答案正好相反。
刻滑阶段带过来的两板不等重。
faults.symptom: 在易碎壳雪里越压越狠；一只板钻下去，另一只在上面。

faults.diagnosis_test: 出声报前面第二个空隙（dr-15-04）；报得比板晚就是视线毛病。

cues: 看空隙。
往前看两个空隙。

faults.looks_like: 靠近树干时弯又晚又挤，肩膀朝障碍物转。
faults.name: 盯着树干
root_causes: 眼睛落在危险物上，而不是前面两个空隙。
半径大过树距，于是每个空隙都是意外。
faults.symptom: 眼睛盯着想避开的那棵树，然后就转向了它。

faults.diagnosis_test: 在开阔野雪上守住 4 米走廊滑 20 个弯（dr-15-05），数压刃止速次数。

cues: 屈下去解刃。
转脚，不转身体。

faults.name: 野雪里只有一种转弯尺寸
root_causes: 小半径只在压雪上练过，那里解刃更容易。
靠站起来解刃，而小弯没有这个时间。
faults.symptom: 野雪里每个弯都是同一中等半径；地形一紧就横切。

faults.diagnosis_test: 从侧面拍一段乱雪横切（dr-15-01）：头盔的线跟着雪面走，就是没吸收。

cues: 用腿骑过去。
速度多一点，刃少一点。

faults.name: 乱雪里腿是僵的
root_causes: 站姿已经伸开，行程没余量。
速度太低，浮不到上面，每堆雪都撞。
faults.symptom: 被雪面弹来弹去，收在后座上，然后怪雪。

faults.diagnosis_test: 同伴在下去之前突然抽问：出口、集合点、顺序。当场编的就不合格。

cues: 每次下去之前都简报。
看不见的地形一个一个来。

faults.looks_like: 一群人一起进树林，分开出来。
faults.name: 同伴规程走形
root_causes: 深雪日的兴奋，恰恰是规程守得最差的时候。
把「场内有巡逻」读成「有人在看着我」。
faults.symptom: 同伴「在这条道上某个地方」；出口、集合点和顺序没人说定。

faults.diagnosis_test: 问今天的雪崩问题类型、坡向和海拔带。答不上来就不是一个决定。

cues: 绳子不是难度等级。
整个这一级，只在场内。

faults.looks_like: 没有信标、雪铲、探杆就进了侧野雪。
faults.name: 把技术自信当成危险判断
root_causes: 在变化雪况里的本事，感觉像是在雪崩地形里的本事。
跟着雪痕走——雪痕记录的是有人去过，不是安全。
faults.symptom: 把绳子或闸门读成难度标记，因为滑起来轻松就跨过去了。

zh.goal: 在乱雪、壳雪和风吹雪里有节奏地滑，在林间雪道守住小半径，永远不跳过同伴规程。
zh.one_line: 雪不再配合，地形也不再重复：战术每段坡都换，基本要素一条不换。
safety_notes: 树坑和深雪在场内就能致命。头朝下埋进去：立刻用手臂在面前护出呼吸空间、停止挣扎、发出声响，并且不要指望靠自己脱身。
同伴指的是视线内可见、几秒钟就会发现你不见了的人，不是「在同一条道上」的人。树林和深雪，绝不一个人去。
侧野雪和野雪（backcountry）不在范围内。绳子不是难度等级，雪痕记录的是有人去过，不是那里安全。

cues: 软处腿伸长，硬处腿缩短。
让雪去动你的脚，不要动你的头。
skills.description: 腿当悬挂，行程留余量：雪顶回来缩短，遇软坑伸长，身体走平线。
skills.name: 逐个弯吸收变化的阻力
skills.why: 行程没余量，一块硬雪就能让你剩下整趟都落在脚后面。

cues: 两只脚一样重，一路到底。
更圆、更慢，或者走人。
skills.description: 两只板负荷接近相等、同一拍换刃，谁都不会单独破壳。
skills.name: 易碎壳雪里双脚当一个平台
skills.why: 单独立刃的那只板钻到壳下面，另一只还在壳上，接着那条腿就被扭。

cues: 脚在转，胸口对着那个空隙。
屈下去解刃，不要站起来。
skills.description: 在 4-6 米走廊里转弯，靠腿部转动和屈腿解刃，不靠刃。
skills.name: 野雪里随叫随到的小半径
skills.why: 林子里没有商量尺寸的余地；最小半径 10 米，你就只是乘客。

cues: 看你要走的那个空隙，不看你不想撞的那棵树。
永远往前看两个空隙。
skills.description: 眼睛走在前面两三个空隙，落点在空隙，不在树干。
skills.name: 在树林里读线：看空隙
skills.why: 视线带着板走。看着自己怕的东西，人就会转向它。

cues: 下去之前先说它是什么。
改计划，不改基本要素。
skills.description: 把雪面出声说出来——乱雪、易碎壳雪、日晒壳雪、风板雪、再冻雪——再说出它改的那个战术。
skills.name: 滑之前先给雪起名字
skills.why: 基本要素从不随雪变，战术永远随雪变；叫不出雪面名字的人只好每次重造技术。

cues: 下去之前先说出口和集合点。
看不见同伴就停下来喊。
skills.description: 看不见的地形一个一个来，视线内可见，而不是「在同一条道上」；出口和集合点在下去之前就说定。
misconceptions: 以为「场内」就等于安全。巡逻管的是雪崩风险，不会站在每棵树下面。
skills.name: 同伴规程与深雪自救
skills.why: 这是唯一一项缺了会死人的技能：树坑在同伴视线内有救，没有同伴通常救不回来。

tactics: 去滑没被滑过的缝：雪道边缘、缆车下方、地形凸起背后。
跟着融冻的钟走：东坡趁早，南坡上午中段，西坡最后。
看不见的地形一个一个来，停在上方看得见的位置。

avoid: 绳索或闸门之外：那是侧野雪，不在范围内。
还没变软的春季再冻雪面。
降雪后 48 小时内的密树林。
terrain.ideal_description: 有巡逻的非压雪地形，20-30 度、出口开阔，加树距 8-10 米、够滑 30 个弯的林间雪道。

zh.why_it_matters: 乱雪是粉雪到十一点的样子，也是野雪里最常见的雪面。它也是场内滑雪开始出人命的地方——树坑。

adjustments: Self-coaching is developmentally inappropriate here: children in this band cannot reliably self-assess, and the loop belongs to the coach or programme.
What transfers is video as evidence and one cue per run. The lane choice belongs to the parents and the programme.
do_not: Do not ask a child to diagnose their own fundamentals.
Do not specialise a child into one lane before adolescence.

adjustments: This is the band the stage is most useful to: masters racing and instructor-track clinics both fit adult schedules and adult motivation.
The maintenance share rises as volume falls. Spread acquisition across more days rather than drilling to fatigue.
Maintenance becomes the majority of the plan - an optimization, not a concession: a held gate beats a half-built new one.
Choose the lane by consequence as well as interest. Technique clinics and masters racing keep the feedback without the exposure.

criteria_modifications.change: The maintenance share may be 80% or higher; the plan-versus-actual tolerance of 20% is unchanged.

adjustments: Self-video from below flatters alignment problems. Where an A-frame persists across two filmed sessions, the next step is a bootfitter, not another drill.
Diagnose equipment before technique: for a lighter skier, a shorter or softer ski changes the footage more than any cue.

criteria_modifications.change: Include one from-side clip in both films; the fore/aft and alignment changes that matter here are invisible from below.

en.core_question: Can I keep improving without an instructor beside me?

dose.notes: Four filmed sessions per season.

drills.name: Two-angle video protocol
drills.purpose: Produces footage that can be diagnosed, not a highlight clip.
drills.setup: Phone on a pole at the side of the run, marked start and finish.
steps: Film 20 turns from below, then the same 20 from the side.
Watch once at 0.25x for the whole picture, then once per fundamental.
Write one sentence naming one fundamental. No lists.
drills.success_indicator: One fundamental named in one sentence, with the frame that proves it.

dose.notes: 10 logged runs.

drills.name: One-cue run
drills.purpose: Stops cue-stacking: one instruction is the only permitted content of a run.
drills.setup: Any run where speed is not an issue.
steps: Say the cue out loud at the top, before pushing off.
Ski the whole run with that cue only, however obvious the other faults get.
Log the cue and one line of effect, on the lift.
drills.success_indicator: At the bottom you can state the cue and its effect.

dose.notes: 4-6 weeks apart, same run, comparable conditions.

drills.name: Same-run comparison
drills.purpose: Separates real change from a good day, which nothing else does.
drills.setup: One benchmark run, one filming spot, comparable snow.
steps: Film the benchmark and name the fundamental you will train.
Train it for 4-6 weeks, changing nothing else.
Re-film the same run and watch both side by side.
drills.success_indicator: A change in the named fundamental that a second viewer also sees.

drills.name: Five-fundamental self-audit
drills.purpose: Forces a diagnosis at the level of fundamentals instead of a fault list.
drills.setup: One filmed run from dr-16-01, and a scorer who is not you.
steps: Score fd-1 to fd-5 out of 5 from the footage, and write why.
Have a partner or coach score the same footage blind.
Compare, take the lowest fundamental, and pick its drill.
drills.success_indicator: Your lowest score matches the independent scorer's within one point.

dose.notes: One lap every ski day.

drills.name: Deliberate easy-terrain lap
drills.purpose: Buys back the only terrain where a pattern can actually change.
drills.setup: One grade below your best terrain, first or last run of the day.
steps: Ski it as drills only: no free skiing, no speed.
Name one fundamental before pushing off and hold it all run.
On a trip, make this day one's terrain.
drills.success_indicator: Drill quality on the easy lap matches what you film.

drills.name: Fear script rehearsal
drills.purpose: Turns fear coaching into a sequence you can run on yourself.
drills.setup: A partner at a real edge of their terrain, and time in hand.
steps: They say what they see. Validate it, then ask: is the run-out safe, would a fall be serious?
Give the exit first - sideslip, traverse, a place to stop - then ask for one turn.
Hand over one controllable thing, then have them restate the intervention.
drills.success_indicator: They restate the intervention in their own words and finish the run.

drills.name: Lane sampling block
drills.purpose: Replaces a preference with evidence before a season is spent on it.
drills.setup: One candidate lane, three sessions.
steps: Three sessions in the lane: a masters race night, a park progression zone, or a clinic day.
Write what improved, what it cost in days and money, what risk it added.
Commit for the season, or sample the next lane - never two at once.
drills.success_indicator: A written decision with a stated cost, not a preference.

faults.diagnosis_test: Name the fundamental you worked on last month and produce the footage. Usually neither exists.

cues: Film 20 turns today.
One fundamental, written down.

faults.name: No feedback loop
root_causes: Video feels vain, or discouraging on first viewing.
No benchmark run, so nothing is comparable.
faults.symptom: Seasons of skiing with no film, no log and no named fault; progress asserted from how the day felt.

faults.diagnosis_test: Count runs one grade below your best terrain across the last 10 ski days. Zero is the fault.

cues: One easy lap, every day.
Drills only on that lap.

faults.name: Never skiing easy terrain
root_causes: Easy terrain reads as regression rather than as where patterns change.
A peer group whose terrain choice sets yours.
faults.symptom: Every run is at the limit, so no drill is ever done well and difficulty gets mistaken for practice.

faults.diagnosis_test: Over the last 20 runs, who chose the line, the speed and the turn size? Never you is the fault.

cues: Ski the first run alone.
Name the run you would have chosen.

faults.name: Always skiing with a faster partner
